audios.title: Populism and the rhetoric of resentment

sentences.target: Populism frames politics as a struggle between a virtuous people and a corrupt elite, collapsing the complexity of governance into a simple moral binary.
sentences.native: El populismo enmarca la política como una lucha entre un pueblo virtuoso y una élite corrupta, reduciendo la complejidad de la gobernanza a un simple binario moral.
sentences.en: Populism frames politics as a struggle between a virtuous people and a corrupt elite, collapsing the complexity of governance into a simple moral binary.
sentences.es: El populismo enmarca la política como una lucha entre un pueblo virtuoso y una élite corrupta, reduciendo la complejidad de la gobernanza a un simple binario moral.

sentences.target: Populist leaders tend to claim a direct, unmediated relationship with the popular will, bypassing established intermediary institutions.
sentences.native: Los líderes populistas tienden a reclamar una relación directa y no mediada con la voluntad popular, evitando las instituciones intermediarias establecidas.
sentences.en: Populist leaders tend to claim a direct, unmediated relationship with the popular will, bypassing established intermediary institutions.
sentences.es: Los líderes populistas tienden a reclamar una relación directa y no mediada con la voluntad popular, evitando las instituciones intermediarias establecidas.

sentences.target: The rhetoric of resentment mobilises voters by channelling legitimate grievances toward scapegoated out-groups.
sentences.native: La retórica del resentimiento moviliza a los votantes canalizando agravios legítimos hacia grupos externos convertidos en chivos expiatorios.
sentences.en: The rhetoric of resentment mobilises voters by channelling legitimate grievances toward scapegoated out-groups.
sentences.es: La retórica del resentimiento moviliza a los votantes canalizando agravios legítimos hacia grupos externos convertidos en chivos expiatorios.

sentences.target: Scholars disagree about whether populism is inherently anti-democratic or can serve as a corrective to elite capture of political institutions.
sentences.native: Los académicos no están de acuerdo sobre si el populismo es inherentemente antidemocrático o puede servir como correctivo a la captura elitista de las instituciones políticas.
sentences.en: Scholars disagree about whether populism is inherently anti-democratic or can serve as a corrective to elite capture of political institutions.
sentences.es: Los académicos no están de acuerdo sobre si el populismo es inherentemente antidemocrático o puede servir como correctivo a la captura elitista de las instituciones políticas.

sentences.target: The challenge for liberal democracies is to address the underlying grievances that fuel populism without validating its exclusionary logic.
sentences.native: El desafío para las democracias liberales es abordar los agravios subyacentes que alimentan el populismo sin validar su lógica excluyente.
sentences.en: The challenge for liberal democracies is to address the underlying grievances that fuel populism without validating its exclusionary logic.
sentences.es: El desafío para las democracias liberales es abordar los agravios subyacentes que alimentan el populismo sin validar su lógica excluyente.

questions.q: How does the speaker describe the core narrative structure of populism?
options: A technocratic vision of rational governance
A struggle between a virtuous people and a corrupt elite
A coalition-building strategy among established parties
A call for radical economic redistribution
questions.answer: A struggle between a virtuous people and a corrupt elite

questions.q: What does the speaker say the rhetoric of resentment does?
options: Creates new policy platforms to address inequality
Channels legitimate grievances toward scapegoated out-groups
Encourages civic participation through grassroots organising
Builds bridges between different social classes
questions.answer: Channels legitimate grievances toward scapegoated out-groups

questions.q: What does the speaker say is the challenge for liberal democracies?
options: Banning populist parties through electoral reform
Addressing underlying grievances without validating populism's exclusionary logic
Strengthening international institutions to counter nationalist movements
Increasing economic growth to eliminate the conditions for populism
questions.answer: Addressing underlying grievances without validating populism's exclusionary logic

audios.title: The separation of powers and checks and balances

sentences.target: The doctrine of the separation of powers distributes legislative, executive, and judicial authority among distinct institutions to prevent tyranny.
sentences.native: La doctrina de la separación de poderes distribuye la autoridad legislativa, ejecutiva y judicial entre instituciones distintas para prevenir la tiranía.
sentences.en: The doctrine of the separation of powers distributes legislative, executive, and judicial authority among distinct institutions to prevent tyranny.
sentences.es: La doctrina de la separación de poderes distribuye la autoridad legislativa, ejecutiva y judicial entre instituciones distintas para prevenir la tiranía.

sentences.target: Checks and balances create a system of mutual accountability in which each branch constrains the others.
sentences.native: Los controles y equilibrios crean un sistema de responsabilidad mutua en el que cada rama limita a las demás.
sentences.en: Checks and balances create a system of mutual accountability in which each branch constrains the others.
sentences.es: Los controles y equilibrios crean un sistema de responsabilidad mutua en el que cada rama limita a las demás.

sentences.target: An independent judiciary is widely regarded as the most critical safeguard against executive overreach.
sentences.native: Un poder judicial independiente es ampliamente considerado como la salvaguarda más crítica contra el exceso del ejecutivo.
sentences.en: An independent judiciary is widely regarded as the most critical safeguard against executive overreach.
sentences.es: Un poder judicial independiente es ampliamente considerado como la salvaguarda más crítica contra el exceso del ejecutivo.

sentences.target: The concentration of power in the executive branch, even when popularly mandated, poses a structural threat to constitutional order.
sentences.native: La concentración de poder en el poder ejecutivo, incluso cuando tiene mandato popular, representa una amenaza estructural para el orden constitucional.
sentences.en: The concentration of power in the executive branch, even when popularly mandated, poses a structural threat to constitutional order.
sentences.es: La concentración de poder en el poder ejecutivo, incluso cuando tiene mandato popular, representa una amenaza estructural para el orden constitucional.

sentences.target: Constitutional design alone cannot guarantee liberty if the political culture does not sustain a genuine commitment to the rule of law.
sentences.native: El diseño constitucional por sí solo no puede garantizar la libertad si la cultura política no sostiene un compromiso genuino con el estado de derecho.
sentences.en: Constitutional design alone cannot guarantee liberty if the political culture does not sustain a genuine commitment to the rule of law.
sentences.es: El diseño constitucional por sí solo no puede garantizar la libertad si la cultura política no sostiene un compromiso genuino con el estado de derecho.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the separation of powers according to the speaker?
options: To increase government efficiency through specialisation
To distribute authority to prevent tyranny
To ensure equal representation for all citizens
To speed up the legislative process
questions.answer: To distribute authority to prevent tyranny

questions.q: Which institution does the speaker identify as the most critical safeguard against executive overreach?
options: The free press
The legislature
An independent judiciary
Civil society organisations
questions.answer: An independent judiciary

questions.q: What does the speaker say constitutional design alone cannot guarantee?
options: Economic prosperity for all citizens
Liberty, without a political culture committed to the rule of law
Democratic elections free from interference
International respect for the country's legal system
questions.answer: Liberty, without a political culture committed to the rule of law

sentences.target: Electoral systems shape not only who wins elections but also which parties exist, how voters behave, and how governments are held accountable.
sentences.native: Los sistemas electorales determinan no solo quién gana las elecciones sino también qué partidos existen, cómo se comportan los votantes y cómo se rinden cuentas los gobiernos.
sentences.en: Electoral systems shape not only who wins elections but also which parties exist, how voters behave, and how governments are held accountable.
sentences.es: Los sistemas electorales determinan no solo quién gana las elecciones sino también qué partidos existen, cómo se comportan los votantes y cómo se rinden cuentas los gobiernos.

sentences.target: First-past-the-post systems tend to produce stable single-party governments but can severely distort representation.
sentences.native: Los sistemas de primera mayoría tienden a producir gobiernos estables de un solo partido, pero pueden distorsionar gravemente la representación.
sentences.en: First-past-the-post systems tend to produce stable single-party governments but can severely distort representation.
sentences.es: Los sistemas de primera mayoría tienden a producir gobiernos estables de un solo partido, pero pueden distorsionar gravemente la representación.

sentences.target: Proportional representation produces legislatures that more faithfully mirror the diversity of the electorate but may encourage coalition fragmentation.
sentences.native: La representación proporcional produce legislaturas que reflejan más fielmente la diversidad del electorado, pero puede fomentar la fragmentación de la coalición.
sentences.en: Proportional representation produces legislatures that more faithfully mirror the diversity of the electorate but may encourage coalition fragmentation.
sentences.es: La representación proporcional produce legislaturas que reflejan más fielmente la diversidad del electorado, pero puede fomentar la fragmentación de la coalición.

sentences.target: Gerrymandering allows the incumbent party to manipulate constituency boundaries to entrench its own electoral advantage.
sentences.native: La manipulación de distritos electorales permite al partido gobernante manipular los límites de las circunscripciones para afianzar su propia ventaja electoral.
sentences.en: Gerrymandering allows the incumbent party to manipulate constituency boundaries to entrench its own electoral advantage.
sentences.es: La manipulación de distritos electorales permite al partido gobernante manipular los límites de las circunscripciones para afianzar su propia ventaja electoral.

sentences.target: No electoral system is neutral; each embeds assumptions about the nature of political representation and the proper relationship between votes and seats.
sentences.native: Ningún sistema electoral es neutral; cada uno incorpora supuestos sobre la naturaleza de la representación política y la relación adecuada entre votos y escaños.
sentences.en: No electoral system is neutral; each embeds assumptions about the nature of political representation and the proper relationship between votes and seats.
sentences.es: Ningún sistema electoral es neutral; cada uno incorpora supuestos sobre la naturaleza de la representación política y la relación adecuada entre votos y escaños.

questions.q: What is a characteristic weakness of first-past-the-post systems according to the speaker?
options: They produce too many coalition governments
They can severely distort representation despite producing stable governments
They give too much power to small regional parties
They lead to chronic voter apathy
questions.answer: They can severely distort representation despite producing stable governments

questions.q: What risk does the speaker associate with proportional representation?
options: It discourages voter participation
It may encourage coalition fragmentation
It gives excessive power to the executive
It makes it easier to gerrymander constituencies
questions.answer: It may encourage coalition fragmentation

questions.q: What does the speaker say about the neutrality of electoral systems?
options: Modern electoral systems have been designed to be entirely neutral
No electoral system is neutral; each embeds assumptions about representation
Proportional systems are the most neutral because they reflect vote shares
Neutrality can be achieved through independent boundary commissions
questions.answer: No electoral system is neutral; each embeds assumptions about representation

sentences.target: Corruption diverts public resources, distorts policy decisions, and corrodes citizens' trust in the institutions that govern them.
sentences.native: La corrupción desvía recursos públicos, distorsiona las decisiones políticas y corroe la confianza de los ciudadanos en las instituciones que los gobiernan.
sentences.en: Corruption diverts public resources, distorts policy decisions, and corrodes citizens' trust in the institutions that govern them.
sentences.es: La corrupción desvía recursos públicos, distorsiona las decisiones políticas y corroe la confianza de los ciudadanos en las instituciones que los gobiernan.

sentences.target: Grand corruption involving political elites is qualitatively different from petty corruption and requires different anti-corruption strategies.
sentences.native: La gran corrupción que involucra a élites políticas es cualitativamente diferente de la corrupción menor y requiere diferentes estrategias anticorrupción.
sentences.en: Grand corruption involving political elites is qualitatively different from petty corruption and requires different anti-corruption strategies.
sentences.es: La gran corrupción que involucra a élites políticas es cualitativamente diferente de la corrupción menor y requiere diferentes estrategias anticorrupción.

sentences.target: Transparency and accountability mechanisms are only effective where there is genuine political will to enforce them.
sentences.native: Los mecanismos de transparencia y responsabilidad solo son efectivos donde existe una voluntad política genuina de hacerlos cumplir.
sentences.en: Transparency and accountability mechanisms are only effective where there is genuine political will to enforce them.
sentences.es: Los mecanismos de transparencia y responsabilidad solo son efectivos donde existe una voluntad política genuina de hacerlos cumplir.

sentences.target: Whistleblower protection is a critical component of any robust anti-corruption framework.
sentences.native: La protección de los denunciantes es un componente crítico de cualquier marco sólido anticorrupción.
sentences.en: Whistleblower protection is a critical component of any robust anti-corruption framework.
sentences.es: La protección de los denunciantes es un componente crítico de cualquier marco sólido anticorrupción.

sentences.target: Research consistently finds that high levels of corruption are associated with lower economic growth and reduced quality of public services.
sentences.native: La investigación encuentra consistentemente que los altos niveles de corrupción están asociados con menor crecimiento económico y calidad reducida de los servicios públicos.
sentences.en: Research consistently finds that high levels of corruption are associated with lower economic growth and reduced quality of public services.
sentences.es: La investigación encuentra consistentemente que los altos niveles de corrupción están asociados con menor crecimiento económico y calidad reducida de los servicios públicos.

questions.q: How does the speaker distinguish grand corruption from petty corruption?
options: Grand corruption involves larger sums of money taken from the public
Grand corruption involves political elites and is qualitatively different, requiring different strategies
Grand corruption is more difficult to prosecute due to legal immunity
Grand corruption occurs only in authoritarian regimes
questions.answer: Grand corruption involves political elites and is qualitatively different, requiring different strategies

questions.q: Under what condition does the speaker say transparency mechanisms are effective?
options: When international organisations monitor compliance
When there is genuine political will to enforce them
When civil society is sufficiently organised to demand accountability
When economic development reaches a sufficient threshold
questions.answer: When there is genuine political will to enforce them

questions.q: What does research consistently find about high levels of corruption?
options: They are mainly found in developing economies with weak legal systems
They are associated with lower economic growth and reduced public service quality
They can be tolerated when economic growth remains strong
They are declining globally due to digital transparency tools
questions.answer: They are associated with lower economic growth and reduced public service quality

audios.title: Nationalism, identity and the politics of belonging

sentences.target: Nationalism is not a monolithic ideology; civic nationalism and ethnic nationalism rest on fundamentally different conceptions of political community.
sentences.native: El nacionalismo no es una ideología monolítica; el nacionalismo cívico y el étnico descansan en concepciones fundamentalmente diferentes de comunidad política.
sentences.en: Nationalism is not a monolithic ideology; civic nationalism and ethnic nationalism rest on fundamentally different conceptions of political community.
sentences.es: El nacionalismo no es una ideología monolítica; el nacionalismo cívico y el étnico descansan en concepciones fundamentalmente diferentes de comunidad política.

sentences.target: Benedict Anderson described nations as imagined communities, united not by direct personal bonds but by shared narratives and symbols.
sentences.native: Benedict Anderson describió las naciones como comunidades imaginadas, unidas no por vínculos personales directos sino por narrativas y símbolos compartidos.
sentences.en: Benedict Anderson described nations as imagined communities, united not by direct personal bonds but by shared narratives and symbols.
sentences.es: Benedict Anderson describió las naciones como comunidades imaginadas, unidas no por vínculos personales directos sino por narrativas y símbolos compartidos.

sentences.target: Ethnic nationalism defines membership in terms of descent and cultural heritage, often producing exclusionary politics toward minorities.
sentences.native: El nacionalismo étnico define la membresía en términos de descendencia y herencia cultural, produciendo frecuentemente políticas excluyentes hacia las minorías.
sentences.en: Ethnic nationalism defines membership in terms of descent and cultural heritage, often producing exclusionary politics toward minorities.
sentences.es: El nacionalismo étnico define la membresía en términos de descendencia y herencia cultural, produciendo frecuentemente políticas excluyentes hacia las minorías.

sentences.target: Civic nationalism ties identity to shared political values and institutions rather than to ethnicity or religion.
sentences.native: El nacionalismo cívico vincula la identidad a valores e instituciones políticas compartidos en lugar de a la etnicidad o la religión.
sentences.en: Civic nationalism ties identity to shared political values and institutions rather than to ethnicity or religion.
sentences.es: El nacionalismo cívico vincula la identidad a valores e instituciones políticas compartidos en lugar de a la etnicidad o la religión.

sentences.target: The resurgence of nationalist movements across both established and emerging democracies has reignited debates about the relationship between national identity and human rights.
sentences.native: El resurgimiento de los movimientos nacionalistas en democracias establecidas y emergentes ha reavivado los debates sobre la relación entre la identidad nacional y los derechos humanos.
sentences.en: The resurgence of nationalist movements across both established and emerging democracies has reignited debates about the relationship between national identity and human rights.
sentences.es: El resurgimiento de los movimientos nacionalistas en democracias establecidas y emergentes ha reavivado los debates sobre la relación entre la identidad nacional y los derechos humanos.

questions.q: How does Benedict Anderson describe nations according to the speaker?
options: As organic communities defined by shared bloodlines
As imagined communities united by shared narratives and symbols
As political contracts between individuals and their state
As economic unions held together by mutual interest
questions.answer: As imagined communities united by shared narratives and symbols

questions.q: What is the key difference the speaker draws between civic and ethnic nationalism?
options: Civic nationalism is more common in democratic societies
Civic nationalism ties identity to shared political values; ethnic nationalism ties it to descent and culture
Ethnic nationalism is always more violent than civic nationalism
Civic nationalism emerged earlier historically than ethnic nationalism
questions.answer: Civic nationalism ties identity to shared political values; ethnic nationalism ties it to descent and culture

questions.q: What has the resurgence of nationalism reignited, according to the speaker?
options: Debates about immigration quotas and border control
Debates about the relationship between national identity and human rights
Academic controversy over the definition of sovereignty
Conflict between regional powers over spheres of influence
questions.answer: Debates about the relationship between national identity and human rights

audios.title: Political polarisation and the crisis of dialogue

sentences.target: Affective polarisation — the degree to which partisans dislike and distrust those on the other side — has intensified sharply in many democracies.
sentences.native: La polarización afectiva, el grado en que los partidarios no gustan y desconfían de los del otro lado, se ha intensificado marcadamente en muchas democracias.
sentences.en: Affective polarisation — the degree to which partisans dislike and distrust those on the other side — has intensified sharply in many democracies.
sentences.es: La polarización afectiva, el grado en que los partidarios no gustan y desconfían de los del otro lado, se ha intensificado marcadamente en muchas democracias.

sentences.target: Unlike ideological polarisation, affective polarisation is driven less by policy disagreement than by negative out-group sentiment.
sentences.native: A diferencia de la polarización ideológica, la polarización afectiva está impulsada menos por el desacuerdo sobre políticas que por el sentimiento negativo hacia el grupo externo.
sentences.en: Unlike ideological polarisation, affective polarisation is driven less by policy disagreement than by negative out-group sentiment.
sentences.es: A diferencia de la polarización ideológica, la polarización afectiva está impulsada menos por el desacuerdo sobre políticas que por el sentimiento negativo hacia el grupo externo.

sentences.target: Social media platforms amplify outrage and division because content that triggers strong negative emotions generates greater engagement.
sentences.native: Las plataformas de redes sociales amplifican el ultraje y la división porque el contenido que desencadena emociones negativas intensas genera mayor participación.
sentences.en: Social media platforms amplify outrage and division because content that triggers strong negative emotions generates greater engagement.
sentences.es: Las plataformas de redes sociales amplifican el ultraje y la división porque el contenido que desencadena emociones negativas intensas genera mayor participación.

sentences.target: Deliberative democracy advocates argue that structured dialogue across difference can reduce polarisation and rebuild civic trust.
sentences.native: Los defensores de la democracia deliberativa argumentan que el diálogo estructurado a través de las diferencias puede reducir la polarización y reconstruir la confianza cívica.
sentences.en: Deliberative democracy advocates argue that structured dialogue across difference can reduce polarisation and rebuild civic trust.
sentences.es: Los defensores de la democracia deliberativa argumentan que el diálogo estructurado a través de las diferencias puede reducir la polarización y reconstruir la confianza cívica.

sentences.target: When political opponents are perceived as enemies rather than adversaries, compromise becomes psychologically and politically impossible.
sentences.native: Cuando los oponentes políticos son percibidos como enemigos en lugar de adversarios, el compromiso se vuelve psicológica y políticamente imposible.
sentences.en: When political opponents are perceived as enemies rather than adversaries, compromise becomes psychologically and politically impossible.
sentences.es: Cuando los oponentes políticos son percibidos como enemigos en lugar de adversarios, el compromiso se vuelve psicológica y políticamente imposible.

questions.q: How does the speaker define affective polarisation?
options: Disagreement between parties over specific policy issues
The degree to which partisans dislike and distrust those on the other side
The ideological distance between left and right political parties
The breakdown of cross-party coalition governments
questions.answer: The degree to which partisans dislike and distrust those on the other side

questions.q: Why do social media platforms amplify polarisation according to the speaker?
options: They are designed to promote government propaganda
Content that triggers strong negative emotions generates greater engagement
They restrict the circulation of moderate political opinions
They are primarily used by already politically extreme users
questions.answer: Content that triggers strong negative emotions generates greater engagement

questions.q: What happens when political opponents are perceived as enemies rather than adversaries?
options: New compromise-oriented parties tend to emerge
Compromise becomes psychologically and politically impossible
Voter turnout drops dramatically
Political institutions become stronger in response
questions.answer: Compromise becomes psychologically and politically impossible

audios.title: The surveillance state and digital civil liberties

sentences.target: Mass surveillance capabilities have expanded dramatically with the digitisation of communication and the development of advanced data analytics.
sentences.native: Las capacidades de vigilancia masiva se han expandido dramáticamente con la digitalización de las comunicaciones y el desarrollo de análisis de datos avanzados.
sentences.en: Mass surveillance capabilities have expanded dramatically with the digitisation of communication and the development of advanced data analytics.
sentences.es: Las capacidades de vigilancia masiva se han expandido dramáticamente con la digitalización de las comunicaciones y el desarrollo de análisis de datos avanzados.

sentences.target: The chilling effect of surveillance — where people self-censor knowing they may be watched — poses a fundamental threat to freedom of expression.
sentences.native: El efecto intimidatorio de la vigilancia, donde las personas se autocensuran sabiendo que pueden ser observadas, representa una amenaza fundamental para la libertad de expresión.
sentences.en: The chilling effect of surveillance — where people self-censor knowing they may be watched — poses a fundamental threat to freedom of expression.
sentences.es: El efecto intimidatorio de la vigilancia, donde las personas se autocensuran sabiendo que pueden ser observadas, representa una amenaza fundamental para la libertad de expresión.

sentences.target: Democratic states face a genuine tension between the legitimate security need for intelligence gathering and the civil liberties of their citizens.
sentences.native: Los estados democráticos enfrentan una tensión genuina entre la necesidad legítima de seguridad para la recopilación de inteligencia y las libertades civiles de sus ciudadanos.
sentences.en: Democratic states face a genuine tension between the legitimate security need for intelligence gathering and the civil liberties of their citizens.
sentences.es: Los estados democráticos enfrentan una tensión genuina entre la necesidad legítima de seguridad para la recopilación de inteligencia y las libertades civiles de sus ciudadanos.

sentences.target: Authoritarian regimes have leveraged surveillance technology to identify and suppress political dissent with unprecedented efficiency.
sentences.native: Los regímenes autoritarios han aprovechado la tecnología de vigilancia para identificar y suprimir la disidencia política con eficiencia sin precedentes.
sentences.en: Authoritarian regimes have leveraged surveillance technology to identify and suppress political dissent with unprecedented efficiency.
sentences.es: Los regímenes autoritarios han aprovechado la tecnología de vigilancia para identificar y suprimir la disidencia política con eficiencia sin precedentes.

sentences.target: Meaningful oversight of intelligence agencies requires judicial authorisation, parliamentary scrutiny, and genuine whistleblower protection.
sentences.native: La supervisión significativa de las agencias de inteligencia requiere autorización judicial, escrutinio parlamentario y protección genuina de los denunciantes.
sentences.en: Meaningful oversight of intelligence agencies requires judicial authorisation, parliamentary scrutiny, and genuine whistleblower protection.
sentences.es: La supervisión significativa de las agencias de inteligencia requiere autorización judicial, escrutinio parlamentario y protección genuina de los denunciantes.

questions.q: What does the speaker call the 'chilling effect' of surveillance?
options: The economic cost of running surveillance infrastructure
The way surveillance technology slows down digital communications
Where people self-censor knowing they may be watched
The intimidation of political opponents through public exposure
questions.answer: Where people self-censor knowing they may be watched

questions.q: What tension do democratic states face according to the speaker?
options: Between maintaining sovereignty and complying with international law
Between legitimate security needs for intelligence and citizens' civil liberties
Between transparency to citizens and confidentiality in diplomacy
Between protecting citizens' data and allowing innovation to flourish
questions.answer: Between legitimate security needs for intelligence and citizens' civil liberties

questions.q: What three things does the speaker say meaningful oversight of intelligence agencies requires?
options: Public debate, media scrutiny, and citizen consent
Judicial authorisation, parliamentary scrutiny, and whistleblower protection
Independent review boards, term limits, and public reporting
International monitoring, bilateral agreements, and civil society access
questions.answer: Judicial authorisation, parliamentary scrutiny, and whistleblower protection

audios.title: Multilateralism and the crisis of global governance

sentences.target: The multilateral order built after 1945 rested on the assumption that states could manage shared problems through negotiated rules and international institutions.
sentences.native: El orden multilateral construido después de 1945 descansaba en el supuesto de que los estados podían gestionar problemas compartidos a través de reglas negociadas e instituciones internacionales.
sentences.en: The multilateral order built after 1945 rested on the assumption that states could manage shared problems through negotiated rules and international institutions.
sentences.es: El orden multilateral construido después de 1945 descansaba en el supuesto de que los estados podían gestionar problemas compartidos a través de reglas negociadas e instituciones internacionales.

sentences.target: The rise of great power competition has severely strained the capacity of multilateral institutions to manage global challenges.
sentences.native: El auge de la competencia entre grandes potencias ha tensionado gravemente la capacidad de las instituciones multilaterales para gestionar los desafíos globales.
sentences.en: The rise of great power competition has severely strained the capacity of multilateral institutions to manage global challenges.
sentences.es: El auge de la competencia entre grandes potencias ha tensionado gravemente la capacidad de las instituciones multilaterales para gestionar los desafíos globales.

sentences.target: Multilateral institutions suffer from a principal-agent problem: member states create them but often refuse to cede the authority needed for effective governance.
sentences.native: Las instituciones multilaterales sufren un problema de agente principal: los estados miembros las crean pero a menudo se niegan a ceder la autoridad necesaria para una gobernanza efectiva.
sentences.en: Multilateral institutions suffer from a principal-agent problem: member states create them but often refuse to cede the authority needed for effective governance.
sentences.es: Las instituciones multilaterales sufren un problema de agente principal: los estados miembros las crean pero a menudo se niegan a ceder la autoridad necesaria para una gobernanza efectiva.

sentences.target: Climate change, pandemic preparedness, and nuclear proliferation are problems that no state can solve unilaterally.
sentences.native: El cambio climático, la preparación para pandemias y la proliferación nuclear son problemas que ningún estado puede resolver unilateralmente.
sentences.en: Climate change, pandemic preparedness, and nuclear proliferation are problems that no state can solve unilaterally.
sentences.es: El cambio climático, la preparación para pandemias y la proliferación nuclear son problemas que ningún estado puede resolver unilateralmente.

sentences.target: The reform of multilateral institutions to reflect the shifting distribution of global power is essential but politically fraught.
sentences.native: La reforma de las instituciones multilaterales para reflejar la distribución cambiante del poder global es esencial pero políticamente complicada.
sentences.en: The reform of multilateral institutions to reflect the shifting distribution of global power is essential but politically fraught.
sentences.es: La reforma de las instituciones multilaterales para reflejar la distribución cambiante del poder global es esencial pero políticamente complicada.

questions.q: What assumption did the post-1945 multilateral order rest on according to the speaker?
options: That the United States would serve as the sole global guarantor of peace
That states could manage shared problems through negotiated rules and institutions
That economic interdependence would prevent major conflicts
That nuclear deterrence would create lasting stability between superpowers
questions.answer: That states could manage shared problems through negotiated rules and institutions

questions.q: What principal-agent problem do multilateral institutions suffer from?
options: Secretariats become too powerful and ignore member state preferences
Member states create institutions but often refuse to cede the authority needed for effectiveness
Smaller member states are consistently outvoted by larger powers
Staff appointments are made on political rather than merit-based grounds
questions.answer: Member states create institutions but often refuse to cede the authority needed for effectiveness

questions.q: Why does the speaker say reform of multilateral institutions is politically fraught?
options: Because wealthy nations resist paying larger membership contributions
Because reform requires reflecting the shifting distribution of global power
Because international law prevents structural changes to existing institutions
Because public opinion in most countries opposes international cooperation

questions.q: What do the Nuremberg Code and Declaration of Helsinki establish?

Foundational principles for the ethical conduct of research on human subjects
Legal rights of researchers to publish their findings freely
Standards for the statistical analysis of clinical trial data
questions.answer: Foundational principles for the ethical conduct of research on human subjects

questions.q: Why is the Tuskegee study described as a paradigm case of ethics failure?
options: Researchers fabricated data to obtain continued funding for the study
Black men were deliberately denied treatment to observe natural disease progression
Participants were coerced into joining the study against their will
Researchers published false results that harmed public health policy
questions.answer: Black men were deliberately denied treatment to observe natural disease progression

questions.q: What new ethical challenges does digital research present?
options: The difficulty of recruiting sufficient participants for statistically valid studies
Data privacy, consent for repurposing of data, and research on social media without participants' knowledge
The problem of researchers being biased by their own social media use
The challenge of publishing findings quickly enough to be relevant to policy
questions.answer: Data privacy, consent for repurposing of data, and research on social media without participants' knowledge

audios.title: Open access, knowledge commons and academic publishing

sentences.target: Academic publishers charge substantial subscription fees for access to research that was typically funded by public money and peer-reviewed by unpaid academics.
sentences.native: Las editoriales académicas cobran sustanciales tarifas de suscripción por el acceso a investigaciones que fueron típicamente financiadas con dinero público y revisadas por pares por académicos no remunerados.
sentences.en: Academic publishers charge substantial subscription fees for access to research that was typically funded by public money and peer-reviewed by unpaid academics.
sentences.es: Las editoriales académicas cobran sustanciales tarifas de suscripción por el acceso a investigaciones que fueron típicamente financiadas con dinero público y revisadas por pares por académicos no remunerados.

sentences.target: The open access movement argues that publicly funded research should be freely available to anyone, without paywalls.
sentences.native: El movimiento de acceso abierto argumenta que la investigación financiada públicamente debe estar disponible de forma gratuita para cualquier persona, sin muros de pago.
sentences.en: The open access movement argues that publicly funded research should be freely available to anyone, without paywalls.
sentences.es: El movimiento de acceso abierto argumenta que la investigación financiada públicamente debe estar disponible de forma gratuita para cualquier persona, sin muros de pago.

sentences.target: The rise of article processing charges in gold open access journals has shifted rather than eliminated financial barriers, disadvantaging researchers from lower-income countries.
sentences.cs: El aumento de los cargos por procesamiento de artículos en revistas de acceso abierto dorado ha desplazado en lugar de eliminar las barreras financieras, perjudicando a los investigadores de países de menores ingresos.
sentences.en: The rise of article processing charges in gold open access journals has shifted rather than eliminated financial barriers, disadvantaging researchers from lower-income countries.

sentences.target: Preprint servers such as arXiv and bioRxiv have accelerated the dissemination of research but raise concerns about the circulation of unvetted findings.
sentences.native: Los servidores de preprints como arXiv y bioRxiv han acelerado la difusión de la investigación pero plantean preocupaciones sobre la circulación de hallazgos no verificados.
sentences.en: Preprint servers such as arXiv and bioRxiv have accelerated the dissemination of research but raise concerns about the circulation of unvetted findings.
sentences.es: Los servidores de preprints como arXiv y bioRxiv han acelerado la difusión de la investigación pero plantean preocupaciones sobre la circulación de hallazgos no verificados.

sentences.target: The question of who controls the infrastructure of scientific communication has significant implications for how knowledge is produced and whose knowledge counts.
sentences.native: La pregunta de quién controla la infraestructura de la comunicación científica tiene implicaciones significativas para cómo se produce el conocimiento y de quién es el conocimiento que cuenta.
sentences.en: The question of who controls the infrastructure of scientific communication has significant implications for how knowledge is produced and whose knowledge counts.
sentences.es: La pregunta de quién controla la infraestructura de la comunicación científica tiene implicaciones significativas para cómo se produce el conocimiento y de quién es el conocimiento que cuenta.

questions.q: What contradiction does the speaker identify in the academic publishing model?
options: Publishers charge for access to research funded by public money and peer-reviewed by unpaid academics
Journals accept articles from commercial researchers but not from independent scholars
Academic publishers profit from research that they neither conduct nor fund
Research findings are restricted to subscribers despite being produced in publicly funded universities
questions.answer: Publishers charge for access to research funded by public money and peer-reviewed by unpaid academics

questions.q: What problem does the speaker identify with gold open access article processing charges?
options: They make it too easy for poorly designed studies to be published
They shift rather than eliminate financial barriers, disadvantaging researchers from lower-income countries
They create a perverse incentive to publish more and shorter articles
They discourage collaboration between researchers from different institutions
questions.answer: They shift rather than eliminate financial barriers, disadvantaging researchers from lower-income countries

questions.q: What concern do preprint servers raise according to the speaker?
options: They make it harder for researchers to protect their intellectual property
They allow circulation of unvetted findings that have not been peer-reviewed
They create duplicate publication problems that journals refuse to address
They undermine the prestige of established academic journals
questions.answer: They allow circulation of unvetted findings that have not been peer-reviewed

audios.title: Confirmation bias and motivated reasoning in research

sentences.target: Confirmation bias leads researchers to seek, interpret, and remember information in ways that confirm their pre-existing hypotheses.
sentences.native: El sesgo de confirmación lleva a los investigadores a buscar, interpretar y recordar información de maneras que confirmen sus hipótesis preexistentes.
sentences.en: Confirmation bias leads researchers to seek, interpret, and remember information in ways that confirm their pre-existing hypotheses.
sentences.es: El sesgo de confirmación lleva a los investigadores a buscar, interpretar y recordar información de maneras que confirmen sus hipótesis preexistentes.

sentences.target: Motivated reasoning differs from simple confirmation bias in that it involves the selective deployment of reasoning capacities to reach a desired conclusion.
sentences.native: El razonamiento motivado difiere del simple sesgo de confirmación en que implica el despliegue selectivo de capacidades de razonamiento para alcanzar una conclusión deseada.
sentences.en: Motivated reasoning differs from simple confirmation bias in that it involves the selective deployment of reasoning capacities to reach a desired conclusion.
sentences.es: El razonamiento motivado difiere del simple sesgo de confirmación en que implica el despliegue selectivo de capacidades de razonamiento para alcanzar una conclusión deseada.

sentences.target: Adversarial collaborations, in which researchers who hold opposing views design studies together, are a promising method for reducing the influence of motivated reasoning.
sentences.native: Las colaboraciones adversariales, en las que investigadores con puntos de vista opuestos diseñan estudios juntos, son un método prometedor para reducir la influencia del razonamiento motivado.
sentences.en: Adversarial collaborations, in which researchers who hold opposing views design studies together, are a promising method for reducing the influence of motivated reasoning.
sentences.es: Las colaboraciones adversariales, en las que investigadores con puntos de vista opuestos diseñan estudios juntos, son un método prometedor para reducir la influencia del razonamiento motivado.

sentences.target: Strong inference — the deliberate effort to design experiments that could falsify competing hypotheses — is a powerful antidote to confirmation bias.
sentences.native: La inferencia fuerte, el esfuerzo deliberado de diseñar experimentos que puedan falsificar hipótesis competidoras, es un poderoso antídoto contra el sesgo de confirmación.
sentences.en: Strong inference — the deliberate effort to design experiments that could falsify competing hypotheses — is a powerful antidote to confirmation bias.
sentences.es: La inferencia fuerte, el esfuerzo deliberado de diseñar experimentos que puedan falsificar hipótesis competidoras, es un poderoso antídoto contra el sesgo de confirmación.

sentences.target: The sociology of science reveals that even scientists are embedded in social networks, funding structures, and disciplinary paradigms that shape what questions get asked.
sentences.native: La sociología de la ciencia revela que incluso los científicos están integrados en redes sociales, estructuras de financiación y paradigmas disciplinarios que dan forma a qué preguntas se hacen.
sentences.en: The sociology of science reveals that even scientists are embedded in social networks, funding structures, and disciplinary paradigms that shape what questions get asked.
sentences.es: La sociología de la ciencia revela que incluso los científicos están integrados en redes sociales, estructuras de financiación y paradigmas disciplinarios que dan forma a qué preguntas se hacen.

questions.q: How does motivated reasoning differ from simple confirmation bias?
options: Motivated reasoning is unconscious while confirmation bias is deliberate
Motivated reasoning involves selectively deploying reasoning capacities to reach a desired conclusion
Confirmation bias affects scientists; motivated reasoning affects policymakers
Motivated reasoning only occurs when financial interests are at stake
questions.answer: Motivated reasoning involves selectively deploying reasoning capacities to reach a desired conclusion

questions.q: What are adversarial collaborations designed to do?
options: Allow researchers to compete for the same research funding
Produce more aggressive peer review by involving rivals
Reduce motivated reasoning by having researchers with opposing views design studies together
Speed up research by dividing methodological tasks between teams
questions.answer: Reduce motivated reasoning by having researchers with opposing views design studies together

questions.q: What does the sociology of science reveal about researchers according to the speaker?
options: That scientists are immune to social influences due to rigorous training
That scientists are embedded in social networks and paradigms that shape what questions get asked
That scientific communities are self-correcting faster than critics claim
That funding structures have no significant effect on research outcomes
questions.answer: That scientists are embedded in social networks and paradigms that shape what questions get asked

audios.title: Evidence-based medicine and the hierarchy of evidence

sentences.target: Evidence-based medicine holds that clinical decisions should be grounded in the best available research evidence, integrated with clinical expertise and patient values.
sentences.native: La medicina basada en evidencia sostiene que las decisiones clínicas deben basarse en la mejor evidencia de investigación disponible, integrada con la experiencia clínica y los valores del paciente.
sentences.en: Evidence-based medicine holds that clinical decisions should be grounded in the best available research evidence, integrated with clinical expertise and patient values.
sentences.es: La medicina basada en evidencia sostiene que las decisiones clínicas deben basarse en la mejor evidencia de investigación disponible, integrada con la experiencia clínica y los valores del paciente.

sentences.target: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses sit at the apex of the evidence hierarchy because they synthesise findings across many studies, reducing the influence of single anomalous results.
sentences.native: Las revisiones sistemáticas y los metaanálisis se encuentran en el vértice de la jerarquía de la evidencia porque sintetizan hallazgos de muchos estudios, reduciendo la influencia de resultados individuales anómalos.
sentences.en: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses sit at the apex of the evidence hierarchy because they synthesise findings across many studies, reducing the influence of single anomalous results.
sentences.es: Las revisiones sistemáticas y los metaanálisis se encuentran en el vértice de la jerarquía de la evidencia porque sintetizan hallazgos de muchos estudios, reduciendo la influencia de resultados individuales anómalos.

sentences.target: The randomised controlled trial is the gold standard for evaluating causal claims about treatment effectiveness, as randomisation eliminates selection bias.
sentences.native: El ensayo controlado aleatorio es el estándar de oro para evaluar afirmaciones causales sobre la efectividad del tratamiento, ya que la aleatorización elimina el sesgo de selección.
sentences.en: The randomised controlled trial is the gold standard for evaluating causal claims about treatment effectiveness, as randomisation eliminates selection bias.
sentences.es: El ensayo controlado aleatorio es el estándar de oro para evaluar afirmaciones causales sobre la efectividad del tratamiento, ya que la aleatorización elimina el sesgo de selección.

sentences.target: Absolute risk reduction, rather than relative risk reduction, gives patients and clinicians a more accurate picture of the real-world impact of treatments.
sentences.native: La reducción absoluta del riesgo, en lugar de la reducción relativa del riesgo, da a los pacientes y médicos una imagen más precisa del impacto real de los tratamientos.
sentences.en: Absolute risk reduction, rather than relative risk reduction, gives patients and clinicians a more accurate picture of the real-world impact of treatments.
sentences.es: La reducción absoluta del riesgo, en lugar de la reducción relativa del riesgo, da a los pacientes y médicos una imagen más precisa del impacto real de los tratamientos.

sentences.target: The applicability of trial evidence to individual patients is limited by factors such as comorbidities, age, and the underrepresentation of certain groups in clinical research.
sentences.native: La aplicabilidad de la evidencia de ensayos a pacientes individuales está limitada por factores como comorbilidades, edad y la subrepresentación de ciertos grupos en la investigación clínica.
sentences.en: The applicability of trial evidence to individual patients is limited by factors such as comorbidities, age, and the underrepresentation of certain groups in clinical research.
sentences.es: La aplicabilidad de la evidencia de ensayos a pacientes individuales está limitada por factores como comorbilidades, edad y la subrepresentación de ciertos grupos en la investigación clínica.

questions.q: Why do systematic reviews and meta-analyses sit at the apex of the evidence hierarchy?
options: Because they are conducted by the most eminent researchers in each field
Because they synthesise findings across many studies, reducing the influence of single anomalous results
Because they use the most sophisticated statistical methods available
Because they are subject to the most rigorous peer review process
questions.answer: Because they synthesise findings across many studies, reducing the influence of single anomalous results

questions.q: Why is the randomised controlled trial called the gold standard for causal claims?
options: Because it produces larger sample sizes than observational studies
Because randomisation eliminates selection bias when evaluating treatment effectiveness
Because it is the most cost-effective research design for clinical questions
Because it can be conducted more quickly than longitudinal observational studies
questions.answer: Because randomisation eliminates selection bias when evaluating treatment effectiveness

questions.q: Why does the speaker recommend using absolute rather than relative risk reduction?
options: Absolute risk reduction is easier to calculate using standard statistical software
Absolute risk reduction gives patients and clinicians a more accurate picture of real-world treatment impact
Absolute risk reduction is required by international clinical guidelines
Relative risk reduction consistently exaggerates the benefits of ineffective treatments
questions.answer: Absolute risk reduction gives patients and clinicians a more accurate picture of real-world treatment impact

audios.title: Communicating science to a sceptical public

sentences.target: The deficit model of science communication assumes that public scepticism arises from ignorance, and that providing more information will change attitudes.
sentences.native: El modelo de déficit de comunicación científica asume que el escepticismo público surge de la ignorancia, y que proporcionar más información cambiará las actitudes.
sentences.en: The deficit model of science communication assumes that public scepticism arises from ignorance, and that providing more information will change attitudes.
sentences.es: El modelo de déficit de comunicación científica asume que el escepticismo público surge de la ignorancia, y que proporcionar más información cambiará las actitudes.

sentences.target: Research consistently shows that the deficit model is inadequate: more knowledge does not straightforwardly translate into greater acceptance of scientific consensus.
sentences.native: La investigación muestra consistentemente que el modelo de déficit es inadecuado: más conocimiento no se traduce directamente en mayor aceptación del consenso científico.
sentences.en: Research consistently shows that the deficit model is inadequate: more knowledge does not straightforwardly translate into greater acceptance of scientific consensus.
sentences.es: La investigación muestra consistentemente que el modelo de déficit es inadecuado: más conocimiento no se traduce directamente en mayor aceptación del consenso científico.

sentences.target: Values, identity, and trust in institutions mediate the relationship between scientific knowledge and public beliefs more powerfully than factual understanding.
sentences.native: Los valores, la identidad y la confianza en las instituciones median la relación entre el conocimiento científico y las creencias públicas de manera más poderosa que la comprensión factual.
sentences.en: Values, identity, and trust in institutions mediate the relationship between scientific knowledge and public beliefs more powerfully than factual understanding.
sentences.es: Los valores, la identidad y la confianza en las instituciones median la relación entre el conocimiento científico y las creencias públicas de manera más poderosa que la comprensión factual.

sentences.target: Narrative and emotional framing can be more effective than statistical presentation at making scientific evidence persuasive to general audiences.
sentences.native: El enmarcado narrativo y emocional puede ser más efectivo que la presentación estadística para hacer que la evidencia científica sea persuasiva para audiencias generales.
sentences.en: Narrative and emotional framing can be more effective than statistical presentation at making scientific evidence persuasive to general audiences.
sentences.es: El enmarcado narrativo y emocional puede ser más efectivo que la presentación estadística para hacer que la evidencia científica sea persuasiva para audiencias generales.

sentences.target: Scientists who engage publicly with contested issues face tension between their role as neutral experts and their responsibilities as citizens with expertise-informed views.
sentences.native: Los científicos que participan públicamente en temas controvertidos enfrentan tensión entre su rol como expertos neutrales y sus responsabilidades como ciudadanos con opiniones informadas por su experiencia.
sentences.en: Scientists who engage publicly with contested issues face tension between their role as neutral experts and their responsibilities as citizens with expertise-informed views.
sentences.es: Los científicos que participan públicamente en temas controvertidos enfrentan tensión entre su rol como expertos neutrales y sus responsabilidades como ciudadanos con opiniones informadas por su experiencia.

questions.q: What assumption does the deficit model of science communication make?
options: That scientists need better training in public speaking
That public scepticism arises from ignorance and can be fixed by providing more information
That media coverage of science is systematically biased against expert views
That scientific literacy tests should be required for voters on policy referendums
questions.answer: That public scepticism arises from ignorance and can be fixed by providing more information

questions.q: What do values and identity mediate more powerfully than factual understanding?
options: The relationship between education level and political preferences
The relationship between scientific knowledge and public beliefs
The relationship between media exposure and voting behaviour
The relationship between income and attitudes toward redistribution
questions.answer: The relationship between scientific knowledge and public beliefs

questions.q: What tension do publicly engaged scientists face?
options: Between their obligation to publish and their duty to advise government
Between their role as neutral experts and their responsibilities as citizens with expert-informed views
Between pursuing fundamental research and addressing applied policy questions
Between communicating uncertainty and maintaining credibility with general audiences
questions.answer: Between their role as neutral experts and their responsibilities as citizens with expert-informed views

audios.title: Peer review: strengths, weaknesses and alternatives

sentences.target: Peer review is the process by which submitted manuscripts are evaluated by expert reviewers before publication, providing a quality filter on the scientific literature.
sentences.native: La revisión por pares es el proceso mediante el cual los manuscritos presentados son evaluados por revisores expertos antes de su publicación, proporcionando un filtro de calidad en la literatura científica.
sentences.en: Peer review is the process by which submitted manuscripts are evaluated by expert reviewers before publication, providing a quality filter on the scientific literature.
sentences.es: La revisión por pares es el proceso mediante el cual los manuscritos presentados son evaluados por revisores expertos antes de su publicación, proporcionando un filtro de calidad en la literatura científica.

sentences.target: Studies have found that peer review has low inter-rater reliability: different reviewers often reach opposite conclusions about the same manuscript.
sentences.native: Los estudios han encontrado que la revisión por pares tiene baja confiabilidad entre evaluadores: diferentes revisores a menudo llegan a conclusiones opuestas sobre el mismo manuscrito.
sentences.en: Studies have found that peer review has low inter-rater reliability: different reviewers often reach opposite conclusions about the same manuscript.
sentences.es: Los estudios han encontrado que la revisión por pares tiene baja confiabilidad entre evaluadores: diferentes revisores a menudo llegan a conclusiones opuestas sobre el mismo manuscrito.

sentences.target: Bias in peer review has been documented along the lines of author institution, country of origin, and gender, disadvantaging researchers from less prestigious backgrounds.
sentences.native: El sesgo en la revisión por pares ha sido documentado a lo largo de líneas de institución de autor, país de origen y género, perjudicando a los investigadores de orígenes menos prestigiosos.
sentences.en: Bias in peer review has been documented along the lines of author institution, country of origin, and gender, disadvantaging researchers from less prestigious backgrounds.
sentences.es: El sesgo en la revisión por pares ha sido documentado a lo largo de líneas de institución de autor, país de origen y género, perjudicando a los investigadores de orígenes menos prestigiosos.

sentences.target: Open peer review — in which reviewer identities and reports are published alongside articles — increases accountability and may improve review quality.
sentences.native: La revisión por pares abierta, en la que las identidades de los revisores y los informes se publican junto con los artículos, aumenta la responsabilidad y puede mejorar la calidad de la revisión.
sentences.en: Open peer review — in which reviewer identities and reports are published alongside articles — increases accountability and may improve review quality.
sentences.es: La revisión por pares abierta, en la que las identidades de los revisores y los informes se publican junto con los artículos, aumenta la responsabilidad y puede mejorar la calidad de la revisión.

sentences.target: Despite its well-documented limitations, no alternative mechanism has convincingly replaced peer review as the primary gatekeeper of scientific publication.
sentences.native: A pesar de sus limitaciones bien documentadas, ningún mecanismo alternativo ha reemplazado convincentemente la revisión por pares como el guardián principal de la publicación científica.
sentences.en: Despite its well-documented limitations, no alternative mechanism has convincingly replaced peer review as the primary gatekeeper of scientific publication.
sentences.es: A pesar de sus limitaciones bien documentadas, ningún mecanismo alternativo ha reemplazado convincentemente la revisión por pares como el guardián principal de la publicación científica.

questions.q: What problem with peer review do studies on inter-rater reliability reveal?
options: Reviewers take too long to provide their reports
Different reviewers often reach opposite conclusions about the same manuscript
Reviewers consistently prefer articles from prestigious institutions
Most submitted manuscripts are rejected regardless of quality
questions.answer: Different reviewers often reach opposite conclusions about the same manuscript

questions.q: What bias has been documented in peer review?
options: Bias in favour of authors who have previously reviewed for the same journal
Bias along lines of author institution, country of origin, and gender
Bias toward studies with larger sample sizes and more sophisticated methods
Bias against replication studies and null results
questions.answer: Bias along lines of author institution, country of origin, and gender

questions.q: What does the speaker say about alternatives to peer review?
options: Preprint servers have effectively replaced peer review in most fields
Open peer review has been universally adopted as the superior alternative
No alternative has convincingly replaced peer review as the primary publication gatekeeper
Post-publication peer review is more effective but too slow for practical use
questions.answer: No alternative has convincingly replaced peer review as the primary publication gatekeeper

audios.title: Research funding, priorities and the shaping of knowledge

sentences.target: The distribution of research funding shapes what questions scientists ask, what methods they use, and ultimately what knowledge gets produced.
sentences.native: La distribución del financiamiento de investigación da forma a qué preguntas hacen los científicos, qué métodos usan y en última instancia qué conocimiento se produce.
sentences.en: The distribution of research funding shapes what questions scientists ask, what methods they use, and ultimately what knowledge gets produced.
sentences.es: La distribución del financiamiento de investigación da forma a qué preguntas hacen los científicos, qué métodos usan y en última instancia qué conocimiento se produce.

sentences.target: Industry funding of research creates conflicts of interest that have been shown to bias results toward conclusions favourable to funders.
sentences.native: El financiamiento industrial de la investigación crea conflictos de interés que han demostrado sesgar los resultados hacia conclusiones favorables para los financiadores.
sentences.en: Industry funding of research creates conflicts of interest that have been shown to bias results toward conclusions favourable to funders.
sentences.es: El financiamiento industrial de la investigación crea conflictos de interés que han demostrado sesgar los resultados hacia conclusiones favorables para los financiadores.

sentences.target: The pressure to secure competitive grants drives researchers toward fashionable topics and away from high-risk, potentially transformative research.
sentences.native: La presión para asegurar subvenciones competitivas impulsa a los investigadores hacia temas de moda y alejándolos de la investigación de alto riesgo y potencialmente transformadora.
sentences.en: The pressure to secure competitive grants drives researchers toward fashionable topics and away from high-risk, potentially transformative research.
sentences.es: La presión para asegurar subvenciones competitivas impulsa a los investigadores hacia temas de moda y alejándolos de la investigación de alto riesgo y potencialmente transformadora.

sentences.target: Blue-sky research — basic science without immediate practical application — has historically been the source of the most important long-term technological breakthroughs.
sentences.native: La investigación de cielo azul, la ciencia básica sin aplicación práctica inmediata, ha sido históricamente la fuente de los avances tecnológicos a largo plazo más importantes.
sentences.en: Blue-sky research — basic science without immediate practical application — has historically been the source of the most important long-term technological breakthroughs.
sentences.es: La investigación de cielo azul, la ciencia básica sin aplicación práctica inmediata, ha sido históricamente la fuente de los avances tecnológicos a largo plazo más importantes.

sentences.target: Neglected tropical diseases receive a fraction of global research funding relative to their disease burden, reflecting the purchasing power of affected populations rather than public health need.
sentences.native: Las enfermedades tropicales descuidadas reciben una fracción del financiamiento global de investigación en relación con su carga de enfermedad, reflejando el poder adquisitivo de las poblaciones afectadas en lugar de la necesidad de salud pública.
sentences.en: Neglected tropical diseases receive a fraction of global research funding relative to their disease burden, reflecting the purchasing power of affected populations rather than public health need.
sentences.es: Las enfermedades tropicales descuidadas reciben una fracción del financiamiento global de investigación en relación con su carga de enfermedad, reflejando el poder adquisitivo de las poblaciones afectadas en lugar de la necesidad de salud pública.

questions.q: What does industry funding of research create, according to the speaker?
options: Greater efficiency and faster publication of results
Conflicts of interest that bias results toward conclusions favourable to funders
Better alignment between research topics and real-world applications
Stronger incentives for early-career researchers to enter science
questions.answer: Conflicts of interest that bias results toward conclusions favourable to funders

questions.q: What effect does the pressure to secure competitive grants have on research?
options: It improves research quality by rewarding the best-designed projects
It drives researchers toward fashionable topics and away from high-risk transformative research
It ensures resources are allocated to the most urgent public health priorities
It increases collaboration between academic and industrial researchers
questions.answer: It drives researchers toward fashionable topics and away from high-risk transformative research

questions.q: Why do neglected tropical diseases receive little research funding?
options: Because they are considered too difficult to treat with current technology
Because they affect populations in countries with strong regulatory barriers to research
Because the funding reflects the purchasing power of affected populations rather than public health need
Because researchers prefer to work on conditions they can study in their own countries
questions.answer: Because the funding reflects the purchasing power of affected populations rather than public health need

sentences.target: Quantitative research seeks to measure phenomena numerically, test hypotheses, and generalise findings to broader populations through statistical inference.
sentences.native: La investigación cuantitativa busca medir fenómenos numéricamente, probar hipótesis y generalizar hallazgos a poblaciones más amplias a través de inferencia estadística.
sentences.en: Quantitative research seeks to measure phenomena numerically, test hypotheses, and generalise findings to broader populations through statistical inference.
sentences.es: La investigación cuantitativa busca medir fenómenos numéricamente, probar hipótesis y generalizar hallazgos a poblaciones más amplias a través de inferencia estadística.

sentences.target: Qualitative research explores meanings, experiences, and social processes through methods such as interviews, ethnography, and discourse analysis.
sentences.native: La investigación cualitativa explora significados, experiencias y procesos sociales a través de métodos como entrevistas, etnografía y análisis del discurso.
sentences.en: Qualitative research explores meanings, experiences, and social processes through methods such as interviews, ethnography, and discourse analysis.
sentences.es: La investigación cualitativa explora significados, experiencias y procesos sociales a través de métodos como entrevistas, etnografía y análisis del discurso.

sentences.target: The hierarchy that privileges quantitative methods as more scientific reflects positivist assumptions that are themselves contested within the philosophy of social science.
sentences.native: La jerarquía que privilegia los métodos cuantitativos como más científicos refleja supuestos positivistas que son en sí mismos disputados dentro de la filosofía de las ciencias sociales.
sentences.en: The hierarchy that privileges quantitative methods as more scientific reflects positivist assumptions that are themselves contested within the philosophy of social science.
sentences.es: La jerarquía que privilegia los métodos cuantitativos como más científicos refleja supuestos positivistas que son en sí mismos disputados dentro de la filosofía de las ciencias sociales.

sentences.target: Mixed methods research combines quantitative and qualitative approaches to exploit the complementary strengths of each within a single study.
sentences.native: La investigación de métodos mixtos combina enfoques cuantitativos y cualitativos para explotar las fortalezas complementarias de cada uno dentro de un solo estudio.
sentences.en: Mixed methods research combines quantitative and qualitative approaches to exploit the complementary strengths of each within a single study.
sentences.es: La investigación de métodos mixtos combina enfoques cuantitativos y cualitativos para explotar las fortalezas complementarias de cada uno dentro de un solo estudio.
