audios.title: Climate tipping points and Earth system thresholds

sentences.target: Climate tipping points are thresholds beyond which a change in the Earth system becomes self-sustaining, potentially irreversible, and independent of further human forcing.
sentences.native: Los puntos de inflexión climática son umbrales más allá de los cuales un cambio en el sistema Tierra se vuelve autosostenible, potencialmente irreversible e independiente de más forzamiento humano.
sentences.en: Climate tipping points are thresholds beyond which a change in the Earth system becomes self-sustaining, potentially irreversible, and independent of further human forcing.
sentences.es: Los puntos de inflexión climática son umbrales más allá de los cuales un cambio en el sistema Tierra se vuelve autosostenible, potencialmente irreversible e independiente de más forzamiento humano.

sentences.target: Examples of potential tipping elements include the collapse of the West Antarctic ice sheet, Amazon dieback, and the disruption of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation.
sentences.native: Ejemplos de posibles elementos de inflexión incluyen el colapso de la capa de hielo de la Antártida Occidental, la pérdida de la Amazonia y la interrupción de la Circulación Meridional del Atlántico.
sentences.en: Examples of potential tipping elements include the collapse of the West Antarctic ice sheet, Amazon dieback, and the disruption of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation.
sentences.es: Ejemplos de posibles elementos de inflexión incluyen el colapso de la capa de hielo de la Antártida Occidental, la pérdida de la Amazonia y la interrupción de la Circulación Meridional del Atlántico.

sentences.target: Tipping cascades — where the crossing of one tipping point increases the likelihood of others — could produce non-linear, mutually reinforcing destabilisation of the Earth system.
sentences.native: Las cascadas de inflexión, donde cruzar un punto de inflexión aumenta la probabilidad de otros, podrían producir una desestabilización no lineal y mutuamente reforzada del sistema Tierra.
sentences.en: Tipping cascades — where the crossing of one tipping point increases the likelihood of others — could produce non-linear, mutually reinforcing destabilisation of the Earth system.
sentences.es: Las cascadas de inflexión, donde cruzar un punto de inflexión aumenta la probabilidad de otros, podrían producir una desestabilización no lineal y mutuamente reforzada del sistema Tierra.

sentences.target: The precautionary logic of avoiding tipping point risks is compelling even where scientific uncertainty about the precise thresholds remains high.
sentences.native: La lógica precautoria de evitar los riesgos de los puntos de inflexión es convincente incluso cuando la incertidumbre científica sobre los umbrales precisos sigue siendo alta.
sentences.en: The precautionary logic of avoiding tipping point risks is compelling even where scientific uncertainty about the precise thresholds remains high.
sentences.es: La lógica precautoria de evitar los riesgos de los puntos de inflexión es convincente incluso cuando la incertidumbre científica sobre los umbrales precisos sigue siendo alta.

sentences.target: Current climate models may underestimate tipping point risks because the underlying dynamics involve processes that are difficult to represent at global scale.
sentences.native: Los modelos climáticos actuales pueden subestimar los riesgos de los puntos de inflexión porque las dinámicas subyacentes involucran procesos que son difíciles de representar a escala global.
sentences.en: Current climate models may underestimate tipping point risks because the underlying dynamics involve processes that are difficult to represent at global scale.
sentences.es: Los modelos climáticos actuales pueden subestimar los riesgos de los puntos de inflexión porque las dinámicas subyacentes involucran procesos que son difíciles de representar a escala global.

questions.q: How does the speaker define a climate tipping point?
options: A temperature level at which extreme weather events become more frequent
A political threshold at which governments are forced to adopt climate policies
A threshold beyond which Earth system change becomes self-sustaining and potentially irreversible
A point at which economic losses from climate change exceed adaptation costs
questions.answer: A threshold beyond which Earth system change becomes self-sustaining and potentially irreversible

questions.q: What is a tipping cascade?
options: A rapid succession of extreme weather events in a single region
Where crossing one tipping point increases the likelihood of others, producing mutually reinforcing destabilisation
The cascading economic effects of a climate disaster on financial systems
A sequence of policy failures that prevent effective climate action
questions.answer: Where crossing one tipping point increases the likelihood of others, producing mutually reinforcing destabilisation

questions.q: Why may current climate models underestimate tipping point risks?
options: Because they rely on historical data that predates industrial climate forcing
Because scientists are politically cautious about alarming the public
Because the underlying dynamics involve processes difficult to represent at global scale
Because the models were not designed to simulate extreme warming scenarios
questions.answer: Because the underlying dynamics involve processes difficult to represent at global scale

audios.title: Carbon markets, offsets and the politics of net zero

sentences.target: Carbon markets create a price signal that is intended to incentivise emissions reductions where they are cheapest, theoretically achieving a given mitigation target at lower overall cost.
sentences.native: Los mercados de carbono crean una señal de precios destinada a incentivar las reducciones de emisiones donde son más baratas, logrando teóricamente un objetivo de mitigación dado a un costo global más bajo.
sentences.en: Carbon markets create a price signal that is intended to incentivise emissions reductions where they are cheapest, theoretically achieving a given mitigation target at lower overall cost.
sentences.es: Los mercados de carbono crean una señal de precios destinada a incentivar las reducciones de emisiones donde son más baratas, logrando teóricamente un objetivo de mitigación dado a un costo global más bajo.

sentences.target: Carbon offset markets allow companies to compensate for their own emissions by funding emission reductions or sequestration projects elsewhere.
sentences.native: Los mercados de compensación de carbono permiten a las empresas compensar sus propias emisiones financiando reducciones de emisiones o proyectos de secuestro en otro lugar.
sentences.en: Carbon offset markets allow companies to compensate for their own emissions by funding emission reductions or sequestration projects elsewhere.
sentences.es: Los mercados de compensación de carbono permiten a las empresas compensar sus propias emisiones financiando reducciones de emisiones o proyectos de secuestro en otro lugar.

sentences.target: Criticism of offsets centres on the difficulty of ensuring additionality — that the emission reductions would not have occurred anyway — and permanence, particularly for forestry projects.
sentences.native: La crítica de las compensaciones se centra en la dificultad de garantizar la adicionalidad, que las reducciones de emisiones no habrían ocurrido de todos modos, y la permanencia, particularmente para los proyectos forestales.
sentences.en: Criticism of offsets centres on the difficulty of ensuring additionality — that the emission reductions would not have occurred anyway — and permanence, particularly for forestry projects.
sentences.es: La crítica de las compensaciones se centra en la dificultad de garantizar la adicionalidad, que las reducciones de emisiones no habrían ocurrido de todos modos, y la permanencia, particularmente para los proyectos forestales.

sentences.target: Greenwashing through the purchase of low-quality carbon offsets allows companies to claim net-zero status while continuing to emit without meaningful reductions.
sentences.native: El lavado verde a través de la compra de compensaciones de carbono de baja calidad permite a las empresas reclamar el estado de cero neto mientras continúan emitiendo sin reducciones significativas.
sentences.en: Greenwashing through the purchase of low-quality carbon offsets allows companies to claim net-zero status while continuing to emit without meaningful reductions.
sentences.es: El lavado verde a través de la compra de compensaciones de carbono de baja calidad permite a las empresas reclamar el estado de cero neto mientras continúan emitiendo sin reducciones significativas.

sentences.target: Genuine net zero requires eliminating the vast majority of emissions and balancing only residual hard-to-abate emissions with high-quality carbon removal.
sentences.native: El cero neto genuino requiere eliminar la gran mayoría de las emisiones y equilibrar solo las emisiones residuales difíciles de reducir con eliminación de carbono de alta calidad.
sentences.en: Genuine net zero requires eliminating the vast majority of emissions and balancing only residual hard-to-abate emissions with high-quality carbon removal.
sentences.es: El cero neto genuino requiere eliminar la gran mayoría de las emisiones y equilibrar solo las emisiones residuales difíciles de reducir con eliminación de carbono de alta calidad.

questions.q: What theoretical advantage do carbon markets offer for achieving climate targets?
options: They create binding international commitments that are legally enforceable
They incentivise reductions where cheapest, achieving targets at lower overall cost
They provide predictable revenue streams for renewable energy investment
They create public awareness of the true cost of carbon emissions
questions.answer: They incentivise reductions where cheapest, achieving targets at lower overall cost

questions.q: What is the additionality problem with carbon offsets?
options: Whether the offset project generates enough carbon sequestration to justify its cost
Whether the emission reductions would have occurred anyway without the offset funding
Whether the project is located in the same country as the emitting company
Whether future generations benefit equally from the offset investment
questions.answer: Whether the emission reductions would have occurred anyway without the offset funding

questions.q: What does the speaker say genuine net zero requires?
options: Purchasing sufficient high-quality offsets to balance all current emissions
Eliminating the vast majority of emissions and using carbon removal only for hard-to-abate residual emissions
Achieving a balance between global emissions and natural carbon sinks
Reducing emissions by at least 90% below current levels by 2050
questions.answer: Eliminating the vast majority of emissions and using carbon removal only for hard-to-abate residual emissions

They tend to have the fewest resources for adaptation despite facing the most severe risks

sentences.target: The governance of geoengineering presents profound challenges: who decides whether to deploy it, under what conditions, and who bears the risk of adverse side effects?
sentences.native: La gobernanza de la geoingeniería presenta desafíos profundos: ¿quién decide si desplegarla, bajo qué condiciones y quién asume el riesgo de efectos secundarios adversos?
sentences.en: The governance of geoengineering presents profound challenges: who decides whether to deploy it, under what conditions, and who bears the risk of adverse side effects?

options: Nuclear energy and renewable energy deployment at global scale
Carbon dioxide removal and solar radiation management
Ocean fertilisation and reforestation at planetary scale
Methane capture and nitrous oxide reduction in agriculture
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide removal and solar radiation management

questions.q: What is the termination shock problem?
options: The risk that geoengineering will cause permanent damage to the ozone layer
If solar geoengineering is suddenly stopped, rapid warming could be far worse than any avoided
The economic shock to fossil fuel industries when carbon removal becomes cost-effective
The geopolitical crisis triggered when one country unilaterally deploys geoengineering

questions.q: What governance challenge does geoengineering present?
options: Existing international treaties explicitly prohibit all forms of environmental modification
No country has the technical capacity to deploy geoengineering unilaterally
It is unclear who decides whether to deploy it, under what conditions, and who bears risk of side effects
The scientific community is divided over whether geoengineering research should be conducted
questions.answer: It is unclear who decides whether to deploy it, under what conditions, and who bears risk of side effects

audios.title: The Responsibility to Protect and the limits of sovereignty

sentences.target: The Responsibility to Protect doctrine holds that sovereignty entails responsibility: states that fail to protect their populations from atrocity crimes forfeit the shield of non-intervention.
sentences.native: La doctrina de la Responsabilidad de Proteger sostiene que la soberanía implica responsabilidad: los estados que no protegen a sus poblaciones de crímenes de atrocidad pierden el escudo de la no intervención.
sentences.en: The Responsibility to Protect doctrine holds that sovereignty entails responsibility: states that fail to protect their populations from atrocity crimes forfeit the shield of non-intervention.
sentences.es: La doctrina de la Responsabilidad de Proteger sostiene que la soberanía implica responsabilidad: los estados que no protegen a sus poblaciones de crímenes de atrocidad pierden el escudo de la no intervención.

sentences.target: R2P was unanimously endorsed by the UN General Assembly in 2005 but has proved deeply contested in practice, with interventions often alleged to be selective or politically motivated.
sentences.native: La RdeP fue respaldada unánimemente por la Asamblea General de la ONU en 2005 pero ha resultado profundamente controvertida en la práctica, con intervenciones frecuentemente señaladas como selectivas o políticamente motivadas.
sentences.en: R2P was unanimously endorsed by the UN General Assembly in 2005 but has proved deeply contested in practice, with interventions often alleged to be selective or politically motivated.
sentences.es: La RdeP fue respaldada unánimemente por la Asamblea General de la ONU en 2005 pero ha resultado profundamente controvertida en la práctica, con intervenciones frecuentemente señaladas como selectivas o políticamente motivadas.

sentences.target: The Security Council veto means that R2P cannot be invoked against states allied with a permanent member, creating a fundamental accountability gap at the heart of the doctrine.
sentences.native: El veto del Consejo de Seguridad significa que la RdeP no puede invocarse contra estados aliados con un miembro permanente, creando una brecha de responsabilidad fundamental en el corazón de la doctrina.
sentences.en: The Security Council veto means that R2P cannot be invoked against states allied with a permanent member, creating a fundamental accountability gap at the heart of the doctrine.
sentences.es: El veto del Consejo de Seguridad significa que la RdeP no puede invocarse contra estados aliados con un miembro permanente, creando una brecha de responsabilidad fundamental en el corazón de la doctrina.

sentences.target: Critics argue that humanitarian intervention under R2P has been used as a pretext for regime change that exceeds its stated mandate, as illustrated by the controversy over the Libya intervention.
sentences.native: Los críticos argumentan que la intervención humanitaria bajo la RdeP ha sido utilizada como pretexto para el cambio de régimen que excede su mandato declarado, como lo ilustra la controversia sobre la intervención en Libia.
sentences.en: Critics argue that humanitarian intervention under R2P has been used as a pretext for regime change that exceeds its stated mandate, as illustrated by the controversy over the Libya intervention.
sentences.es: Los críticos argumentan que la intervención humanitaria bajo la RdeP ha sido utilizada como pretexto para el cambio de régimen que excede su mandato declarado, como lo ilustra la controversia sobre la intervención en Libia.

sentences.target: The tension between R2P and the principle of sovereign equality reflects a deeper unresolved question about the relationship between international human rights law and the Westphalian state system.
sentences.native: La tensión entre la RdeP y el principio de igualdad soberana refleja una pregunta más profunda sin resolver sobre la relación entre el derecho internacional de derechos humanos y el sistema estatal westfaliano.
sentences.en: The tension between R2P and the principle of sovereign equality reflects a deeper unresolved question about the relationship between international human rights law and the Westphalian state system.
sentences.es: La tensión entre la RdeP y el principio de igualdad soberana refleja una pregunta más profunda sin resolver sobre la relación entre el derecho internacional de derechos humanos y el sistema estatal westfaliano.

questions.q: What does the Responsibility to Protect doctrine hold about sovereignty?
options: Sovereignty is absolute and cannot be overridden by any external authority
Sovereignty entails responsibility; states that fail to protect populations forfeit the shield of non-intervention
Sovereignty is a legal fiction that should be replaced by global governance
Sovereignty applies only to states that comply with international human rights standards
questions.answer: Sovereignty entails responsibility; states that fail to protect populations forfeit the shield of non-intervention

questions.q: What fundamental accountability gap does the Security Council veto create for R2P?
options: It means the UN Secretary-General cannot invoke R2P without member state approval
It means R2P cannot be invoked against states allied with a permanent Security Council member
It prevents the International Criminal Court from prosecuting atrocity crimes under R2P
It makes Security Council resolutions on humanitarian intervention legally unenforceable
questions.answer: It means R2P cannot be invoked against states allied with a permanent Security Council member

questions.q: What concern about the Libya intervention does the speaker raise?
options: The intervention caused more civilian casualties than the threat it was meant to prevent
Humanitarian intervention under R2P was used as a pretext for regime change beyond its mandate
The Security Council resolution was passed without adequate debate or legal review
The intervention failed to protect the civilian population it was designed to safeguard
questions.answer: Humanitarian intervention under R2P was used as a pretext for regime change beyond its mandate

audios.title: International criminal justice and the challenge of accountability

sentences.target: The International Criminal Court was established by the Rome Statute in 2002 to prosecute individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of aggression.
sentences.native: La Corte Penal Internacional fue establecida por el Estatuto de Roma en 2002 para procesar a individuos por genocidio, crímenes de guerra, crímenes de lesa humanidad y el crimen de agresión.
sentences.en: The International Criminal Court was established by the Rome Statute in 2002 to prosecute individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of aggression.
sentences.es: La Corte Penal Internacional fue establecida por el Estatuto de Roma en 2002 para procesar a individuos por genocidio, crímenes de guerra, crímenes de lesa humanidad y el crimen de agresión.

sentences.target: The principle of complementarity means the ICC only acts when states are unable or unwilling to genuinely investigate and prosecute crimes within their jurisdiction.
sentences.native: El principio de complementariedad significa que la CPI solo actúa cuando los estados no pueden o no quieren investigar y procesar genuinamente los crímenes dentro de su jurisdicción.
sentences.en: The principle of complementarity means the ICC only acts when states are unable or unwilling to genuinely investigate and prosecute crimes within their jurisdiction.
sentences.es: El principio de complementariedad significa que la CPI solo actúa cuando los estados no pueden o no quieren investigar y procesar genuinamente los crímenes dentro de su jurisdicción.

sentences.target: The ICC's limited jurisdiction — which excludes major powers including the United States, Russia, and China — severely constrains its capacity to deliver universal justice.
sentences.native: La jurisdicción limitada de la CPI, que excluye a las grandes potencias incluidas Estados Unidos, Rusia y China, restringe gravemente su capacidad para administrar justicia universal.
sentences.en: The ICC's limited jurisdiction — which excludes major powers including the United States, Russia, and China — severely constrains its capacity to deliver universal justice.
sentences.es: La jurisdicción limitada de la CPI, que excluye a las grandes potencias incluidas Estados Unidos, Rusia y China, restringe gravemente su capacidad para administrar justicia universal.

sentences.target: Tensions between peace and justice arise when prosecuting atrocity perpetrators may undermine fragile peace negotiations by removing incentives for armed actors to negotiate.
sentences.native: Las tensiones entre paz y justicia surgen cuando el procesamiento de los perpetradores de atrocidades puede socavar las frágiles negociaciones de paz al eliminar los incentivos para que los actores armados negocien.
sentences.en: Tensions between peace and justice arise when prosecuting atrocity perpetrators may undermine fragile peace negotiations by removing incentives for armed actors to negotiate.
sentences.es: Las tensiones entre paz y justicia surgen cuando el procesamiento de los perpetradores de atrocidades puede socavar las frágiles negociaciones de paz al eliminar los incentivos para que los actores armados negocien.

sentences.target: The selective prosecution of powerful versus weak states and non-state actors has led critics to characterise international criminal justice as 'victor's justice' or as an instrument of Western power.
sentences.native: El enjuiciamiento selectivo de estados poderosos versus débiles y actores no estatales ha llevado a los críticos a caracterizar la justicia penal internacional como 'justicia del vencedor' o como instrumento del poder occidental.

questions.q: What does the principle of complementarity mean for the ICC?
options: The ICC complements regional human rights courts by handling the most serious cases
The ICC only acts when states are unable or unwilling to genuinely investigate crimes themselves
The ICC's jurisdiction complements that of the UN Security Council on peace and security matters
The ICC requires two states to jointly refer a situation before it can open an investigation
questions.answer: The ICC only acts when states are unable or unwilling to genuinely investigate crimes themselves

questions.q: What tension between peace and justice does the speaker describe?
options: Whether it is just to punish individuals for crimes committed under orders from superiors
Prosecuting atrocity perpetrators may undermine peace negotiations by removing incentives to negotiate
Whether international courts should prioritise reparations for victims over criminal punishment
The difficulty of gathering evidence in active conflict zones without endangering witnesses
questions.answer: Prosecuting atrocity perpetrators may undermine peace negotiations by removing incentives to negotiate

questions.q: What criticism do critics make of international criminal justice?
options: It focuses too heavily on individual accountability rather than structural reform
It is too slow and expensive to serve as a genuine deterrent against atrocities
Selective prosecution of weaker states has led it to be characterised as victor's justice
It has failed to develop a coherent body of jurisprudence on complex atrocity crimes
questions.answer: Selective prosecution of weaker states has led it to be characterised as victor's justice

audios.title: Economic sanctions as a foreign policy instrument

sentences.target: Economic sanctions impose costs on target states to coerce a change in policy, signal disapproval, or punish violations of international norms, without resort to military force.

sentences.en: Economic sanctions impose costs on target states to coerce a change in policy, signal disapproval, or punish violations of international norms, without resort to military force.
sentences.es: Las sanciones económicas imponen costos a los estados objetivo para coaccionar un cambio de política, señalar desaprobación o castigar las violaciones de las normas internacionales, sin recurrir a la fuerza militar.

sentences.target: The effectiveness of sanctions in achieving their stated goals is contested in the scholarly literature; studies suggest success rates are modest and conditions-dependent.
sentences.native: La efectividad de las sanciones para lograr sus objetivos declarados es controvertida en la literatura académica; los estudios sugieren que las tasas de éxito son modestas y dependen de las condiciones.

sentences.target: Smart or targeted sanctions attempt to focus pressure on specific individuals — leaders, oligarchs, generals — through travel bans and asset freezes, minimising collateral civilian harm.
sentences.native: Las sanciones inteligentes o dirigidas intentan concentrar la presión en individuos específicos, líderes, oligarcas, generales, mediante prohibiciones de viaje y congelación de activos, minimizando el daño civil colateral.

sentences.target: Sanctions effectiveness depends critically on multilateral enforcement: unilateral sanctions by a single state can be circumvented if target states find alternative partners.
sentences.native: La efectividad de las sanciones depende fundamentalmente de la aplicación multilateral: las sanciones unilaterales de un solo estado pueden eludirse si los estados objetivo encuentran socios alternativos.
sentences.en: Sanctions effectiveness depends critically on multilateral enforcement: unilateral sanctions by a single state can be circumvented if target states find alternative partners.
sentences.es: La efectividad de las sanciones depende fundamentalmente de la aplicación multilateral: las sanciones unilaterales de un solo estado pueden eludirse si los estados objetivo encuentran socios alternativos.

questions.q: What three goals do economic sanctions aim to achieve according to the speaker?
options: Deter future aggression, punish past behaviour, and reward compliance
Coerce a policy change, signal disapproval, and punish violations of norms
Isolate target states, support opposition groups, and build international coalitions
Create economic crises, trigger regime change, and restore international order
questions.answer: Coerce a policy change, signal disapproval, and punish violations of norms

questions.q: What problem do comprehensive sanctions regimes create?
options: They require unanimous consent in the UN Security Council to remain legitimate
They can impose severe humanitarian costs on civilians while insulating the intended elite targets
They are too slow to implement to be effective in fast-moving crises
They tend to increase the target state's international support and legitimacy

questions.q: Why does sanctions effectiveness depend on multilateral enforcement?
options: Because international law prohibits unilateral sanctions without Security Council authorisation
Because single-state sanctions can be circumvented if target states find alternative partners
Because multilateral sanctions are harder to challenge in international courts
Because powerful states are less likely to comply with sanctions they did not help design
questions.answer: Because single-state sanctions can be circumvented if target states find alternative partners

audios.title: Nuclear deterrence, disarmament and strategic stability

sentences.target: Nuclear deterrence theory holds that the catastrophic consequences of nuclear exchange prevent rational states from initiating armed conflict that could escalate to nuclear use.
sentences.native: La teoría de la disuasión nuclear sostiene que las consecuencias catastróficas de un intercambio nuclear impiden que los estados racionales inicien un conflicto armado que podría escalar al uso nuclear.
sentences.en: Nuclear deterrence theory holds that the catastrophic consequences of nuclear exchange prevent rational states from initiating armed conflict that could escalate to nuclear use.
sentences.es: La teoría de la disuasión nuclear sostiene que las consecuencias catastróficas de un intercambio nuclear impiden que los estados racionales inicien un conflicto armado que podría escalar al uso nuclear.

sentences.target: Mutual assured destruction provided a perverse but arguably stable equilibrium during the Cold War, yet it rested on assumptions about rationality that could fail under real-world pressures.
sentences.native: La destrucción mutua asegurada proporcionó un equilibrio perverso pero posiblemente estable durante la Guerra Fría, sin embargo descansó en supuestos sobre la racionalidad que podrían fallar bajo presiones del mundo real.

sentences.target: The proliferation of nuclear weapons to additional states increases the probability that deterrence will fail due to miscalculation, miscommunication, or the involvement of non-state actors.
sentences.native: La proliferación de armas nucleares a estados adicionales aumenta la probabilidad de que la disuasión falle debido a un error de cálculo, mala comunicación o la participación de actores no estatales.
sentences.en: The proliferation of nuclear weapons to additional states increases the probability that deterrence will fail due to miscalculation, miscommunication, or the involvement of non-state actors.
sentences.es: La proliferación de armas nucleares a estados adicionales aumenta la probabilidad de que la disuasión falle debido a un error de cálculo, mala comunicación o la participación de actores no estatales.

sentences.target: The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons represents a normative challenge to deterrence doctrine, rejecting the legitimacy of nuclear weapons as a security instrument.
sentences.native: El Tratado sobre la Prohibición de las Armas Nucleares representa un desafío normativo a la doctrina de la disuasión, rechazando la legitimidad de las armas nucleares como instrumento de seguridad.

sentences.target: Strategic stability is increasingly challenged by the development of hypersonic delivery systems, cyber capabilities targeting nuclear command and control, and the erosion of arms control agreements.

sentences.en: Strategic stability is increasingly challenged by the development of hypersonic delivery systems, cyber capabilities targeting nuclear command and control, and the erosion of arms control agreements.

questions.q: What assumption does nuclear deterrence theory rest on?
options: That states are willing to use nuclear weapons first if sufficiently threatened
That catastrophic consequences of nuclear exchange prevent rational states from initiating conflict
That international law provides sufficient constraints on nuclear weapons use
That the economic costs of nuclear programmes deter most states from pursuing them

questions.q: What risk does nuclear proliferation increase according to the speaker?
options: That existing nuclear states will develop larger arsenals to maintain superiority
That international disarmament negotiations will permanently break down
That deterrence will fail due to miscalculation, miscommunication, or non-state actors
That conventional military conflicts will escalate more rapidly than during the Cold War
questions.answer: That deterrence will fail due to miscalculation, miscommunication, or non-state actors

questions.q: What challenges to strategic stability does the speaker identify?
options: Declining defence budgets in NATO states and increasing Russian conventional forces
Hypersonic delivery systems, cyber capabilities targeting nuclear command, and erosion of arms control
The emergence of new nuclear powers in Asia and the Middle East
The development of missile defence systems that undermine deterrence equilibria
questions.answer: Hypersonic delivery systems, cyber capabilities targeting nuclear command, and erosion of arms control

audios.title: Refugee law, asylum and the right to protection

sentences.en: The 1951 Refugee Convention defines a refugee as a person who has a well-founded fear of persecution on grounds of race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership of a particular social group.
sentences.es: La Convención de Refugiados de 1951 define a un refugiado como una persona que tiene un temor fundado de persecución por motivos de raza, religión, nacionalidad, opinión política o pertenencia a un determinado grupo social.

sentences.target: Non-refoulement — the principle that no one may be returned to a country where they face serious risk of harm — is widely regarded as a jus cogens norm of international law.

sentences.en: The distinction between refugees — who meet the 1951 Convention definition — and economic migrants — who move primarily for economic reasons — is legally significant but increasingly difficult to apply.

sentences.native: El desplazamiento climático, el movimiento forzado de personas debido a eventos relacionados con el clima, no está cubierto por la Convención de 1951, creando una importante brecha de protección legal para una población creciente.

questions.q: What grounds does the 1951 Refugee Convention recognise for refugee status?
options: Poverty, conflict, and natural disaster
Race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership of a particular social group
Any circumstance where return would cause serious hardship
Specific categories of state-sponsored persecution only
questions.answer: Race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership of a particular social group

questions.q: What does the principle of non-refoulement prohibit?
options: The deportation of asylum seekers before their claims have been assessed
Returning anyone to a country where they face a serious risk of harm
The detention of asylum seekers awaiting a decision on their status

questions.q: What does the speaker say is lost when a dominant language displaces a minority one?
options: Primarily vocabulary and grammatical structures that are difficult to document
Only the spoken forms of the language since writing systems can be preserved
The entire cultural logic, ecological knowledge, and worldview embedded in the language
The political institutions and economic systems of the minority community
questions.answer: The entire cultural logic, ecological knowledge, and worldview embedded in the language

questions.q: What benefit does the speaker attribute to developing metalinguistic awareness?
options: Faster acquisition of grammar rules in a second language
A deeper engagement with the ideological dimensions of texts
Better pronunciation and accent reduction in spoken language
Improved memory retention of vocabulary and idiomatic expressions
questions.answer: A deeper engagement with the ideological dimensions of texts

sentences.target: Connotation — the emotional and cultural associations that words carry beyond their literal definitions — is one of the most powerful and least consciously recognised aspects of how language shapes thought.
sentences.native: La connotación, las asociaciones emocionales y culturales que las palabras llevan más allá de sus definiciones literales, es uno de los aspectos más poderosos y menos conscientemente reconocidos de cómo el lenguaje moldea el pensamiento.
sentences.en: Connotation — the emotional and cultural associations that words carry beyond their literal definitions — is one of the most powerful and least consciously recognised aspects of how language shapes thought.
sentences.es: La connotación, las asociaciones emocionales y culturales que las palabras llevan más allá de sus definiciones literales, es uno de los aspectos más poderosos y menos conscientemente reconocidos de cómo el lenguaje moldea el pensamiento.

sentences.target: Euphemism allows speakers to discuss difficult realities — death, failure, violence, discrimination — while maintaining social comfort, but it also risks trivialising or obscuring those realities in ways that serve political purposes.
sentences.native: El eufemismo permite a los hablantes discutir realidades difíciles, muerte, fracaso, violencia, discriminación, mientras mantienen la comodidad social, pero también arriesga trivializar u obscurecer esas realidades de maneras que sirven propósitos políticos.
sentences.en: Euphemism allows speakers to discuss difficult realities — death, failure, violence, discrimination — while maintaining social comfort, but it also risks trivialising or obscuring those realities in ways that serve political purposes.
sentences.es: El eufemismo permite a los hablantes discutir realidades difíciles, muerte, fracaso, violencia, discriminación, mientras mantienen la comodidad social, pero también arriesga trivializar u obscurecer esas realidades de maneras que sirven propósitos políticos.

sentences.target: The distinction between descriptivism — recording how language is actually used — and prescriptivism — enforcing rules about how it should be used — reflects a tension between linguistic authenticity and social standardisation.
sentences.native: La distinción entre el descriptivismo, registrar cómo se usa el idioma realmente, y el prescriptivismo, imponer reglas sobre cómo debería usarse, refleja una tensión entre la autenticidad lingüística y la estandarización social.
sentences.en: The distinction between descriptivism — recording how language is actually used — and prescriptivism — enforcing rules about how it should be used — reflects a tension between linguistic authenticity and social standardisation.
sentences.es: La distinción entre el descriptivismo, registrar cómo se usa el idioma realmente, y el prescriptivismo, imponer reglas sobre cómo debería usarse, refleja una tensión entre la autenticidad lingüística y la estandarización social.

sentences.target: Neologisms are linguistic fossils in reverse: where fossils record what once existed, neologisms document emerging realities, reflecting new technologies, social arrangements, and cultural anxieties as they crystallise into shared concepts.
sentences.native: Los neologismos son fósiles lingüísticos al revés: donde los fósiles registran lo que existió una vez, los neologismos documentan realidades emergentes, reflejando nuevas tecnologías, acuerdos sociales y ansiedades culturales a medida que se cristalizan en conceptos compartidos.
sentences.en: Neologisms are linguistic fossils in reverse: where fossils record what once existed, neologisms document emerging realities, reflecting new technologies, social arrangements, and cultural anxieties as they crystallise into shared concepts.
sentences.es: Los neologismos son fósiles lingüísticos al revés: donde los fósiles registran lo que existió una vez, los neologismos documentan realidades emergentes, reflejando nuevas tecnologías, acuerdos sociales y ansiedades culturales a medida que se cristalizan en conceptos compartidos.

sentences.target: Semiotics — the study of signs and their meanings — reveals that communication extends far beyond words to include gestures, images, spatial arrangements, and the countless non-verbal signals through which meaning is continuously negotiated.
sentences.native: La semiótica, el estudio de los signos y sus significados, revela que la comunicación se extiende mucho más allá de las palabras para incluir gestos, imágenes, disposiciones espaciales y las innumerables señales no verbales a través de las cuales el significado se negocia continuamente.
sentences.en: Semiotics — the study of signs and their meanings — reveals that communication extends far beyond words to include gestures, images, spatial arrangements, and the countless non-verbal signals through which meaning is continuously negotiated.
sentences.es: La semiótica, el estudio de los signos y sus significados, revela que la comunicación se extiende mucho más allá de las palabras para incluir gestos, imágenes, disposiciones espaciales y las innumerables señales no verbales a través de las cuales el significado se negocia continuamente.

questions.q: How does the speaker describe connotation?
options: The grammatical rules governing word order in a sentence
The emotional and cultural associations words carry beyond their literal definitions
The process by which new words enter the formal dictionary
The phonetic properties that distinguish one word from another
questions.answer: The emotional and cultural associations words carry beyond their literal definitions

questions.q: What risk does the speaker associate with euphemism?
options: Confusing audiences who prefer direct and unambiguous communication
Making language more difficult to learn for non-native speakers
Trivialising or obscuring realities in ways that serve political purposes
Reducing the precision and clarity of academic and legal discourse
questions.answer: Trivialising or obscuring realities in ways that serve political purposes

questions.q: What does the speaker say neologisms document?
options: The historical evolution of grammar rules across different language families
The influence of classical Latin and Greek on modern vocabulary
Emerging realities including new technologies and cultural anxieties
The differences in register between formal and informal modes of communication
questions.answer: Emerging realities including new technologies and cultural anxieties

audios.title: English as a Global Lingua Franca

sentences.target: The rise of English to global dominance was not the product of any intrinsic linguistic superiority but rather the result of specific historical processes: British colonialism, American economic and cultural hegemony, and the technological architectures of the internet age.
sentences.native: El ascenso del inglés a la dominancia global no fue el producto de ninguna superioridad lingüística intrínseca sino el resultado de procesos históricos específicos: el colonialismo británico, la hegemonía económica y cultural estadounidense, y las arquitecturas tecnológicas de la era de internet.
sentences.en: The rise of English to global dominance was not the product of any intrinsic linguistic superiority but rather the result of specific historical processes: British colonialism, American economic and cultural hegemony, and the technological architectures of the internet age.
sentences.es: El ascenso del inglés a la dominancia global no fue el producto de ninguna superioridad lingüística intrínseca sino el resultado de procesos históricos específicos: el colonialismo británico, la hegemonía económica y cultural estadounidense, y las arquitecturas tecnológicas de la era de internet.

sentences.target: When speakers from different language backgrounds communicate in English as their shared medium, the language inevitably absorbs features from their native tongues, producing the rich diversity of Englishes now spoken across the globe.
sentences.native: Cuando hablantes de diferentes orígenes lingüísticos se comunican en inglés como medio compartido, el idioma absorbe inevitablemente características de sus lenguas nativas, produciendo la rica diversidad de ingleses que ahora se habla en todo el mundo.
sentences.en: When speakers from different language backgrounds communicate in English as their shared medium, the language inevitably absorbs features from their native tongues, producing the rich diversity of Englishes now spoken across the globe.
sentences.es: Cuando hablantes de diferentes orígenes lingüísticos se comunican en inglés como medio compartido, el idioma absorbe inevitablemente características de sus lenguas nativas, produciendo la rica diversidad de ingleses que ahora se habla en todo el mundo.

sentences.target: The global dominance of English creates what linguists call 'linguistic privilege': native English speakers communicate effortlessly in a world where others must invest years of labour simply to participate on equal terms.
sentences.native: La dominancia global del inglés crea lo que los lingüistas llaman 'privilegio lingüístico': los hablantes nativos de inglés se comunican sin esfuerzo en un mundo donde otros deben invertir años de trabajo simplemente para participar en igualdad de condiciones.
sentences.en: The global dominance of English creates what linguists call 'linguistic privilege': native English speakers communicate effortlessly in a world where others must invest years of labour simply to participate on equal terms.
sentences.es: La dominancia global del inglés crea lo que los lingüistas llaman 'privilegio lingüístico': los hablantes nativos de inglés se comunican sin esfuerzo en un mundo donde otros deben invertir años de trabajo simplemente para participar en igualdad de condiciones.

sentences.target: Research into multilingualism consistently finds that the capacity to operate across two or more linguistic systems enhances cognitive flexibility, metacognitive awareness, and the ability to hold multiple perspectives simultaneously.
sentences.native: La investigación sobre el multilingüismo encuentra consistentemente que la capacidad de operar a través de dos o más sistemas lingüísticos mejora la flexibilidad cognitiva, la conciencia metacognitiva y la habilidad de mantener múltiples perspectivas simultáneamente.
sentences.en: Research into multilingualism consistently finds that the capacity to operate across two or more linguistic systems enhances cognitive flexibility, metacognitive awareness, and the ability to hold multiple perspectives simultaneously.
sentences.es: La investigación sobre el multilingüismo encuentra consistentemente que la capacidad de operar a través de dos o más sistemas lingüísticos mejora la flexibilidad cognitiva, la conciencia metacognitiva y la habilidad de mantener múltiples perspectivas simultáneamente.

sentences.target: For the advanced learner, the goal is not merely to sound native but to develop a sophisticated command that includes sensitivity to register, cultural inference, and the connotative weight of vocabulary choices — the qualities that distinguish fluency from mastery.
sentences.native: Para el estudiante avanzado, el objetivo no es simplemente sonar nativo sino desarrollar un dominio sofisticado que incluya sensibilidad al registro, inferencia cultural y el peso connotativo de las elecciones de vocabulario, las cualidades que distinguen la fluidez del dominio.
sentences.en: For the advanced learner, the goal is not merely to sound native but to develop a sophisticated command that includes sensitivity to register, cultural inference, and the connotative weight of vocabulary choices — the qualities that distinguish fluency from mastery.
sentences.es: Para el estudiante avanzado, el objetivo no es simplemente sonar nativo sino desarrollar un dominio sofisticado que incluya sensibilidad al registro, inferencia cultural y el peso connotativo de las elecciones de vocabulario, las cualidades que distinguen la fluidez del dominio.

questions.q: What does the speaker attribute the rise of English to global dominance to?
options: The inherent simplicity and flexibility of English grammar
The richness and expressiveness of the English literary tradition
British colonialism, American hegemony, and internet-age technological architectures
The widespread adoption of English as the official language of international institutions
questions.answer: British colonialism, American hegemony, and internet-age technological architectures

questions.q: What do linguists call the advantage native English speakers have in a globalised world?
options: Cultural capital
Linguistic privilege
Communicative competence
Language dominance
questions.answer: Linguistic privilege

questions.q: What qualities does the speaker say distinguish fluency from mastery?
options: Speed of production and breadth of vocabulary in academic contexts
The ability to understand native speakers in unscripted conversational settings
Sensitivity to register, cultural inference, and the connotative weight of vocabulary
Consistent grammatical accuracy in both written and spoken communication
questions.answer: Sensitivity to register, cultural inference, and the connotative weight of vocabulary

sentences.target: Globalisation's central paradox is that it has simultaneously been the most powerful engine of economic growth in human history — lifting hundreds of millions out of extreme poverty — and one of the most potent generators of inequality within developed nations.
sentences.native: La paradoja central de la globalización es que ha sido simultáneamente el motor más poderoso de crecimiento económico en la historia humana, sacando a cientos de millones de la pobreza extrema, y uno de los generadores más potentes de desigualdad dentro de las naciones desarrolladas.
sentences.en: Globalisation's central paradox is that it has simultaneously been the most powerful engine of economic growth in human history — lifting hundreds of millions out of extreme poverty — and one of the most potent generators of inequality within developed nations.
sentences.es: La paradoja central de la globalización es que ha sido simultáneamente el motor más poderoso de crecimiento económico en la historia humana, sacando a cientos de millones de la pobreza extrema, y uno de los generadores más potentes de desigualdad dentro de las naciones desarrolladas.

sentences.target: Trade liberalisation generates aggregate economic gains, but these gains are distributed unequally: highly educated workers in export-oriented sectors benefit substantially, while manufacturing workers in import-competing industries bear concentrated, long-lasting costs.
sentences.native: La liberalización comercial genera ganancias económicas agregadas, pero estas ganancias se distribuyen de manera desigual: los trabajadores altamente educados en sectores orientados a la exportación se benefician sustancialmente, mientras que los trabajadores manufactureros en industrias que compiten con importaciones asumen costos concentrados y duraderos.
sentences.en: Trade liberalisation generates aggregate economic gains, but these gains are distributed unequally: highly educated workers in export-oriented sectors benefit substantially, while manufacturing workers in import-competing industries bear concentrated, long-lasting costs.
sentences.es: La liberalización comercial genera ganancias económicas agregadas, pero estas ganancias se distribuyen de manera desigual: los trabajadores altamente educados en sectores orientados a la exportación se benefician sustancialmente, mientras que los trabajadores manufactureros en industrias que compiten con importaciones asumen costos concentrados y duraderos.

sentences.target: The global supply chain revolution enabled corporations to fragment production across dozens of countries, reducing costs dramatically while simultaneously making both individual firms and national economies acutely vulnerable to disruption.
sentences.native: La revolución de la cadena de suministro global permitió a las corporaciones fragmentar la producción en docenas de países, reduciendo dramáticamente los costos mientras que simultáneamente hacía que tanto las empresas individuales como las economías nacionales fueran agudamente vulnerables a las disrupciones.
sentences.en: The global supply chain revolution enabled corporations to fragment production across dozens of countries, reducing costs dramatically while simultaneously making both individual firms and national economies acutely vulnerable to disruption.
sentences.es: La revolución de la cadena de suministro global permitió a las corporaciones fragmentar la producción en docenas de países, reduciendo dramáticamente los costos mientras que simultáneamente hacía que tanto las empresas individuales como las economías nacionales fueran agudamente vulnerables a las disrupciones.

sentences.target: Capital's ability to move across borders far more freely than labour creates a structural asymmetry: corporations can credibly threaten to offshore production if labour costs rise or regulatory standards are strengthened, constraining the policy options available to governments.
sentences.native: La capacidad del capital para moverse a través de las fronteras con mucha más libertad que el trabajo crea una asimetría estructural: las corporaciones pueden amenazar de manera creíble con deslocalizar la producción si los costos laborales aumentan o se fortalecen los estándares regulatorios, restringiendo las opciones de política disponibles para los gobiernos.
sentences.en: Capital's ability to move across borders far more freely than labour creates a structural asymmetry: corporations can credibly threaten to offshore production if labour costs rise or regulatory standards are strengthened, constraining the policy options available to governments.
sentences.es: La capacidad del capital para moverse a través de las fronteras con mucha más libertad que el trabajo crea una asimetría estructural: las corporaciones pueden amenazar de manera creíble con deslocalizar la producción si los costos laborales aumentan o se fortalecen los estándares regulatorios, restringiendo las opciones de política disponibles para los gobiernos.

sentences.target: The political backlash against globalisation in many advanced economies reflects genuine grievances that mainstream economic policy failed to address: the distributional consequences of trade, the erosion of community economic foundations, and the sense of loss of control over one's economic destiny.
sentences.native: El rechazo político a la globalización en muchas economías avanzadas refleja agravios genuinos que la política económica convencional no abordó: las consecuencias distributivas del comercio, la erosión de los fundamentos económicos comunitarios y la sensación de pérdida de control sobre el propio destino económico.
sentences.en: The political backlash against globalisation in many advanced economies reflects genuine grievances that mainstream economic policy failed to address: the distributional consequences of trade, the erosion of community economic foundations, and the sense of loss of control over one's economic destiny.
sentences.es: El rechazo político a la globalización en muchas economías avanzadas refleja agravios genuinos que la política económica convencional no abordó: las consecuencias distributivas del comercio, la erosión de los fundamentos económicos comunitarios y la sensación de pérdida de control sobre el propio destino económico.

questions.q: What does the speaker identify as globalisation's central paradox?
options: It benefits developing nations economically while undermining their cultural identity
It creates growth and reduces extreme poverty while generating inequality within developed nations
It increases trade volumes while simultaneously reducing the number of trading nations
It empowers multinational corporations while weakening smaller domestic businesses
questions.answer: It creates growth and reduces extreme poverty while generating inequality within developed nations

questions.q: What structural asymmetry does the speaker identify?
options: Developed nations benefit more from trade agreements than developing ones
Capital can move across borders far more freely than labour
Large corporations receive regulatory advantages over smaller domestic firms
Export-oriented workers earn significantly more than those in service industries
questions.answer: Capital can move across borders far more freely than labour

questions.q: According to the speaker, what does the political backlash against globalisation reflect?
options: Protectionist ideology promoted by industries that cannot compete internationally
Irrational fears about immigration and cultural change driven by populist politicians
Genuine grievances about distributional consequences that mainstream policy failed to address
A preference for national sovereignty over international cooperation on economic issues
questions.answer: Genuine grievances about distributional consequences that mainstream policy failed to address

sentences.target: Just-in-time supply chain management — delivering components precisely when needed, with minimal inventory — maximises efficiency in stable conditions but creates catastrophic vulnerability when disruptions occur, as the COVID-19 pandemic vividly demonstrated.
sentences.native: La gestión de la cadena de suministro justo a tiempo, entregar componentes precisamente cuando se necesitan con inventario mínimo, maximiza la eficiencia en condiciones estables pero crea una vulnerabilidad catastrófica cuando ocurren disrupciones, como la pandemia de COVID-19 demostró vividamente.
sentences.en: Just-in-time supply chain management — delivering components precisely when needed, with minimal inventory — maximises efficiency in stable conditions but creates catastrophic vulnerability when disruptions occur, as the COVID-19 pandemic vividly demonstrated.
sentences.es: La gestión de la cadena de suministro justo a tiempo, entregar componentes precisamente cuando se necesitan con inventario mínimo, maximiza la eficiencia en condiciones estables pero crea una vulnerabilidad catastrófica cuando ocurren disrupciones, como la pandemia de COVID-19 demostró vividamente.

sentences.target: The concentration of production of critical goods — semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, rare earth minerals — in a small number of countries has created strategic dependencies that increasingly blur the boundary between economics and national security.
sentences.native: La concentración de la producción de bienes críticos, semiconductores, productos farmacéuticos y minerales de tierras raras, en un pequeño número de países ha creado dependencias estratégicas que cada vez más difuminan la frontera entre la economía y la seguridad nacional.
sentences.en: The concentration of production of critical goods — semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, rare earth minerals — in a small number of countries has created strategic dependencies that increasingly blur the boundary between economics and national security.
sentences.es: La concentración de la producción de bienes críticos, semiconductores, productos farmacéuticos y minerales de tierras raras, en un pequeño número de países ha creado dependencias estratégicas que cada vez más difuminan la frontera entre la economía y la seguridad nacional.

sentences.target: Reshoring and nearshoring — returning production to the home country or neighbouring nations — offer resilience benefits but at significant cost: higher wages, regulatory compliance expenses, and the loss of specialisation gains from global division of labour.
sentences.native: La relocalización y la deslocalización cercana, devolver la producción al país de origen o naciones vecinas, ofrecen beneficios de resiliencia pero a un costo significativo: salarios más altos, gastos de cumplimiento normativo y la pérdida de las ganancias de especialización de la división global del trabajo.
sentences.en: Reshoring and nearshoring — returning production to the home country or neighbouring nations — offer resilience benefits but at significant cost: higher wages, regulatory compliance expenses, and the loss of specialisation gains from global division of labour.
sentences.es: La relocalización y la deslocalización cercana, devolver la producción al país de origen o naciones vecinas, ofrecen beneficios de resiliencia pero a un costo significativo: salarios más altos, gastos de cumplimiento normativo y la pérdida de las ganancias de especialización de la división global del trabajo.

sentences.target: Remittances — money sent by migrants to their home countries — represent a form of supply chain in human capital: individuals export their labour to higher-wage economies and transfer a share of their earnings to sustain families and communities at home.
sentences.native: Las remesas, el dinero enviado por migrantes a sus países de origen, representan una forma de cadena de suministro en capital humano: los individuos exportan su trabajo a economías de salarios más altos y transfieren una parte de sus ganancias para sostener a sus familias y comunidades en casa.
sentences.en: Remittances — money sent by migrants to their home countries — represent a form of supply chain in human capital: individuals export their labour to higher-wage economies and transfer a share of their earnings to sustain families and communities at home.
sentences.es: Las remesas, el dinero enviado por migrantes a sus países de origen, representan una forma de cadena de suministro en capital humano: los individuos exportan su trabajo a economías de salarios más altos y transfieren una parte de sus ganancias para sostener a sus familias y comunidades en casa.

sentences.target: Building more resilient supply chains requires accepting some reduction in efficiency — maintaining buffer stocks, diversifying suppliers, investing in domestic capacity — a trade-off that pure market logic resists but which strategic and humanitarian considerations increasingly demand.
sentences.native: Construir cadenas de suministro más resilientes requiere aceptar alguna reducción en la eficiencia, mantener inventarios de amortiguación, diversificar proveedores e invertir en capacidad doméstica, una compensación que la lógica puramente de mercado resiste pero que las consideraciones estratégicas y humanitarias exigen cada vez más.
sentences.en: Building more resilient supply chains requires accepting some reduction in efficiency — maintaining buffer stocks, diversifying suppliers, investing in domestic capacity — a trade-off that pure market logic resists but which strategic and humanitarian considerations increasingly demand.
sentences.es: Construir cadenas de suministro más resilientes requiere aceptar alguna reducción en la eficiencia, mantener inventarios de amortiguación, diversificar proveedores e invertir en capacidad doméstica, una compensación que la lógica puramente de mercado resiste pero que las consideraciones estratégicas y humanitarias exigen cada vez más.

questions.q: What fundamental tension does the speaker identify in just-in-time supply chain management?
options: It reduces costs for corporations while increasing prices for consumers
It maximises efficiency in stable conditions but creates catastrophic vulnerability to disruption
It benefits large corporations while undermining smaller suppliers and subcontractors
It optimises short-term profitability at the expense of long-term technological development
questions.answer: It maximises efficiency in stable conditions but creates catastrophic vulnerability to disruption

questions.q: What economic-security boundary does the speaker say is increasingly blurred?
options: Between fiscal policy and monetary policy in managing inflation
Between domestic regulation and international trade law
Between the concentration of critical goods production and national security
Between corporate governance standards and geopolitical risk management
questions.answer: Between the concentration of critical goods production and national security

questions.q: How does the speaker describe remittances in terms of supply chain logic?
options: As a form of foreign direct investment that builds long-term productive capacity
As a supply chain in human capital where labour is exported and earnings transferred home
As a mechanism that reduces inequality by redistributing global economic gains
As a financial flow that bypasses formal banking systems and evades regulation
questions.answer: As a supply chain in human capital where labour is exported and earnings transferred home

sentences.target: The International Monetary Fund, the World Bank, and the World Trade Organisation were designed in the mid-twentieth century to manage an international economy very different from today's: smaller, less financially integrated, and dominated by fewer state actors.
sentences.native: El Fondo Monetario Internacional, el Banco Mundial y la Organización Mundial del Comercio fueron diseñados a mediados del siglo XX para gestionar una economía internacional muy diferente a la actual: más pequeña, menos financieramente integrada y dominada por menos actores estatales.
sentences.en: The International Monetary Fund, the World Bank, and the World Trade Organisation were designed in the mid-twentieth century to manage an international economy very different from today's: smaller, less financially integrated, and dominated by fewer state actors.
sentences.es: El Fondo Monetario Internacional, el Banco Mundial y la Organización Mundial del Comercio fueron diseñados a mediados del siglo XX para gestionar una economía internacional muy diferente a la actual: más pequeña, menos financieramente integrada y dominada por menos actores estatales.

sentences.target: Conditionality — the requirement that borrowing governments implement structural reforms as a condition of receiving IMF or World Bank assistance — has been deeply controversial, with critics arguing it imposes ideological prescriptions that serve creditor interests over debtor welfare.
sentences.native: La condicionalidad, el requisito de que los gobiernos deudores implementen reformas estructurales como condición para recibir asistencia del FMI o el Banco Mundial, ha sido profundamente controvertida, con críticos que argumentan que impone prescripciones ideológicas que sirven a los intereses de los acreedores sobre el bienestar de los deudores.
sentences.en: Conditionality — the requirement that borrowing governments implement structural reforms as a condition of receiving IMF or World Bank assistance — has been deeply controversial, with critics arguing it imposes ideological prescriptions that serve creditor interests over debtor welfare.
sentences.es: La condicionalidad, el requisito de que los gobiernos deudores implementen reformas estructurales como condición para recibir asistencia del FMI o el Banco Mundial, ha sido profundamente controvertida, con críticos que argumentan que impone prescripciones ideológicas que sirven a los intereses de los acreedores sobre el bienestar de los deudores.

sentences.target: The rise of China's Belt and Road Initiative as an alternative source of development finance has challenged the Western-dominated institutions' monopoly on infrastructure lending, giving developing nations new leverage — and new risks — in negotiating with established lenders.
sentences.native: El surgimiento de la Iniciativa del Cinturón y la Ruta de China como fuente alternativa de financiamiento para el desarrollo ha desafiado el monopolio de las instituciones dominadas por Occidente en préstamos para infraestructura, dando a las naciones en desarrollo nuevo apalancamiento y nuevos riesgos en las negociaciones con los prestamistas establecidos.
sentences.en: The rise of China's Belt and Road Initiative as an alternative source of development finance has challenged the Western-dominated institutions' monopoly on infrastructure lending, giving developing nations new leverage — and new risks — in negotiating with established lenders.
sentences.es: El surgimiento de la Iniciativa del Cinturón y la Ruta de China como fuente alternativa de financiamiento para el desarrollo ha desafiado el monopolio de las instituciones dominadas por Occidente en préstamos para infraestructura, dando a las naciones en desarrollo nuevo apalancamiento y nuevos riesgos en las negociaciones con los prestamistas establecidos.

sentences.target: Global tax governance — establishing minimum corporate tax rates, combating profit shifting to tax havens, and ensuring that digital companies pay taxes where they generate value — represents one of the most politically complex governance challenges of the era.
sentences.native: La gobernanza fiscal global, establecer tasas impositivas corporativas mínimas, combatir el traslado de ganancias a paraísos fiscales y garantizar que las empresas digitales paguen impuestos donde generan valor, representa uno de los desafíos de gobernanza políticamente más complejos de la era.
sentences.en: Global tax governance — establishing minimum corporate tax rates, combating profit shifting to tax havens, and ensuring that digital companies pay taxes where they generate value — represents one of the most politically complex governance challenges of the era.
sentences.es: La gobernanza fiscal global, establecer tasas impositivas corporativas mínimas, combatir el traslado de ganancias a paraísos fiscales y garantizar que las empresas digitales paguen impuestos donde generan valor, representa uno de los desafíos de gobernanza políticamente más complejos de la era.

sentences.target: Effective global economic governance requires not just technical rules but political legitimacy: institutions whose membership, voting rights, and leadership reflect the current distribution of global economic power rather than the hierarchy that existed in 1945.
sentences.native: La gobernanza económica global efectiva requiere no solo reglas técnicas sino legitimidad política: instituciones cuya membresía, derechos de voto y liderazgo reflejen la distribución actual del poder económico global en lugar de la jerarquía que existía en 1945.
sentences.en: Effective global economic governance requires not just technical rules but political legitimacy: institutions whose membership, voting rights, and leadership reflect the current distribution of global economic power rather than the hierarchy that existed in 1945.
sentences.es: La gobernanza económica global efectiva requiere no solo reglas técnicas sino legitimidad política: instituciones cuya membresía, derechos de voto y liderazgo reflejen la distribución actual del poder económico global en lugar de la jerarquía que existía en 1945.

questions.q: What criticism does the speaker raise about IMF and World Bank conditionality?
options: It requires reforms that are too slow to implement given borrowing countries' short-term fiscal needs
It imposes ideological prescriptions that serve creditor interests over debtor welfare
It gives too much flexibility to borrowing governments to evade necessary fiscal adjustments
It prioritises social spending programmes over the structural reforms needed for growth
questions.answer: It imposes ideological prescriptions that serve creditor interests over debtor welfare

questions.q: What effect has China's Belt and Road Initiative had on global development finance?
options: It has replaced Western-dominated institutions as the primary source of development lending worldwide
It has led Western institutions to reduce conditionality requirements on their loans
It has given developing nations new leverage in negotiations with established lenders while introducing new risks
It has focused exclusively on infrastructure finance while avoiding social sector investments
questions.answer: It has given developing nations new leverage in negotiations with established lenders while introducing new risks

questions.q: What does the speaker say effective global economic governance requires beyond technical rules?
options: Military enforcement mechanisms to ensure compliance with trade and financial agreements
Political legitimacy from institutions reflecting the current distribution of global economic power
Annual renegotiation of rules to adapt to rapidly changing economic conditions
Universal membership with equal voting rights regardless of each nation's economic size
questions.answer: Political legitimacy from institutions reflecting the current distribution of global economic power

sentences.target: Ethos is the rhetorical appeal to credibility: a speaker who demonstrates expertise, integrity, and genuine concern for the audience's interests has already secured a significant persuasive advantage before advancing a single argument.
sentences.native: El ethos es el recurso retórico a la credibilidad: un orador que demuestra experiencia, integridad y genuina preocupación por los intereses del público ya ha asegurado una ventaja persuasiva significativa antes de avanzar un solo argumento.
sentences.en: Ethos is the rhetorical appeal to credibility: a speaker who demonstrates expertise, integrity, and genuine concern for the audience's interests has already secured a significant persuasive advantage before advancing a single argument.
sentences.es: El ethos es el recurso retórico a la credibilidad: un orador que demuestra experiencia, integridad y genuina preocupación por los intereses del público ya ha asegurado una ventaja persuasiva significativa antes de avanzar un solo argumento.

sentences.target: Credibility is not static but constructed in the moment of speaking: tone, vocabulary choice, the acknowledgement of complexity, and the willingness to concede valid counter-arguments all signal whether the speaker can be trusted.
sentences.native: La credibilidad no es estática sino que se construye en el momento de hablar: el tono, la elección de vocabulario, el reconocimiento de la complejidad y la disposición a conceder contraargumentos válidos señalan si el orador puede ser de confianza.
sentences.en: Credibility is not static but constructed in the moment of speaking: tone, vocabulary choice, the acknowledgement of complexity, and the willingness to concede valid counter-arguments all signal whether the speaker can be trusted.
sentences.es: La credibilidad no es estática sino que se construye en el momento de hablar: el tono, la elección de vocabulario, el reconocimiento de la complejidad y la disposición a conceder contraargumentos válidos señalan si el orador puede ser de confianza.

sentences.target: An expert who speaks condescendingly destroys ethos more efficiently than a non-expert who speaks with humility: audiences forgive ignorance far more readily than arrogance.
sentences.native: Un experto que habla condescendientemente destruye el ethos más eficientemente que un no experto que habla con humildad: los públicos perdonan la ignorancia con mucha más facilidad que la arrogancia.
sentences.en: An expert who speaks condescendingly destroys ethos more efficiently than a non-expert who speaks with humility: audiences forgive ignorance far more readily than arrogance.
sentences.es: Un experto que habla condescendientemente destruye el ethos más eficientemente que un no experto que habla con humildad: los públicos perdonan la ignorancia con mucha más facilidad que la arrogancia.

sentences.target: In the digital age, ethos must be established rapidly and across multiple channels simultaneously: the speaker whose online profile contradicts their public persona suffers a credibility gap that no amount of eloquence can bridge.
sentences.native: En la era digital, el ethos debe establecerse rápidamente y a través de múltiples canales simultáneamente: el orador cuyo perfil en línea contradice su persona pública sufre una brecha de credibilidad que ninguna cantidad de elocuencia puede cerrar.
sentences.en: In the digital age, ethos must be established rapidly and across multiple channels simultaneously: the speaker whose online profile contradicts their public persona suffers a credibility gap that no amount of eloquence can bridge.
sentences.es: En la era digital, el ethos debe establecerse rápidamente y a través de múltiples canales simultáneamente: el orador cuyo perfil en línea contradice su persona pública sufre una brecha de credibilidad que ninguna cantidad de elocuencia puede cerrar.

sentences.target: The deepest form of ethos is consistency over time: a speaker who has defended unpopular positions when convenient positions were available, and has been proved right, accumulates a credibility reserve that can sustain them through periods of doubt.
sentences.native: La forma más profunda de ethos es la consistencia a lo largo del tiempo: un orador que ha defendido posiciones impopulares cuando estaban disponibles posiciones convenientes y ha demostrado tener razón acumula una reserva de credibilidad que puede sostenerlos durante períodos de duda.
sentences.en: The deepest form of ethos is consistency over time: a speaker who has defended unpopular positions when convenient positions were available, and has been proved right, accumulates a credibility reserve that can sustain them through periods of doubt.
sentences.es: La forma más profunda de ethos es la consistencia a lo largo del tiempo: un orador que ha defendido posiciones impopulares cuando estaban disponibles posiciones convenientes y ha demostrado tener razón acumula una reserva de credibilidad que puede sostenerlos durante períodos de duda.

questions.q: What does the speaker say about the relationship between expertise and ethos?
options: Expertise always guarantees high ethos regardless of communication style
An expert who speaks condescendingly can destroy ethos more than a humble non-expert
Ethos is primarily determined by professional qualifications and academic credentials
Expert speakers automatically receive more trust than non-experts in all contexts
questions.answer: An expert who speaks condescendingly can destroy ethos more than a humble non-expert

questions.q: How does the speaker define the deepest form of ethos?
options: The ability to adapt one's message to different audiences and contexts
Consistency over time, especially defending unpopular positions that prove correct
The combination of formal credentials with clear and accessible communication
The strategic use of personal stories to humanise abstract arguments
questions.answer: Consistency over time, especially defending unpopular positions that prove correct

questions.q: What challenge does the digital age pose for ethos according to the speaker?
options: It requires speakers to master multiple technical platforms simultaneously
Online profiles that contradict the public persona create an unbridgeable credibility gap
Digital audiences are more sceptical and require more evidence than traditional ones
The speed of digital communication prevents the careful construction of credibility
questions.answer: Online profiles that contradict the public persona create an unbridgeable credibility gap

audios.title: Logos and the Structure of Argument

sentences.target: Logos — the appeal to reason — requires not just accurate information but a structure that makes the relationship between premises and conclusions clear: an audience cannot be persuaded by logic they cannot follow.
sentences.native: El logos, el recurso a la razón, requiere no solo información precisa sino una estructura que haga clara la relación entre premisas y conclusiones: un público no puede ser persuadido por una lógica que no puede seguir.
sentences.en: Logos — the appeal to reason — requires not just accurate information but a structure that makes the relationship between premises and conclusions clear: an audience cannot be persuaded by logic they cannot follow.
