sentences.es: La trama no es lo mismo que la historia: la historia es la secuencia cronológica de eventos, mientras que la trama es su disposición, la selección de qué eventos mostrar, en qué orden y desde la perspectiva de quién, un conjunto de elecciones que determina el significado que produce la narrativa.

sentences.target: In medias res — beginning a narrative in the middle of the action and establishing context retrospectively — creates immediate engagement at the cost of initial disorientation: the reader must hold uncertainty until the backstory resolves it.
sentences.native: In medias res, comenzar una narrativa en medio de la acción y establecer el contexto retrospectivamente, crea un compromiso inmediato a costa de la desorientación inicial: el lector debe sostener la incertidumbre hasta que la historia de fondo la resuelva.
sentences.en: In medias res — beginning a narrative in the middle of the action and establishing context retrospectively — creates immediate engagement at the cost of initial disorientation: the reader must hold uncertainty until the backstory resolves it.
sentences.es: In medias res, comenzar una narrativa en medio de la acción y establecer el contexto retrospectivamente, crea un compromiso inmediato a costa de la desorientación inicial: el lector debe sostener la incertidumbre hasta que la historia de fondo la resuelva.

sentences.target: The denouement reveals retrospective meaning: events that seemed coincidental or contingent during the narrative become, after the ending, legible as the necessary expression of character, theme, or fateful logic that the story has been tracing all along.
sentences.native: El desenlace revela el significado retrospectivo: los eventos que parecían coincidentales o contingentes durante la narrativa se vuelven, después del final, legibles como la expresión necesaria del carácter, el tema o la lógica fatal que la historia ha estado trazando todo el tiempo.
sentences.en: The denouement reveals retrospective meaning: events that seemed coincidental or contingent during the narrative become, after the ending, legible as the necessary expression of character, theme, or fateful logic that the story has been tracing all along.
sentences.es: El desenlace revela el significado retrospectivo: los eventos que parecían coincidentales o contingentes durante la narrativa se vuelven, después del final, legibles como la expresión necesaria del carácter, el tema o la lógica fatal que la historia ha estado trazando todo el tiempo.

sentences.target: Subplot is not decoration but structural argument: a well-designed subplot mirrors, contrasts with, or complicates the main plot in ways that deepen the thematic meaning rather than simply adding more events for the reader to follow.
sentences.native: La subtrama no es decoración sino argumento estructural: una subtrama bien diseñada refleja, contrasta con o complica la trama principal de maneras que profundizan el significado temático en lugar de simplemente agregar más eventos para que el lector siga.
sentences.en: Subplot is not decoration but structural argument: a well-designed subplot mirrors, contrasts with, or complicates the main plot in ways that deepen the thematic meaning rather than simply adding more events for the reader to follow.
sentences.es: La subtrama no es decoración sino argumento estructural: una subtrama bien diseñada refleja, contrasta con o complica la trama principal de maneras que profundizan el significado temático en lugar de simplemente agregar más eventos para que el lector siga.

sentences.target: Non-linear narrative — disrupting chronological sequence through flashback, flash-forward, or parallel timelines — is not arbitrary complexity but a formal statement: the disrupted chronology enacts the text's claim that experience is not linear, that cause and effect are more complex than temporal sequence suggests.
sentences.native: La narrativa no lineal, interrumpir la secuencia cronológica mediante flashbacks, flash-forwards o líneas de tiempo paralelas, no es complejidad arbitraria sino una declaración formal: la cronología interrumpida representa la afirmación del texto de que la experiencia no es lineal, que la causa y el efecto son más complejos de lo que sugiere la secuencia temporal.
sentences.en: Non-linear narrative — disrupting chronological sequence through flashback, flash-forward, or parallel timelines — is not arbitrary complexity but a formal statement: the disrupted chronology enacts the text's claim that experience is not linear, that cause and effect are more complex than temporal sequence suggests.
sentences.es: La narrativa no lineal, interrumpir la secuencia cronológica mediante flashbacks, flash-forwards o líneas de tiempo paralelas, no es complejidad arbitraria sino una declaración formal: la cronología interrumpida representa la afirmación del texto de que la experiencia no es lineal, que la causa y el efecto son más complejos de lo que sugiere la secuencia temporal.

questions.q: How does the speaker distinguish plot from story?
options: Story is what actually happened; plot is the narrator's interpretation of those events
Story is the chronological sequence of events; plot is their arrangement — selection, order, and perspective
Plot is the main narrative line; story encompasses plot plus subplot and backstory
Story is the readers' experience of events in real time; plot is the author's retrospective design
questions.answer: Story is the chronological sequence of events; plot is their arrangement — selection, order, and perspective

questions.q: What is the speaker's view of subplot in relation to main plot?
options: Subplot is generally a sign of narrative excess that weakens the main plot's coherence and focus
It is structural argument — mirroring, contrasting with, or complicating the main plot to deepen thematic meaning
Subplot serves primarily to develop secondary characters and expand the narrative world
It provides pacing relief from the main plot's tension and gives readers time to process key developments
questions.answer: It is structural argument — mirroring, contrasting with, or complicating the main plot to deepen thematic meaning

questions.q: What does the speaker say non-linear narrative formally enacts?
options: The author's freedom from the constraints of realist convention and chronological causality
A formal statement that experience is non-linear and that cause and effect are more complex than temporal sequence suggests
The fragmented consciousness of a narrator who is unreliable or psychologically damaged
The postmodern position that narrative is always artifice and that chronology is itself a form of ideology
questions.answer: A formal statement that experience is non-linear and that cause and effect are more complex than temporal sequence suggests

sentences.target: Genre conventions are the shared expectations that readers bring to a text based on its classification: the detective novel promises resolution, the romance promises coupling, the tragedy promises loss — and these promises create the framework within which meaning is produced.
sentences.native: Las convenciones de género son las expectativas compartidas que los lectores traen a un texto basadas en su clasificación: la novela de detectives promete resolución, el romance promete unión, la tragedia promete pérdida, y estas promesas crean el marco dentro del cual se produce el significado.
sentences.en: Genre conventions are the shared expectations that readers bring to a text based on its classification: the detective novel promises resolution, the romance promises coupling, the tragedy promises loss — and these promises create the framework within which meaning is produced.
sentences.es: Las convenciones de género son las expectativas compartidas que los lectores traen a un texto basadas en su clasificación: la novela de detectives promete resolución, el romance promete unión, la tragedia promete pérdida, y estas promesas crean el marco dentro del cual se produce el significado.

sentences.target: A writer who subverts genre conventions is only intelligible against the background of those conventions: the detective novel that withholds resolution, the romance that ends in separation — these are meaningful precisely because they violate what genre has trained the reader to expect.
sentences.native: Un escritor que subvierte las convenciones de género solo es inteligible contra el fondo de esas convenciones: la novela de detectives que no proporciona resolución, el romance que termina en separación, son significativos precisamente porque violan lo que el género ha entrenado al lector a esperar.
sentences.en: A writer who subverts genre conventions is only intelligible against the background of those conventions: the detective novel that withholds resolution, the romance that ends in separation — these are meaningful precisely because they violate what genre has trained the reader to expect.
sentences.es: Un escritor que subvierte las convenciones de género solo es inteligible contra el fondo de esas convenciones: la novela de detectives que no proporciona resolución, el romance que termina en separación, son significativos precisamente porque violan lo que el género ha entrenado al lector a esperar.

sentences.target: The Gothic literary tradition uses the supernatural — or the suggestion of the supernatural — not primarily to frighten but to externalise psychological and social anxieties that realistic fiction lacks the formal resources to represent directly.
sentences.native: La tradición literaria gótica usa lo sobrenatural, o la sugerencia de lo sobrenatural, no principalmente para atemorizar sino para externalizar las ansiedades psicológicas y sociales que la ficción realista carece de los recursos formales para representar directamente.
sentences.en: The Gothic literary tradition uses the supernatural — or the suggestion of the supernatural — not primarily to frighten but to externalise psychological and social anxieties that realistic fiction lacks the formal resources to represent directly.
sentences.es: La tradición literaria gótica usa lo sobrenatural, o la sugerencia de lo sobrenatural, no principalmente para atemorizar sino para externalizar las ansiedades psicológicas y sociales que la ficción realista carece de los recursos formales para representar directamente.

sentences.target: Magic realism — treating the fantastical with the same matter-of-fact narration as the mundane — achieves its distinctive effect by refusing to adjudicate between natural and supernatural explanations, leaving both available and leaving the reader without a stable position from which to evaluate events.
sentences.native: El realismo mágico, tratar lo fantástico con la misma narración de hecho que lo mundano, logra su efecto distintivo al negarse a adjudicar entre explicaciones naturales y sobrenaturales, dejando ambas disponibles y dejando al lector sin una posición estable desde la cual evaluar los eventos.
sentences.en: Magic realism — treating the fantastical with the same matter-of-fact narration as the mundane — achieves its distinctive effect by refusing to adjudicate between natural and supernatural explanations, leaving both available and leaving the reader without a stable position from which to evaluate events.
sentences.es: El realismo mágico, tratar lo fantástico con la misma narración de hecho que lo mundano, logra su efecto distintivo al negarse a adjudicar entre explicaciones naturales y sobrenaturales, dejando ambas disponibles y dejando al lector sin una posición estable desde la cual evaluar los eventos.

sentences.target: Postmodern fiction makes its own artificiality visible — through metafiction, narrative intrusion, or the deliberate foregrounding of genre conventions — as a form of epistemological honesty: all fiction is construction, and the postmodern text refuses to pretend otherwise.
sentences.native: La ficción posmoderna hace visible su propia artificialidad, a través de la metaficción, la intrusión narrativa o el primer plano deliberado de las convenciones de género, como una forma de honestidad epistemológica: toda ficción es construcción, y el texto posmoderno se niega a fingir lo contrario.
sentences.en: Postmodern fiction makes its own artificiality visible — through metafiction, narrative intrusion, or the deliberate foregrounding of genre conventions — as a form of epistemological honesty: all fiction is construction, and the postmodern text refuses to pretend otherwise.
sentences.es: La ficción posmoderna hace visible su propia artificialidad, a través de la metaficción, la intrusión narrativa o el primer plano deliberado de las convenciones de género, como una forma de honestidad epistemológica: toda ficción es construcción, y el texto posmoderno se niega a fingir lo contrario.

questions.q: Why does the speaker say genre subversion is only intelligible against genre conventions?
options: Because readers need to know the genre rules before they can appreciate how skillfully a writer has followed them
Because subversion is meaningful only as a violation of what genre has trained the reader to expect
Because subverted genres always eventually return to their conventions in the resolution
Because genre subversion is primarily a commercial strategy to attract readers from multiple genre audiences
questions.answer: Because subversion is meaningful only as a violation of what genre has trained the reader to expect

questions.q: What does the speaker say the Gothic tradition uses the supernatural to do?
options: To create suspense and horror by making the familiar strange and threatening
To externalise psychological and social anxieties that realistic fiction lacks the resources to represent directly
To explore philosophical questions about the nature of reality and perception
To provide a stylised distance from contemporary reality that allows political critique
questions.answer: To externalise psychological and social anxieties that realistic fiction lacks the resources to represent directly

questions.q: How does the speaker characterise postmodern fiction's foregrounding of its own artificiality?
options: As a self-indulgent technique that prioritises formal experimentation over narrative engagement
As a form of epistemological honesty — all fiction is construction and postmodern texts refuse to pretend otherwise
As a commercial strategy that appeals to academics while alienating general readers
As an extension of the modernist project of formal innovation into new narrative territories
questions.answer: As a form of epistemological honesty — all fiction is construction and postmodern texts refuse to pretend otherwise

sentences.target: Literary criticism is not the discovery of a single correct meaning hidden in the text but the production of readings: different critical frameworks illuminate different dimensions of the same text, and no single framework exhausts what a rich literary work has to offer.
sentences.native: La crítica literaria no es el descubrimiento de un único significado correcto oculto en el texto sino la producción de lecturas: diferentes marcos críticos iluminan diferentes dimensiones del mismo texto, y ningún marco único agota lo que una obra literaria rica tiene para ofrecer.
sentences.en: Literary criticism is not the discovery of a single correct meaning hidden in the text but the production of readings: different critical frameworks illuminate different dimensions of the same text, and no single framework exhausts what a rich literary work has to offer.
sentences.es: La crítica literaria no es el descubrimiento de un único significado correcto oculto en el texto sino la producción de lecturas: diferentes marcos críticos iluminan diferentes dimensiones del mismo texto, y ningún marco único agota lo que una obra literaria rica tiene para ofrecer.

sentences.target: Biographical criticism — reading a text as an expression of its author's life and psychology — offers one valid lens while risking the reduction of complex artistic achievement to personal symptom.
sentences.native: La crítica biográfica, leer un texto como expresión de la vida y psicología de su autor, ofrece una lente válida mientras se arriesga a reducir un complejo logro artístico a un síntoma personal.
sentences.en: Biographical criticism — reading a text as an expression of its author's life and psychology — offers one valid lens while risking the reduction of complex artistic achievement to personal symptom.
sentences.es: La crítica biográfica, leer un texto como expresión de la vida y psicología de su autor, ofrece una lente válida mientras se arriesga a reducir un complejo logro artístico a un síntoma personal.

sentences.target: New Criticism insisted on treating the text as a self-sufficient object to be read without reference to authorial intention, historical context, or reader response — a methodological strictness that produced valuable close readings but risked an ahistorical formalism.
sentences.native: La Nueva Crítica insistía en tratar el texto como un objeto autosuficiente que debía leerse sin referencia a la intención del autor, el contexto histórico o la respuesta del lector, un rigor metodológico que produjo valiosas lecturas minuciosas pero arriesgaba un formalismo ahistórico.
sentences.en: New Criticism insisted on treating the text as a self-sufficient object to be read without reference to authorial intention, historical context, or reader response — a methodological strictness that produced valuable close readings but risked an ahistorical formalism.
sentences.es: La Nueva Crítica insistía en tratar el texto como un objeto autosuficiente que debía leerse sin referencia a la intención del autor, el contexto histórico o la respuesta del lector, un rigor metodológico que produjo valiosas lecturas minuciosas pero arriesgaba un formalismo ahistórico.

sentences.target: Feminist literary criticism asks not just what texts say about women but what assumptions about gender they naturalise, which voices they silence, and how the category of literary value has been constructed to exclude or marginalise women's writing.
sentences.native: La crítica literaria feminista pregunta no solo qué dicen los textos sobre las mujeres sino qué suposiciones sobre el género naturalizan, qué voces silencian y cómo la categoría de valor literario ha sido construida para excluir o marginalizar la escritura de las mujeres.
sentences.en: Feminist literary criticism asks not just what texts say about women but what assumptions about gender they naturalise, which voices they silence, and how the category of literary value has been constructed to exclude or marginalise women's writing.
sentences.es: La crítica literaria feminista pregunta no solo qué dicen los textos sobre las mujeres sino qué suposiciones sobre el género naturalizan, qué voces silencian y cómo la categoría de valor literario ha sido construida para excluir o marginalizar la escritura de las mujeres.

sentences.target: The most productive critical reading is one that is theoretically informed without being theoretically imprisoned: the framework is a tool for seeing, not a formula for generating predetermined conclusions regardless of what the text actually does.
sentences.native: La lectura crítica más productiva es la que está informada teóricamente sin estar aprisionada teóricamente: el marco es una herramienta para ver, no una fórmula para generar conclusiones predeterminadas independientemente de lo que el texto realmente hace.
sentences.en: The most productive critical reading is one that is theoretically informed without being theoretically imprisoned: the framework is a tool for seeing, not a formula for generating predetermined conclusions regardless of what the text actually does.
sentences.es: La lectura crítica más productiva es la que está informada teóricamente sin estar aprisionada teóricamente: el marco es una herramienta para ver, no una fórmula para generar conclusiones predeterminadas independientemente de lo que el texto realmente hace.

questions.q: How does the speaker define literary criticism in contrast to discovering hidden meaning?
options: As the application of scientific methods to texts to identify their objective structural properties
As the production of readings — different frameworks illuminate different dimensions without any single one exhausting the text
As the collective judgment of expert readers about which texts have lasting artistic value
As the historical reconstruction of what texts meant to their original audiences and cultural contexts
questions.answer: As the production of readings — different frameworks illuminate different dimensions without any single one exhausting the text

questions.q: What risk does the speaker associate with biographical criticism?
options: That it requires biographical information that is often unreliable or disputed by scholars
The reduction of complex artistic achievement to personal symptom or psychological expression
That it privileges authors who lived colourful or dramatic lives over those with quieter biographies
That it makes it impossible to appreciate texts whose authors left little biographical record
questions.answer: The reduction of complex artistic achievement to personal symptom or psychological expression

questions.q: How does the speaker characterise the relationship between critical theory and reading?
options: Theory should precede reading so that the reader approaches the text with clear interpretive expectations
Theory is a tool for seeing, not a formula for predetermined conclusions regardless of what the text does
Advanced critical theory should replace close reading as the primary mode of literary analysis
Theory is most valuable when it reveals what previous readers have systematically misread in canonical texts
questions.answer: Theory is a tool for seeing, not a formula for predetermined conclusions regardless of what the text does

audios.title: Style, Diction, and the Author's Voice

sentences.target: Style is not how an author says something as opposed to what they say — it is part of the what: the specific choices made at every level of language constitute the meaning, not merely its vehicle.
sentences.native: El estilo no es cómo dice algo un autor en contraposición a qué dice, es parte del qué: las elecciones específicas realizadas en cada nivel del lenguaje constituyen el significado, no meramente su vehículo.
sentences.en: Style is not how an author says something as opposed to what they say — it is part of the what: the specific choices made at every level of language constitute the meaning, not merely its vehicle.
sentences.es: El estilo no es cómo dice algo un autor en contraposición a qué dice, es parte del qué: las elecciones específicas realizadas en cada nivel del lenguaje constituyen el significado, no meramente su vehículo.

sentences.target: Hemingway's iceberg theory — that the dignity of movement of an iceberg is due to only one-eighth of it being above water — describes a prose style that trusts suppression: the reader must supply the emotional weight that the text withholds from explicit statement.
sentences.native: La teoría del iceberg de Hemingway, que la dignidad de movimiento de un iceberg se debe a que solo una octava parte está sobre el agua, describe un estilo de prosa que confía en la supresión: el lector debe suministrar el peso emocional que el texto retiene de la declaración explícita.
sentences.en: Hemingway's iceberg theory — that the dignity of movement of an iceberg is due to only one-eighth of it being above water — describes a prose style that trusts suppression: the reader must supply the emotional weight that the text withholds from explicit statement.
sentences.es: La teoría del iceberg de Hemingway, que la dignidad de movimiento de un iceberg se debe a que solo una octava parte está sobre el agua, describe un estilo de prosa que confía en la supresión: el lector debe suministrar el peso emocional que el texto retiene de la declaración explícita.

sentences.target: Syntactic rhythm — the pattern of sentence lengths and structures — is as expressive as vocabulary: long, elaborately subordinated sentences create the experience of thought in process, while short declarative sentences create urgency, certainty, or the after-shock of revelation.
sentences.native: El ritmo sintáctico, el patrón de longitudes y estructuras de oraciones, es tan expresivo como el vocabulario: las oraciones largas y elaboradamente subordinadas crean la experiencia del pensamiento en proceso, mientras que las oraciones declarativas cortas crean urgencia, certeza o el shock posterior a la revelación.
sentences.en: Syntactic rhythm — the pattern of sentence lengths and structures — is as expressive as vocabulary: long, elaborately subordinated sentences create the experience of thought in process, while short declarative sentences create urgency, certainty, or the after-shock of revelation.
sentences.es: El ritmo sintáctico, el patrón de longitudes y estructuras de oraciones, es tan expresivo como el vocabulario: las oraciones largas y elaboradamente subordinadas crean la experiencia del pensamiento en proceso, mientras que las oraciones declarativas cortas crean urgencia, certeza o el shock posterior a la revelación.

sentences.target: Diction — the specific vocabulary chosen rather than the words that could have been chosen — is the most direct window into an author's aesthetic values: the writer who chooses 'gaunt' over 'thin', 'luminous' over 'bright', is making aesthetic and moral choices, not merely descriptive ones.
sentences.native: La dicción, el vocabulario específico elegido en lugar de las palabras que podrían haberse elegido, es la ventana más directa a los valores estéticos de un autor: el escritor que elige 'demacrado' sobre 'delgado', 'luminoso' sobre 'brillante', está tomando decisiones estéticas y morales, no meramente descriptivas.
sentences.en: Diction — the specific vocabulary chosen rather than the words that could have been chosen — is the most direct window into an author's aesthetic values: the writer who chooses 'gaunt' over 'thin', 'luminous' over 'bright', is making aesthetic and moral choices, not merely descriptive ones.
sentences.es: La dicción, el vocabulario específico elegido en lugar de las palabras que podrían haberse elegido, es la ventana más directa a los valores estéticos de un autor: el escritor que elige 'demacrado' sobre 'delgado', 'luminoso' sobre 'brillante', está tomando decisiones estéticas y morales, no meramente descriptivas.

sentences.target: Voice — the sense of a distinctive, consistent sensibility behind the words — is the most immediately recognisable and most difficult to analyse property of literary style: we know a writer's voice when we encounter it, but describing what produces that effect requires attention to every level of the text simultaneously.
sentences.native: La voz, el sentido de una sensibilidad distintiva y consistente detrás de las palabras, es la propiedad más inmediatamente reconocible y más difícil de analizar del estilo literario: conocemos la voz de un escritor cuando la encontramos, pero describir qué produce ese efecto requiere atención a cada nivel del texto simultáneamente.
sentences.en: Voice — the sense of a distinctive, consistent sensibility behind the words — is the most immediately recognisable and most difficult to analyse property of literary style: we know a writer's voice when we encounter it, but describing what produces that effect requires attention to every level of the text simultaneously.
sentences.es: La voz, el sentido de una sensibilidad distintiva y consistente detrás de las palabras, es la propiedad más inmediatamente reconocible y más difícil de analizar del estilo literario: conocemos la voz de un escritor cuando la encontramos, pero describir qué produce ese efecto requiere atención a cada nivel del texto simultáneamente.

questions.q: How does the speaker refute the idea that style is merely how something is said rather than what is said?
options: By arguing that style determines audience and therefore controls who can access a text's meaning
By asserting that specific language choices at every level constitute the meaning, not merely its vehicle
By showing that the same content in different styles produces texts of different commercial value
By demonstrating that stripped of style, literary texts reduce to the same philosophical content as non-literary ones
questions.answer: By asserting that specific language choices at every level constitute the meaning, not merely its vehicle

questions.q: What does Hemingway's iceberg theory describe according to the speaker?
options: A narrative structure where the most important plot events happen off-page and are reported rather than shown
A prose style that trusts suppression — the reader must supply the emotional weight that the text withholds
A minimalist approach to character description that focuses only on externally observable behaviour
The principle that the most powerful literary effects come from what is structurally central but textually absent
questions.answer: A prose style that trusts suppression — the reader must supply the emotional weight that the text withholds

questions.q: What does the speaker say makes syntactic rhythm expressive?
options: It creates aural patterns that activate the same pleasures as poetry even in prose
Long subordinated sentences create thought in process; short declarative sentences create urgency or post-revelation shock
It allows writers to vary pace in ways that guide reader attention to the most significant narrative moments
The contrast between sentence lengths creates emphasis by making the shorter sentences stand out against longer ones
questions.answer: Long subordinated sentences create thought in process; short declarative sentences create urgency or post-revelation shock

audios.title: Tragedy, Catharsis, and the Tragic Hero

sentences.target: The tragic hero is distinguished not by weakness but by a specific kind of greatness: an excellence of character — courage, intelligence, passion — that becomes, in particular circumstances, the very cause of their downfall.
sentences.native: El héroe trágico se distingue no por la debilidad sino por un tipo específico de grandeza: una excelencia de carácter, coraje, inteligencia, pasión, que se convierte, en circunstancias particulares, en la causa misma de su caída.
sentences.en: The tragic hero is distinguished not by weakness but by a specific kind of greatness: an excellence of character — courage, intelligence, passion — that becomes, in particular circumstances, the very cause of their downfall.
sentences.es: El héroe trágico se distingue no por la debilidad sino por un tipo específico de grandeza: una excelencia de carácter, coraje, inteligencia, pasión, que se convierte, en circunstancias particulares, en la causa misma de su caída.

sentences.target: Hamartia — the tragic flaw or error — is not a moral failing in the conventional sense but a quality that, combined with the particular pressures of the tragic situation, generates the series of choices that lead ineluctably to catastrophe.
sentences.native: La hamartia, el defecto o error trágico, no es un fracaso moral en el sentido convencional sino una cualidad que, combinada con las presiones particulares de la situación trágica, genera la serie de elecciones que conducen inexorablemente a la catástrofe.
sentences.en: Hamartia — the tragic flaw or error — is not a moral failing in the conventional sense but a quality that, combined with the particular pressures of the tragic situation, generates the series of choices that lead ineluctably to catastrophe.
sentences.es: La hamartia, el defecto o error trágico, no es un fracaso moral en el sentido convencional sino una cualidad que, combinada con las presiones particulares de la situación trágica, genera la serie de elecciones que conducen inexorablemente a la catástrofe.

sentences.target: Catharsis — the purging or clarification of pity and fear that Aristotle associated with tragedy — is not sentimental release but a clarifying experience: the controlled encounter with overwhelming emotion in the safety of the theatrical frame restores the audience's capacity for feeling rather than numbing it.
sentences.native: La catarsis, la purga o clarificación de la piedad y el miedo que Aristóteles asoció con la tragedia, no es liberación sentimental sino una experiencia clarificadora: el encuentro controlado con la emoción abrumadora en la seguridad del marco teatral restaura la capacidad del público para sentir en lugar de insensibilizarla.
sentences.en: Catharsis — the purging or clarification of pity and fear that Aristotle associated with tragedy — is not sentimental release but a clarifying experience: the controlled encounter with overwhelming emotion in the safety of the theatrical frame restores the audience's capacity for feeling rather than numbing it.
sentences.es: La catarsis, la purga o clarificación de la piedad y el miedo que Aristóteles asoció con la tragedia, no es liberación sentimental sino una experiencia clarificadora: el encuentro controlado con la emoción abrumadora en la seguridad del marco teatral restaura la capacidad del público para sentir en lugar de insensibilizarla.

sentences.target: The dramatic irony specific to tragedy creates an almost unbearable suspension: the audience, knowing the catastrophe that awaits, watches the protagonist approach it with terrible clarity, while the protagonist remains ignorant of what every action they take is bringing closer.
sentences.native: La ironía dramática específica de la tragedia crea una suspensión casi insoportable: el público, conociendo la catástrofe que espera, ve al protagonista acercarse a ella con terrible claridad, mientras el protagonista permanece ignorante de lo que cada acción que realiza está acercando.
sentences.en: The dramatic irony specific to tragedy creates an almost unbearable suspension: the audience, knowing the catastrophe that awaits, watches the protagonist approach it with terrible clarity, while the protagonist remains ignorant of what every action they take is bringing closer.
sentences.es: La ironía dramática específica de la tragedia crea una suspensión casi insoportable: el público, conociendo la catástrofe que espera, ve al protagonista acercarse a ella con terrible claridad, mientras el protagonista permanece ignorante de lo que cada acción que realiza está acercando.

sentences.target: Modern tragedy modifies the classical form: the hero need not be royal, the downfall need not be total, and the cosmic order need not be restored — what persists is the sense that the protagonist's suffering is not random but is bound to something essential about who they are.
sentences.native: La tragedia moderna modifica la forma clásica: el héroe no necesita ser real, la caída no necesita ser total y el orden cósmico no necesita ser restaurado, lo que persiste es el sentido de que el sufrimiento del protagonista no es aleatorio sino que está ligado a algo esencial sobre quiénes son.
sentences.en: Modern tragedy modifies the classical form: the hero need not be royal, the downfall need not be total, and the cosmic order need not be restored — what persists is the sense that the protagonist's suffering is not random but is bound to something essential about who they are.
sentences.es: La tragedia moderna modifica la forma clásica: el héroe no necesita ser real, la caída no necesita ser total y el orden cósmico no necesita ser restaurado, lo que persiste es el sentido de que el sufrimiento del protagonista no es aleatorio sino que está ligado a algo esencial sobre quiénes son.

questions.q: How does the speaker define hamartia in relation to conventional moral failing?
options: As a more severe form of moral weakness that makes the protagonist's punishment proportionate
As a quality that combined with particular pressures generates choices leading ineluctably to catastrophe rather than a simple moral flaw
As the moment of recognition when the protagonist understands the consequences of their earlier choices
As the hubris or overconfidence that leads the tragic hero to challenge forces beyond their control
questions.answer: As a quality that combined with particular pressures generates choices leading ineluctably to catastrophe rather than a simple moral flaw

questions.q: How does the speaker characterise Aristotle's concept of catharsis?
options: As the simple emotional release that explains why audiences enjoy watching suffering on stage
As a clarifying experience where controlled encounter with overwhelming emotion restores the capacity for feeling
As the moral lesson that tragedy teaches by showing the consequences of excessive ambition or pride
As the aesthetic pleasure of watching a perfectly constructed plot move inevitably toward its conclusion
questions.answer: As a clarifying experience where controlled encounter with overwhelming emotion restores the capacity for feeling

questions.q: What does the speaker identify as persisting in modern tragedy despite its departure from classical form?
options: The requirement that the protagonist belong to a social class whose fall affects the entire community
The sense that the protagonist's suffering is bound to something essential about who they are, not random
The use of dramatic irony to create suspense and the restoration of order in the denouement
The expectation that the tragic hero will achieve a moment of recognition before the final catastrophe
questions.answer: The sense that the protagonist's suffering is bound to something essential about who they are, not random

sentences.target: Literary satire attacks its targets through exaggeration, irony, and wit rather than direct assault: by making what is wrong ridiculous rather than merely condemnable, satire reaches audiences that earnest critique cannot and sustains engagement that anger alone cannot maintain.
sentences.native: La sátira literaria ataca sus objetivos a través de la exageración, la ironía y el ingenio en lugar del asalto directo: al hacer ridículo lo que está mal en lugar de meramente condenable, la sátira llega a públicos a los que la crítica seria no puede y sostiene el compromiso que la ira sola no puede mantener.
sentences.en: Literary satire attacks its targets through exaggeration, irony, and wit rather than direct assault: by making what is wrong ridiculous rather than merely condemnable, satire reaches audiences that earnest critique cannot and sustains engagement that anger alone cannot maintain.
sentences.es: La sátira literaria ataca sus objetivos a través de la exageración, la ironía y el ingenio en lugar del asalto directo: al hacer ridículo lo que está mal en lugar de meramente condenable, la sátira llega a públicos a los que la crítica seria no puede y sostiene el compromiso que la ira sola no puede mantener.

sentences.target: Horatian satire is gentle, urbane, and corrective: it gently ridicules human folly with the expectation that the ridicule will produce shame and improvement rather than outrage and retaliation.
sentences.native: La sátira horaciana es suave, urbana y correctiva: ridiculiza suavemente la locura humana con la expectativa de que el ridículo producirá vergüenza y mejora en lugar de indignación y represalia.
sentences.en: Horatian satire is gentle, urbane, and corrective: it gently ridicules human folly with the expectation that the ridicule will produce shame and improvement rather than outrage and retaliation.
sentences.es: La sátira horaciana es suave, urbana y correctiva: ridiculiza suavemente la locura humana con la expectativa de que el ridículo producirá vergüenza y mejora en lugar de indignación y represalia.

sentences.target: Juvenalian satire is savage, bitter, and contemptuous: it attacks not folly that can be corrected but vice that has corrupted institutions beyond reform, producing rage rather than the comfortable recognition of shared human weakness.
sentences.native: La sátira juvenaliana es salvaje, amarga y despectiva: ataca no la locura que puede corregirse sino el vicio que ha corrompido las instituciones más allá de la reforma, produciendo indignación en lugar del cómodo reconocimiento de la debilidad humana compartida.
sentences.en: Juvenalian satire is savage, bitter, and contemptuous: it attacks not folly that can be corrected but vice that has corrupted institutions beyond reform, producing rage rather than the comfortable recognition of shared human weakness.
sentences.es: La sátira juvenaliana es salvaje, amarga y despectiva: ataca no la locura que puede corregirse sino el vicio que ha corrompido las instituciones más allá de la reforma, produciendo indignación en lugar del cómodo reconocimiento de la debilidad humana compartida.

sentences.target: Swift's A Modest Proposal — calmly proposing that the Irish poor eat their children as a solution to poverty — demonstrates satire's most extreme technique: the maintained deadpan of a monstrous proposal is more devastating than any direct argument could be, because the horror emerges from the reader's own interpretive act.
sentences.native: La Modesta Propuesta de Swift, proponiendo calmamente que los pobres irlandeses coman a sus hijos como solución a la pobreza, demuestra la técnica más extrema de la sátira: el deadpan mantenido de una propuesta monstruosa es más devastador que cualquier argumento directo podría ser, porque el horror emerge del propio acto interpretativo del lector.
sentences.en: Swift's A Modest Proposal — calmly proposing that the Irish poor eat their children as a solution to poverty — demonstrates satire's most extreme technique: the maintained deadpan of a monstrous proposal is more devastating than any direct argument could be, because the horror emerges from the reader's own interpretive act.
sentences.es: La Modesta Propuesta de Swift, proponiendo calmamente que los pobres irlandeses coman a sus hijos como solución a la pobreza, demuestra la técnica más extrema de la sátira: el deadpan mantenido de una propuesta monstruosa es más devastador que cualquier argumento directo podría ser, porque el horror emerge del propio acto interpretativo del lector.

sentences.target: The satirist's dilemma is that their effectiveness depends on the continued existence of the targets they mock: if satire were truly corrective, it would eliminate the conditions that make it necessary, but the greatest satires are produced when those conditions are most entrenched.
sentences.native: El dilema del satirista es que su efectividad depende de la existencia continua de los objetivos que ridiculizan: si la sátira fuera verdaderamente correctiva, eliminaría las condiciones que la hacen necesaria, pero las mejores sátiras se producen cuando esas condiciones están más arraigadas.
sentences.en: The satirist's dilemma is that their effectiveness depends on the continued existence of the targets they mock: if satire were truly corrective, it would eliminate the conditions that make it necessary, but the greatest satires are produced when those conditions are most entrenched.
sentences.es: El dilema del satirista es que su efectividad depende de la existencia continua de los objetivos que ridiculizan: si la sátira fuera verdaderamente correctiva, eliminaría las condiciones que la hacen necesaria, pero las mejores sátiras se producen cuando esas condiciones están más arraigadas.

questions.q: How does the speaker distinguish Horatian from Juvenalian satire?
options: Horatian satire uses verse while Juvenalian satire uses prose as its primary medium
Horatian gently ridicules correctable folly while Juvenalian savagely attacks vice that has corrupted institutions beyond reform
Horatian satire targets individuals while Juvenalian targets institutions and political systems
Horatian satire is more modern while Juvenalian reflects classical Roman moral concerns
questions.answer: Horatian gently ridicules correctable folly while Juvenalian savagely attacks vice that has corrupted institutions beyond reform

questions.q: Why does the speaker say Swift's Modest Proposal is more devastating than direct argument?
options: Because Swift was a clergyman whose religious authority gave the proposal unexpected moral weight
Because the horror emerges from the reader's own interpretive act when they realise the implications of the deadpan tone
Because the proposal was briefly taken seriously by some readers, demonstrating the actual views it was mocking
Because the economic logic of the proposal is internally consistent in a way that makes it harder to dismiss
questions.answer: Because the horror emerges from the reader's own interpretive act when they realise the implications of the deadpan tone

questions.q: What paradox does the speaker identify about satire's relationship with its targets?
options: Satire's success in reaching popular audiences undermines its intellectual credibility with the elite it targets
The satirist's effectiveness depends on the targets' continued existence, but the greatest satires occur when conditions are most entrenched
Satire generates emotional engagement that prevents the rational reflection that actual political change requires
The more popular the satirist, the more likely their targets will respond, which amplifies the satire's reach unintentionally
questions.answer: The satirist's effectiveness depends on the targets' continued existence, but the greatest satires occur when conditions are most entrenched

audios.title: Reading Poetry: Form, Sound, and Meaning

sentences.target: In poetry, form and meaning are inseparable: the line break, the stanza division, the choice of metre or the refusal of metre — these are not containers for pre-existing meaning but part of what the poem means.
sentences.native: En la poesía, la forma y el significado son inseparables: el salto de línea, la división de la estrofa, la elección del metro o el rechazo del metro, no son contenedores de un significado preexistente sino parte de lo que el poema significa.
sentences.en: In poetry, form and meaning are inseparable: the line break, the stanza division, the choice of metre or the refusal of metre — these are not containers for pre-existing meaning but part of what the poem means.
sentences.es: En la poesía, la forma y el significado son inseparables: el salto de línea, la división de la estrofa, la elección del metro o el rechazo del metro, no son contenedores de un significado preexistente sino parte de lo que el poema significa.

sentences.target: The sonnet form carries centuries of convention: choosing to write in sonnets is always an act of self-positioning in relation to that tradition, whether the poet embraces, extends, revises, or deliberately breaks with what the form has historically promised.
sentences.native: La forma del soneto lleva siglos de convención: elegir escribir en sonetos es siempre un acto de autoposicionamiento en relación con esa tradición, ya sea que el poeta abrace, extienda, revise o rompa deliberadamente con lo que la forma ha prometido históricamente.
sentences.en: The sonnet form carries centuries of convention: choosing to write in sonnets is always an act of self-positioning in relation to that tradition, whether the poet embraces, extends, revises, or deliberately breaks with what the form has historically promised.
sentences.es: La forma del soneto lleva siglos de convención: elegir escribir en sonetos es siempre un acto de autoposicionamiento en relación con esa tradición, ya sea que el poeta abrace, extienda, revise o rompa deliberadamente con lo que la forma ha prometido históricamente.

sentences.target: Sound patterns — alliteration, assonance, consonance, and the phonetic texture of vowel and consonant combinations — are not merely musical decoration but semantic resource: harsh consonants and closed vowels create different meaning-effects than liquid consonants and open vowels.
sentences.native: Los patrones sonoros, la aliteración, la asonancia, la consonancia y la textura fonética de las combinaciones vocálicas y consonánticas, no son meramente decoración musical sino recurso semántico: las consonantes duras y las vocales cerradas crean diferentes efectos de significado que las consonantes líquidas y las vocales abiertas.
sentences.en: Sound patterns — alliteration, assonance, consonance, and the phonetic texture of vowel and consonant combinations — are not merely musical decoration but semantic resource: harsh consonants and closed vowels create different meaning-effects than liquid consonants and open vowels.
sentences.es: Los patrones sonoros, la aliteración, la asonancia, la consonancia y la textura fonética de las combinaciones vocálicas y consonánticas, no son meramente decoración musical sino recurso semántico: las consonantes duras y las vocales cerradas crean diferentes efectos de significado que las consonantes líquidas y las vocales abiertas.

sentences.target: The volta — the turn or shift in a poem's argument, typically occurring at the transition between octave and sestet in a sonnet — is the moment where the poem's thinking changes direction, complicates its initial claim, or arrives at a realisation that reframes what has come before.
sentences.native: La vuelta, el giro o cambio en el argumento de un poema, típicamente ocurriendo en la transición entre octava y sexteta en un soneto, es el momento donde el pensamiento del poema cambia de dirección, complica su afirmación inicial o llega a una comprensión que re-encuadra lo que ha venido antes.
sentences.en: The volta — the turn or shift in a poem's argument, typically occurring at the transition between octave and sestet in a sonnet — is the moment where the poem's thinking changes direction, complicates its initial claim, or arrives at a realisation that reframes what has come before.
sentences.es: La vuelta, el giro o cambio en el argumento de un poema, típicamente ocurriendo en la transición entre octava y sexteta en un soneto, es el momento donde el pensamiento del poema cambia de dirección, complica su afirmación inicial o llega a una comprensión que re-encuadra lo que ha venido antes.

sentences.target: Enjambment — allowing the sense to run over from one line to the next — creates productive tension between the syntactic unit and the line unit: the reader experiences the line break as a momentary pause that retrospectively becomes part of the meaning when the next line resolves or redirects it.
sentences.native: El encabalgamiento, permitir que el sentido se extienda de un verso al siguiente, crea una tensión productiva entre la unidad sintáctica y la unidad de línea: el lector experimenta el salto de línea como una pausa momentánea que retrospectivamente se convierte en parte del significado cuando el siguiente verso lo resuelve o redirige.
sentences.en: Enjambment — allowing the sense to run over from one line to the next — creates productive tension between the syntactic unit and the line unit: the reader experiences the line break as a momentary pause that retrospectively becomes part of the meaning when the next line resolves or redirects it.
sentences.es: El encabalgamiento, permitir que el sentido se extienda de un verso al siguiente, crea una tensión productiva entre la unidad sintáctica y la unidad de línea: el lector experimenta el salto de línea como una pausa momentánea que retrospectivamente se convierte en parte del significado cuando el siguiente verso lo resuelve o redirige.

questions.q: How does the speaker describe the relationship between form and meaning in poetry?
options: Form is the aesthetic container that makes meaning accessible to readers unfamiliar with the content
Form and meaning are inseparable — line breaks, stanza divisions, and metre are part of what the poem means
Form provides the rhythmic pleasure while meaning provides the intellectual engagement in the best poetry
The relationship varies by tradition — classical poetry foregrounds form while modern poetry foregrounds meaning
questions.answer: Form and meaning are inseparable — line breaks, stanza divisions, and metre are part of what the poem means

questions.q: What does the speaker say about the function of the volta in a sonnet?
options: It marks the transition from the problem stated in the octave to the solution provided in the sestet
It is the moment where the poem's thinking changes direction, complicates its initial claim, or reframes what came before
It provides the emotional release that the building tension of the octave has been preparing the reader for
It signals the point at which the poem's argument becomes most abstract and philosophical
questions.answer: It is the moment where the poem's thinking changes direction, complicates its initial claim, or reframes what came before

questions.q: What tension does enjambment create according to the speaker?
options: Between the reader's desire for closure and the poem's refusal to provide it until the final line
Between the syntactic unit and the line unit — the line break is a momentary pause that retrospectively becomes part of the meaning
Between the formal constraints of the verse form and the natural rhythm of spoken English
Between the literal meaning of the words and the emotional meaning created by their sound
questions.answer: Between the syntactic unit and the line unit — the line break is a momentary pause that retrospectively becomes part of the meaning

sentences.target: Every text exists in relation to other texts: allusion, quotation, parody, pastiche, and the unconscious shaping of a writer's imagination by the works they have read — these are not departures from originality but the medium through which originality operates.
sentences.native: Todo texto existe en relación con otros textos: la alusión, la cita, la parodia, el pastiche y el moldeado inconsciente de la imaginación de un escritor por las obras que ha leído, no son desviaciones de la originalidad sino el medio a través del cual opera la originalidad.
sentences.en: Every text exists in relation to other texts: allusion, quotation, parody, pastiche, and the unconscious shaping of a writer's imagination by the works they have read — these are not departures from originality but the medium through which originality operates.
sentences.es: Todo texto existe en relación con otros textos: la alusión, la cita, la parodia, el pastiche y el moldeado inconsciente de la imaginación de un escritor por las obras que ha leído, no son desviaciones de la originalidad sino el medio a través del cual opera la originalidad.

sentences.target: A literary allusion performs double work: it enriches the immediate text with the resonances of the alluded work, and it positions the author within a literary tradition, claiming kinship with certain predecessors and implicitly distinguishing themselves from others.
sentences.native: Una alusión literaria realiza un doble trabajo: enriquece el texto inmediato con las resonancias de la obra aludida, y posiciona al autor dentro de una tradición literaria, reclamando parentesco con ciertos predecesores y distinguiéndose implícitamente de otros.
sentences.en: A literary allusion performs double work: it enriches the immediate text with the resonances of the alluded work, and it positions the author within a literary tradition, claiming kinship with certain predecessors and implicitly distinguishing themselves from others.
sentences.es: Una alusión literaria realiza un doble trabajo: enriquece el texto inmediato con las resonancias de la obra aludida, y posiciona al autor dentro de una tradición literaria, reclamando parentesco con ciertos predecesores y distinguiéndose implícitamente de otros.

sentences.target: Parody requires a more intimate understanding of its target than sincere imitation: to exaggerate effectively, the parodist must have internalised the original's style so thoroughly that they can reproduce it at will, then push its characteristic features past the point where they retain aesthetic justification.
sentences.native: La parodia requiere una comprensión más íntima de su objetivo que la imitación sincera: para exagerar efectivamente, el parodista debe haber internalizado el estilo del original tan completamente que pueda reproducirlo a voluntad, luego empujar sus características más allá del punto donde retienen justificación estética.
sentences.en: Parody requires a more intimate understanding of its target than sincere imitation: to exaggerate effectively, the parodist must have internalised the original's style so thoroughly that they can reproduce it at will, then push its characteristic features past the point where they retain aesthetic justification.
sentences.es: La parodia requiere una comprensión más íntima de su objetivo que la imitación sincera: para exagerar efectivamente, el parodista debe haber internalizado el estilo del original tan completamente que pueda reproducirlo a voluntad, luego empujar sus características más allá del punto donde retienen justificación estética.

sentences.target: Pastiche — the imitation of a style without satirical intent — raises questions about the relationship between influence and originality: when does learning from a predecessor become imitation, and when does imitation become theft?
sentences.native: El pastiche, la imitación de un estilo sin intención satírica, plantea preguntas sobre la relación entre la influencia y la originalidad: ¿cuándo aprender de un predecesor se convierte en imitación, y cuándo la imitación se convierte en robo?
sentences.en: Pastiche — the imitation of a style without satirical intent — raises questions about the relationship between influence and originality: when does learning from a predecessor become imitation, and when does imitation become theft?
sentences.es: El pastiche, la imitación de un estilo sin intención satírica, plantea preguntas sobre la relación entre la influencia y la originalidad: ¿cuándo aprender de un predecesor se convierte en imitación, y cuándo la imitación se convierte en robo?

sentences.target: Roland Barthes's declaration that the author is dead — that the meaning of a text is produced in the act of reading rather than in the intention of writing — is not a claim about biography but about authority: the reader cannot be constrained by what the author meant but only by what the text makes possible.
sentences.native: La declaración de Roland Barthes de que el autor ha muerto, que el significado de un texto se produce en el acto de lectura en lugar de en la intención de la escritura, no es una afirmación sobre la biografía sino sobre la autoridad: el lector no puede estar restringido por lo que el autor quiso decir sino solo por lo que el texto hace posible.
sentences.en: Roland Barthes's declaration that the author is dead — that the meaning of a text is produced in the act of reading rather than in the intention of writing — is not a claim about biography but about authority: the reader cannot be constrained by what the author meant but only by what the text makes possible.
sentences.es: La declaración de Roland Barthes de que el autor ha muerto, que el significado de un texto se produce en el acto de lectura en lugar de en la intención de la escritura, no es una afirmación sobre la biografía sino sobre la autoridad: el lector no puede estar restringido por lo que el autor quiso decir sino solo por lo que el texto hace posible.

questions.q: How does the speaker frame literary allusion in relation to originality?
options: Allusion is a form of originality because it creates new meanings by placing familiar content in new contexts
Allusion is not a departure from originality but the medium through which originality operates in a tradition
Originality requires avoiding allusion to ensure the work is not mistaken for derivative or imitative writing
Allusion demonstrates originality by showing the writer's breadth of reading without direct imitation
questions.answer: Allusion is not a departure from originality but the medium through which originality operates in a tradition

questions.q: What does the speaker say parody requires beyond ordinary imitation?
options: A satirical intention that distinguishes the parodist's moral position from the original author's
Such intimate understanding of the target that the parodist can reproduce it at will before pushing it past aesthetic justification
A public recognition that the work is parody rather than sincere imitation, usually through paratext
Greater technical skill than the original because the parodist must simultaneously produce and critique
questions.answer: Such intimate understanding of the target that the parodist can reproduce it at will before pushing it past aesthetic justification

questions.q: What does the speaker say Barthes's 'death of the author' is actually about?
options: The claim that biographical information about an author is irrelevant to understanding their literary intentions
Not biography but authority — the reader cannot be constrained by authorial intent but only by what the text makes possible
The postmodern position that all texts are equivalent because there is no external standard for evaluating quality
The historical observation that authors lose control of their texts' meanings once they enter the public domain
questions.answer: Not biography but authority — the reader cannot be constrained by authorial intent but only by what the text makes possible

sentences.target: Verbal irony says one thing while meaning another, typically the opposite: its success depends entirely on the listener's ability to detect the gap between what is said and what is meant, which requires shared cultural context and attentiveness to tone.
sentences.native: La ironía verbal dice una cosa mientras significa otra, típicamente lo contrario: su éxito depende enteramente de la capacidad del oyente para detectar la brecha entre lo que se dice y lo que se significa, lo que requiere contexto cultural compartido y atención al tono.
sentences.en: Verbal irony says one thing while meaning another, typically the opposite: its success depends entirely on the listener's ability to detect the gap between what is said and what is meant, which requires shared cultural context and attentiveness to tone.
sentences.es: La ironía verbal dice una cosa mientras significa otra, típicamente lo contrario: su éxito depende enteramente de la capacidad del oyente para detectar la brecha entre lo que se dice y lo que se significa, lo que requiere contexto cultural compartido y atención al tono.

sentences.target: Sarcasm is verbal irony deployed as a weapon: while irony can be affectionate or playful, sarcasm is always pointed, always at someone's expense, and carries the implication that the target should have known better than to do or say what they did.
sentences.native: El sarcasmo es la ironía verbal desplegada como un arma: mientras que la ironía puede ser afectuosa o juguetona, el sarcasmo es siempre punzante, siempre a expensas de alguien, y lleva la implicación de que el objetivo debería haber sabido mejor que hacer o decir lo que hizo.
sentences.en: Sarcasm is verbal irony deployed as a weapon: while irony can be affectionate or playful, sarcasm is always pointed, always at someone's expense, and carries the implication that the target should have known better than to do or say what they did.
sentences.es: El sarcasmo es la ironía verbal desplegada como un arma: mientras que la ironía puede ser afectuosa o juguetona, el sarcasmo es siempre punzante, siempre a expensas de alguien, y lleva la implicación de que el objetivo debería haber sabido mejor que hacer o decir lo que hizo.

sentences.target: Understatement — saying less than the truth demands, such as describing a catastrophe as 'a bit unfortunate' — is a characteristically British ironic mode that respects the audience's intelligence by trusting them to supply the missing intensity themselves.
sentences.native: La subestimación, decir menos de lo que la verdad exige, como describir una catástrofe como 'un poco desafortunada', es un modo irónico característicamente británico que respeta la inteligencia del público al confiar en que suministrarán la intensidad faltante ellos mismos.
sentences.en: Understatement — saying less than the truth demands, such as describing a catastrophe as 'a bit unfortunate' — is a characteristically British ironic mode that respects the audience's intelligence by trusting them to supply the missing intensity themselves.
sentences.es: La subestimación, decir menos de lo que la verdad exige, como describir una catástrofe como 'un poco desafortunada', es un modo irónico característicamente británico que respeta la inteligencia del público al confiar en que suministrarán la intensidad faltante ellos mismos.

sentences.target: Dramatic irony is not verbal but structural: it arises when the audience possesses information that a character lacks, generating either the tension of watching someone approach doom unknowingly or the comedy of watching someone operate on false premises that the audience's superior knowledge makes visible as absurd.
sentences.native: La ironía dramática no es verbal sino estructural: surge cuando el público posee información que le falta a un personaje, generando ya sea la tensión de ver a alguien acercarse al destino sin saberlo o la comedia de ver a alguien operar bajo premisas falsas que el conocimiento superior del público hace visibles como absurdas.
sentences.en: Dramatic irony is not verbal but structural: it arises when the audience possesses information that a character lacks, generating either the tension of watching someone approach doom unknowingly or the comedy of watching someone operate on false premises that the audience's superior knowledge makes visible as absurd.
sentences.es: La ironía dramática no es verbal sino estructural: surge cuando el público posee información que le falta a un personaje, generando ya sea la tensión de ver a alguien acercarse al destino sin saberlo o la comedia de ver a alguien operar bajo premisas falsas que el conocimiento superior del público hace visibles como absurdas.

sentences.target: Situational irony differs from dramatic irony in that no audience possesses prior knowledge: it emerges from events themselves when an outcome is the opposite of what the situation seemed to promise — the fire station that burns down is iconic precisely because its situation is defined by its opposition to fire.
sentences.native: La ironía situacional difiere de la ironía dramática en que ningún público posee conocimiento previo: emerge de los eventos mismos cuando un resultado es lo contrario de lo que la situación parecía prometer; el cuartel de bomberos que se incendia es icónico precisamente porque su situación está definida por su oposición al fuego.
sentences.en: Situational irony differs from dramatic irony in that no audience possesses prior knowledge: it emerges from events themselves when an outcome is the opposite of what the situation seemed to promise — the fire station that burns down is iconic precisely because its situation is defined by its opposition to fire.
sentences.es: La ironía situacional difiere de la ironía dramática en que ningún público posee conocimiento previo: emerge de los eventos mismos cuando un resultado es lo contrario de lo que la situación parecía prometer; el cuartel de bomberos que se incendia es icónico precisamente porque su situación está definida por su oposición al fuego.

questions.q: What does the speaker identify as the essential condition for verbal irony to succeed?
options: The speaker must signal ironic intent through exaggerated tone or facial expression
The listener must be able to detect the gap between what is said and what is meant, requiring shared context
The ironic statement must be logically impossible to interpret literally without absurd consequences
Both speakers must belong to the same cultural community with identical social values
questions.answer: The listener must be able to detect the gap between what is said and what is meant, requiring shared context

questions.q: How does the speaker distinguish sarcasm from irony?
options: Sarcasm is always verbal while irony can be situational or dramatic as well
Sarcasm is a weapon — always pointed and at someone's expense — while irony can be affectionate or playful
Sarcasm requires an audience beyond the target while irony can operate as a private signal between two people
Sarcasm is a specifically spoken form while irony is equally effective in written communication
questions.answer: Sarcasm is a weapon — always pointed and at someone's expense — while irony can be affectionate or playful

questions.q: What makes the fire station example iconic as situational irony according to the speaker?
options: Because it involves an institution whose entire purpose is defined by opposition to the thing that destroys it
Because it is unexpected enough to be amusing but plausible enough to have actually occurred
Because it perfectly illustrates how institutional failure generates ironic outcomes
Because the example appears in multiple canonical texts on the theory of irony
questions.answer: Because it involves an institution whose entire purpose is defined by opposition to the thing that destroys it

sentences.target: Comedy operates on the principle of incongruity resolved: something unexpected is introduced, and when the incongruity is resolved in a way that retrospectively makes sense, the cognitive recognition of the resolution generates the affective experience of amusement.
sentences.native: La comedia opera según el principio de la incongruencia resuelta: se introduce algo inesperado, y cuando la incongruencia se resuelve de una manera que retrospectivamente tiene sentido, el reconocimiento cognitivo de la resolución genera la experiencia afectiva de la diversión.
sentences.en: Comedy operates on the principle of incongruity resolved: something unexpected is introduced, and when the incongruity is resolved in a way that retrospectively makes sense, the cognitive recognition of the resolution generates the affective experience of amusement.
sentences.es: La comedia opera según el principio de la incongruencia resuelta: se introduce algo inesperado, y cuando la incongruencia se resuelve de una manera que retrospectivamente tiene sentido, el reconocimiento cognitivo de la resolución genera la experiencia afectiva de la diversión.

sentences.target: Satire is comedy weaponised for critique: by making its targets ridiculous rather than merely wrong, satire reaches audiences that earnest argument cannot and sustains engagement that sustained outrage alone cannot maintain.
sentences.native: La sátira es la comedia convertida en arma para la crítica: al hacer ridículos a sus objetivos en lugar de meramente equivocados, la sátira llega a públicos a los que el argumento serio no puede y sostiene el compromiso que la indignación sostenida sola no puede mantener.
sentences.en: Satire is comedy weaponised for critique: by making its targets ridiculous rather than merely wrong, satire reaches audiences that earnest argument cannot and sustains engagement that sustained outrage alone cannot maintain.
sentences.es: La sátira es la comedia convertida en arma para la crítica: al hacer ridículos a sus objetivos en lugar de meramente equivocados, la sátira llega a públicos a los que el argumento serio no puede y sostiene el compromiso que la indignación sostenida sola no puede mantener.

sentences.target: The comedy of recognition — laughing at ourselves in the foibles the comedian depicts — performs a social function: it confirms shared humanity, dissolves pretension, and creates the sense that everyone in the room is part of the same community of flawed but self-aware people.
sentences.native: La comedia del reconocimiento, reírnos de nosotros mismos en los defectos que el comediante representa, realiza una función social: confirma la humanidad compartida, disuelve la pretensión y crea la sensación de que todos en la sala son parte de la misma comunidad de personas defectuosas pero conscientes de sí mismas.
sentences.en: The comedy of recognition — laughing at ourselves in the foibles the comedian depicts — performs a social function: it confirms shared humanity, dissolves pretension, and creates the sense that everyone in the room is part of the same community of flawed but self-aware people.
sentences.es: La comedia del reconocimiento, reírnos de nosotros mismos en los defectos que el comediante representa, realiza una función social: confirma la humanidad compartida, disuelve la pretensión y crea la sensación de que todos en la sala son parte de la misma comunidad de personas defectuosas pero conscientes de sí mismas.

sentences.target: Black humour insists that laughter is the only honest response to genuinely intolerable situations: not because the situations are not terrible but because solemnity in the face of the absurd is itself a form of dishonesty about how much sense the world actually makes.
sentences.native: El humor negro insiste en que la risa es la única respuesta honesta a situaciones genuinamente intolerables: no porque las situaciones no sean terribles sino porque la solemnidad ante lo absurdo es en sí misma una forma de deshonestidad sobre cuánto sentido tiene realmente el mundo.
sentences.en: Black humour insists that laughter is the only honest response to genuinely intolerable situations: not because the situations are not terrible but because solemnity in the face of the absurd is itself a form of dishonesty about how much sense the world actually makes.
sentences.es: El humor negro insiste en que la risa es la única respuesta honesta a situaciones genuinamente intolerables: no porque las situaciones no sean terribles sino porque la solemnidad ante lo absurdo es en sí misma una forma de deshonestidad sobre cuánto sentido tiene realmente el mundo.

sentences.target: The comedian who 'punches up' — directing humour at the powerful, the hypocritical, and the self-important — is generally regarded as socially legitimate; the comedian who 'punches down' — mocking the vulnerable — faces the accusation that they have converted comedy's social license into a tool of oppression.
sentences.native: El comediante que 'golpea hacia arriba', dirigiendo el humor a los poderosos, los hipócritas y los arrogantes, generalmente se considera socialmente legítimo; el comediante que 'golpea hacia abajo', burlándose de los vulnerables, enfrenta la acusación de haber convertido la licencia social de la comedia en una herramienta de opresión.
sentences.en: The comedian who 'punches up' — directing humour at the powerful, the hypocritical, and the self-important — is generally regarded as socially legitimate; the comedian who 'punches down' — mocking the vulnerable — faces the accusation that they have converted comedy's social license into a tool of oppression.
sentences.es: El comediante que 'golpea hacia arriba', dirigiendo el humor a los poderosos, los hipócritas y los arrogantes, generalmente se considera socialmente legítimo; el comediante que 'golpea hacia abajo', burlándose de los vulnerables, enfrenta la acusación de haber convertido la licencia social de la comedia en una herramienta de opresión.

questions.q: How does the speaker explain why comedy generates amusement using incongruity theory?
options: The unexpected element activates surprise and the surprise itself generates laughter as a release response
Something unexpected is introduced, and when the incongruity is resolved in a way that makes retrospective sense, the recognition generates amusement
Comedy requires that the incongruity be resolved negatively, so that someone or something is diminished by the resolution
The incongruity must be detectable by everyone in the audience simultaneously to produce shared laughter
questions.answer: Something unexpected is introduced, and when the incongruity is resolved in a way that makes retrospective sense, the recognition generates amusement

questions.q: What social function does the speaker attribute to comedy of recognition?
options: It reinforces social hierarchies by allowing the audience to laugh at those below them
It confirms shared humanity, dissolves pretension, and creates community among flawed but self-aware people
It teaches moral lessons by identifying behaviours the audience should avoid through their comic depiction
It provides a safe outlet for social anxieties that would be disruptive if expressed directly
questions.answer: It confirms shared humanity, dissolves pretension, and creates community among flawed but self-aware people

questions.q: What ethical distinction does the speaker draw in relation to punching up versus punching down?
options: Punching up is legally protected speech while punching down may constitute harassment under hate speech laws
Punching up at the powerful is generally regarded as legitimate; punching down at the vulnerable converts social license into a tool of oppression
The distinction is culturally relative and what counts as up or down varies between societies
Punching up is more difficult and therefore demonstrates greater comedic skill than punching down
questions.answer: Punching up at the powerful is generally regarded as legitimate; punching down at the vulnerable converts social license into a tool of oppression

sentences.target: Deadpan humour maintains an absolutely straight face while delivering material that is inherently absurd: the contrast between the gravity of the delivery and the absurdity of the content forces the audience to do the interpretive work themselves, which makes the eventual recognition more satisfying.
sentences.native: El humor deadpan mantiene una cara absolutamente seria mientras entrega material que es inherentemente absurdo: el contraste entre la gravedad de la entrega y lo absurdo del contenido obliga al público a hacer el trabajo interpretativo ellos mismos, lo que hace que el reconocimiento eventual sea más satisfactorio.
sentences.en: Deadpan humour maintains an absolutely straight face while delivering material that is inherently absurd: the contrast between the gravity of the delivery and the absurdity of the content forces the audience to do the interpretive work themselves, which makes the eventual recognition more satisfying.
sentences.es: El humor deadpan mantiene una cara absolutamente seria mientras entrega material que es inherentemente absurdo: el contraste entre la gravedad de la entrega y lo absurdo del contenido obliga al público a hacer el trabajo interpretativo ellos mismos, lo que hace que el reconocimiento eventual sea más satisfactorio.

sentences.target: Wit — the rapid, effortless production of apt and surprising verbal connections — differs from humour more broadly in its emphasis on speed and intelligence: a witty remark must be produced instantly and must demonstrate that the speaker saw a connection that others missed.
sentences.native: El ingenio, la producción rápida y sin esfuerzo de conexiones verbales apropiadas y sorprendentes, difiere del humor más ampliamente en su énfasis en la velocidad y la inteligencia: un comentario ingenioso debe producirse instantáneamente y debe demostrar que el hablante vio una conexión que otros pasaron por alto.
