The declining trust in mainstream media means even accurate reporting is rejected by significant portions of the audience
questions.answer: In a fragmented media landscape, verification and gatekeeping functions are more necessary and harder to sustain

sentences.target: Clinical terminology serves a purpose beyond precision: it creates professional distance between practitioner and the human reality of illness and suffering, allowing medical professionals to think clearly and act decisively in circumstances where pure emotional engagement would be disabling.

sentences.target: The tension between clinical precision and compassionate communication is one of the central challenges of medical practice: the information that must be conveyed is often terrifying, and the language that most accurately conveys it may itself become a barrier to understanding.

questions.q: What does the speaker say sophisticated register command requires beyond knowing specialist features?
options: Producing texts that demonstrate mastery of every feature simultaneously in each communicative act
Knowing when specialist features serve genuine purposes and when they merely obscure meaning or evade accountability
Understanding the historical development of each register so that its conventions can be applied correctly
Producing texts in each register that native specialists cannot distinguish from their own professional writing
questions.answer: Knowing when specialist features serve genuine purposes and when they merely obscure meaning or evade accountability

questions.q: What advanced register competency does the speaker describe in relation to deliberate violations?
options: The ability to identify and correct register violations in others' writing during editing and proofreading
Knowing when to violate register expectations deliberately for precise effect — but only from full control of the register being departed
The capacity to explain why particular register choices are inappropriate and to propose more suitable alternatives
The skill of mixing registers in ways that appear accidental while actually serving precise communicative purposes
questions.answer: Knowing when to violate register expectations deliberately for precise effect — but only from full control of the register being departed

questions.q: How does the speaker ultimately frame register mastery as a social rather than merely linguistic achievement?
options: Because register choices reflect social identity and therefore determine how one is perceived by different communities
Because it is the capacity to participate fully and appropriately in all the different communities of practice that constitute modern life
Because language is inherently social and every linguistic choice is also a social act with consequences for relationships
Because register mastery enables access to the professional networks that provide social and economic opportunity
questions.answer: Because it is the capacity to participate fully and appropriately in all the different communities of practice that constitute modern life

audios.title: How Idioms Work: Meaning Beyond Words

sentences.target: Idiomatic expressions are non-compositional: their meaning cannot be derived by combining the meanings of their parts, which is why 'kick the bucket' cannot be understood from 'kick' and 'bucket' and must be learned as a single lexical item.
sentences.native: Las expresiones idiomáticas son no composicionales: su significado no puede derivarse combinando los significados de sus partes, razón por la cual 'palmar la pata' no puede entenderse desde 'palmar' y 'pata' y debe aprenderse como un único ítem léxico.

sentences.target: The frequency with which native speakers use idioms without noticing them reflects the degree to which idiomatic expressions have been 'semantically bleached' — the original metaphorical force has worn away through overuse, leaving only the conventional meaning.
sentences.native: La frecuencia con la que los hablantes nativos usan modismos sin notarlos refleja el grado en que las expresiones idiomáticas han sido 'blanqueadas semánticamente', la fuerza metafórica original se ha desgastado por el uso excesivo, dejando solo el significado convencional.

sentences.target: Misusing an idiom slightly — 'throw in the sponge' instead of 'throw in the towel' — marks the speaker as a non-native more reliably than any grammatical error, because idioms are stored and reproduced as wholes: there is no rule governing which object a given idiom takes.
sentences.native: Usar un modismo ligeramente mal, 'tirar la esponja' en lugar de 'tirar la toalla', marca al hablante como no nativo con más fiabilidad que cualquier error gramatical, porque los modismos se almacenan y reproducen como un todo: no hay regla que rija qué objeto toma un modismo dado.

sentences.native: La diferencia entre conocer un modismo y controlarlo es la diferencia entre reconocerlo en contexto y desplegarlo espontáneamente en el propio discurso en el momento apropiado con el tono apropiado, una brecha que solo la extensa exposición al uso auténtico puede cerrar.

Their meaning cannot be derived by combining the meanings of their parts and must be learned as a whole

sentences.target: Denotation is the dictionary meaning of a word — its factual, definitional content; connotation is the evaluative, emotional, and social meaning that clusters around a word as a result of how it has been used by the communities that employ it.
sentences.native: La denotación es el significado del diccionario de una palabra, su contenido factual y definitorio; la connotación es el significado evaluativo, emocional y social que se agrupa alrededor de una palabra como resultado de cómo ha sido utilizada por las comunidades que la emplean.
sentences.en: Denotation is the dictionary meaning of a word — its factual, definitional content; connotation is the evaluative, emotional, and social meaning that clusters around a word as a result of how it has been used by the communities that employ it.

sentences.target: Near-synonyms that share a denotative core may differ radically in connotation: 'thrifty', 'economical', 'frugal', and 'miserly' all denote a tendency to spend less than average, but they encode very different evaluations of that tendency — from admirable to contemptible.
sentences.native: Los cuasi sinónimos que comparten un núcleo denotativo pueden diferir radicalmente en connotación: 'ahorrativo', 'económico', 'frugal' y 'tacaño' todos denotan una tendencia a gastar menos que el promedio, pero codifican evaluaciones muy diferentes de esa tendencia, desde admirable hasta despreciable.

sentences.target: The politically charged term is a concentrated case of connotation: 'freedom fighter' and 'terrorist' may describe the same individual's actions, but they activate entirely different normative frameworks, with each term implicitly adjudicating the legitimacy of those actions before any argument has been advanced.
sentences.native: El término políticamente cargado es un caso concentrado de connotación: 'luchador por la libertad' y 'terrorista' pueden describir las acciones del mismo individuo, pero activan marcos normativos completamente diferentes, con cada término adjudicando implícitamente la legitimidad de esas acciones antes de que se haya avanzado ningún argumento.

sentences.target: Euphemism is controlled connotation management: by substituting a term with softer connotations for one with harsher ones, speakers shift the emotional loading of the topic without altering its factual content — 'passed away' describes the same event as 'died' but invites a different emotional response.
sentences.native: El eufemismo es la gestión controlada de la connotación: al sustituir un término con connotaciones más suaves por uno con connotaciones más duras, los hablantes cambian la carga emocional del tema sin alterar su contenido factual; 'falleció' describe el mismo evento que 'murió' pero invita a una respuesta emocional diferente.

sentences.target: Connotative literacy — the ability to recognise the evaluative loading of words, to distinguish it from denotative content, and to make deliberate rather than inadvertent choices — is the most practically consequential of all advanced lexical competencies.
sentences.native: La alfabetización connotativa, la capacidad de reconocer la carga evaluativa de las palabras, distinguirla del contenido denotativo y hacer elecciones deliberadas en lugar de inadvertidas, es la más prácticamente consecuente de todas las competencias léxicas avanzadas.

By showing that thrifty, economical, frugal, and miserly share a denotative core but encode evaluations from admirable to contemptible

sentences.target: Collocations are conventional word pairings whose correctness cannot be determined by grammar or logic but only by the usage patterns that native speakers have crystallised through practice: we 'make' decisions but 'do' favours, 'take' an opportunity but 'seize' a chance.
sentences.native: Las colocaciones son emparejamientos de palabras convencionales cuya corrección no puede determinarse por la gramática o la lógica sino solo por los patrones de uso que los hablantes nativos han cristalizado mediante la práctica: 'tomamos' decisiones pero 'hacemos' favores, 'aprovechamos' una oportunidad pero 'aprovechamos' una chance.
sentences.en: Collocations are conventional word pairings whose correctness cannot be determined by grammar or logic but only by the usage patterns that native speakers have crystallised through practice: we 'make' decisions but 'do' favours, 'take' an opportunity but 'seize' a chance.

sentences.target: Corpus linguistics has quantified the scale of collocational patterning in authentic language: a significant proportion of running text consists of recurring word combinations rather than novel compositional generation — native fluency depends heavily on the extent of one's stored collocation knowledge.
sentences.native: La lingüística de corpus ha cuantificado la escala del patrón colocacional en el lenguaje auténtico: una proporción significativa del texto continuo consiste en combinaciones de palabras recurrentes en lugar de generación composicional novedosa; la fluidez nativa depende en gran medida de la extensión del conocimiento de colocaciones almacenado.
sentences.en: Corpus linguistics has quantified the scale of collocational patterning in authentic language: a significant proportion of running text consists of recurring word combinations rather than novel compositional generation — native fluency depends heavily on the extent of one's stored collocation knowledge.
sentences.es: La lingüística de corpus ha cuantificado la escala del patrón colocacional en el lenguaje auténtico: una proporción significativa del texto continuo consiste en combinaciones de palabras recurrentes en lugar de generación composicional novedosa; la fluidez nativa depende en gran medida de la extensión del conocimiento de colocaciones almacenado.

sentences.target: Strong collocations — pairs where one word strongly predicts the other — are the most visible: 'rancid butter', 'commit a crime', 'heavy smoker'. Weak collocations — where the combination is preferred but not obligatory — are more difficult to acquire because the deviations are less obviously wrong.
sentences.native: Las colocaciones fuertes, pares donde una palabra predice fuertemente a la otra, son las más visibles: 'mantequilla rancia', 'cometer un crimen', 'fumador empedernido'. Las colocaciones débiles, donde la combinación se prefiere pero no es obligatoria, son más difíciles de adquirir porque las desviaciones son menos obviamente incorrectas.

sentences.target: The pedagogical implication of collocation research is that vocabulary teaching cannot focus on individual words: learning that 'heavy' collocates with 'rain', 'traffic', 'drinker', and 'smoker' but not with 'strong', 'rain', or 'breeze' (which take 'strong') cannot be inferred from the meaning of 'heavy' alone.
sentences.native: La implicación pedagógica de la investigación sobre colocaciones es que la enseñanza de vocabulario no puede centrarse en palabras individuales: aprender que 'fuerte' se colocada con 'lluvia', 'tráfico', 'bebedor' y 'fumador' pero no con otros adjetivos que en español significarían lo mismo no puede inferirse del significado de la palabra sola.

sentences.target: Collocational competence signals native-like fluency more clearly than any other single feature: the speaker who consistently chooses grammatically correct but colocationally unusual combinations produces language that feels slightly off to native ears without being identifiably wrong in any way that can be pointed to.
sentences.native: La competencia colocacional señala fluidez nativa con más claridad que cualquier otra característica individual: el hablante que consistentemente elige combinaciones gramaticalmente correctas pero colocacionalmente inusuales produce un lenguaje que suena levemente extraño a oídos nativos sin ser identificablemente incorrecto de ninguna manera que pueda señalarse.

options: By applying the grammatical rules governing verb-object and noun-adjective combinations in English
Only by the usage patterns that native speakers have crystallised through practice, not by grammar or logic

Because the deviations from weak collocations are less obviously wrong, making the errors harder to notice and correct

audios.title: Conceptual Metaphor and How We Think

sentences.target: Lakoff and Johnson's conceptual metaphor theory demonstrated that abstract thought is systematically structured by metaphorical mappings from concrete physical experience: we understand argument through the metaphor of war, time through the metaphor of money, and the mind through the metaphor of a machine.
sentences.native: La teoría de la metáfora conceptual de Lakoff y Johnson demostró que el pensamiento abstracto está estructurado sistemáticamente por mapeos metafóricos de la experiencia física concreta: entendemos el argumento a través de la metáfora de la guerra, el tiempo a través de la metáfora del dinero y la mente a través de la metáfora de una máquina.
sentences.en: Lakoff and Johnson's conceptual metaphor theory demonstrated that abstract thought is systematically structured by metaphorical mappings from concrete physical experience: we understand argument through the metaphor of war, time through the metaphor of money, and the mind through the metaphor of a machine.
sentences.es: La teoría de la metáfora conceptual de Lakoff y Johnson demostró que el pensamiento abstracto está estructurado sistemáticamente por mapeos metafóricos de la experiencia física concreta: entendemos el argumento a través de la metáfora de la guerra, el tiempo a través de la metáfora del dinero y la mente a través de la metáfora de una máquina.

sentences.target: The argument-is-war metaphor is not merely decorative: it shapes which aspects of argument we notice ('attacking weak points'), which moves are available to us ('defending a position'), and what victory and defeat look like — all of which would be different if argument were conceptualised as a dance.
sentences.native: La metáfora 'el argumento es guerra' no es meramente decorativa: da forma a qué aspectos del argumento notamos ('atacar puntos débiles'), qué movimientos están disponibles para nosotros ('defender una posición') y cómo se ven la victoria y la derrota, todo lo cual sería diferente si el argumento se conceptualizara como un baile.

sentences.target: Conceptual metaphors are culturally variable: the metaphor of time-as-money ('spending time', 'saving time', 'wasting time') reflects a specifically modern capitalist relationship with time that is not universal and does not map onto how all cultures conceptualise temporal experience.
sentences.native: Las metáforas conceptuales son culturalmente variables: la metáfora del tiempo como dinero ('gastar tiempo', 'ahorrar tiempo', 'perder el tiempo') refleja una relación específicamente capitalista moderna con el tiempo que no es universal y no se mapea en cómo todas las culturas conceptualizan la experiencia temporal.
sentences.en: Conceptual metaphors are culturally variable: the metaphor of time-as-money ('spending time', 'saving time', 'wasting time') reflects a specifically modern capitalist relationship with time that is not universal and does not map onto how all cultures conceptualise temporal experience.
sentences.es: Las metáforas conceptuales son culturalmente variables: la metáfora del tiempo como dinero ('gastar tiempo', 'ahorrar tiempo', 'perder el tiempo') refleja una relación específicamente capitalista moderna con el tiempo que no es universal y no se mapea en cómo todas las culturas conceptualizan la experiencia temporal.

sentences.target: When a novel metaphor enters the language, it does not merely describe a new reality but actively constitutes one: calling a virus 'going viral' imports the connotations of biological disease — uncontrolled spread, systemic infection, difficult to contain — into a domain where they shape both understanding and response.
sentences.native: Cuando una metáfora novedosa ingresa al lenguaje, no meramente describe una nueva realidad sino que activamente la constituye: llamar a un virus 'volverse viral' importa las connotaciones de la enfermedad biológica, propagación incontrolada, infección sistémica, difícil de contener, a un dominio donde moldean tanto la comprensión como la respuesta.
sentences.en: When a novel metaphor enters the language, it does not merely describe a new reality but actively constitutes one: calling a virus 'going viral' imports the connotations of biological disease — uncontrolled spread, systemic infection, difficult to contain — into a domain where they shape both understanding and response.

sentences.target: Changing the conceptual metaphor used to frame a policy issue can change the solutions that seem available: health researchers have shown that describing crime as a disease generates different policy responses than describing it as a wild beast — 'treatment' versus 'containment' follow from the two frames respectively.

questions.q: What does the speaker say the argument-is-war metaphor shapes beyond the words we use?
options: The emotional intensity of arguments and the social consequences of winning or losing them
Which aspects of argument we notice, which moves are available to us, and what victory and defeat look like
The degree to which we regard opposing viewpoints as legitimate rather than as threats to be defeated
The communicative styles we adopt in argument — more or less aggressive depending on the metaphor's activation
questions.answer: Which aspects of argument we notice, which moves are available to us, and what victory and defeat look like

questions.q: What does the time-as-money metaphor reveal about cultural variation in conceptual metaphors?
options: That more economically developed cultures have richer vocabularies for time management concepts
That this specifically modern capitalist relationship with time is not universal across all cultural conceptualisations
That metaphors about time are more culturally specific than metaphors about space or physical objects
That economic development shapes language structure more profoundly than geography or religion
questions.answer: That this specifically modern capitalist relationship with time is not universal across all cultural conceptualisations

questions.q: What does the crime research example illustrate about metaphor and policy?
options: That politicians deliberately choose metaphors to make their preferred policies seem more appropriate
That disease versus wild beast metaphors generate different policy responses — treatment versus containment
That scientific communication should avoid metaphor to prevent its policy implications from distorting research
That the same metaphor is interpreted differently across cultures, generating divergent policy responses from the same framing
questions.answer: That disease versus wild beast metaphors generate different policy responses — treatment versus containment

audios.title: Phrasal Verbs and the Challenge of Idiomaticity

sentences.target: Phrasal verbs — combinations of a verb and one or more particles whose meaning is not predictable from the components — are among English's most productive and most challenging features: the same verb combined with different particles produces entirely unrelated meanings.
sentences.native: Los verbos frasales, combinaciones de un verbo y una o más partículas cuyo significado no es predecible de los componentes, son una de las características más productivas y más desafiantes del inglés: el mismo verbo combinado con diferentes partículas produce significados completamente no relacionados.
sentences.en: Phrasal verbs — combinations of a verb and one or more particles whose meaning is not predictable from the components — are among English's most productive and most challenging features: the same verb combined with different particles produces entirely unrelated meanings.
sentences.es: Los verbos frasales, combinaciones de un verbo y una o más partículas cuyo significado no es predecible de los componentes, son una de las características más productivas y más desafiantes del inglés: el mismo verbo combinado con diferentes partículas produce significados completamente no relacionados.

sentences.target: The transparency of phrasal verbs ranges from the virtually literal ('sit down') through the partially motivated ('give up' — you give something, and it goes up and away from you) to the entirely opaque ('carry on' — continue — with no discernible compositional logic).
sentences.native: La transparencia de los verbos frasales va desde la prácticamente literal ('sentarse') hasta la parcialmente motivada ('darse por vencido', das algo y se va hacia arriba y lejos de ti) hasta la completamente opaca ('seguir adelante', continuar, sin lógica composicional discernible).
sentences.en: The transparency of phrasal verbs ranges from the virtually literal ('sit down') through the partially motivated ('give up' — you give something, and it goes up and away from you) to the entirely opaque ('carry on' — continue — with no discernible compositional logic).
sentences.es: La transparencia de los verbos frasales va desde la prácticamente literal ('sentarse') hasta la parcialmente motivada ('darse por vencido', das algo y se va hacia arriba y lejos de ti) hasta la completamente opaca ('seguir adelante', continuar, sin lógica composicional discernible).

sentences.target: Register is a crucial variable in phrasal verb choice: 'commence' is the formal alternative to 'kick off', 'terminate' to 'break off', 'investigate' to 'look into' — in academic and legal writing, single-word Latinate verbs are generally preferred to their Anglo-Saxon phrasal equivalents.
sentences.native: El registro es una variable crucial en la elección del verbo frasal: 'comenzar' es la alternativa formal a 'arrancar', 'terminar' a 'cortar', 'investigar' a 'investigar', en la escritura académica y jurídica, los verbos latinos de una sola palabra generalmente se prefieren a sus equivalentes frasales anglosajones.
sentences.en: Register is a crucial variable in phrasal verb choice: 'commence' is the formal alternative to 'kick off', 'terminate' to 'break off', 'investigate' to 'look into' — in academic and legal writing, single-word Latinate verbs are generally preferred to their Anglo-Saxon phrasal equivalents.
sentences.es: El registro es una variable crucial en la elección del verbo frasal: 'comenzar' es la alternativa formal a 'arrancar', 'terminar' a 'cortar', 'investigar' a 'investigar', en la escritura académica y jurídica, los verbos latinos de una sola palabra generalmente se prefieren a sus equivalentes frasales anglosajones.

sentences.target: The separability of transitive phrasal verbs creates an additional complexity: 'turn down' can be separated ('turn the offer down') or kept together ('turn down the offer'), but the rules governing when separation is obligatory, optional, or prohibited are not easily stated and must largely be acquired through exposure.
sentences.native: La separabilidad de los verbos frasales transitivos crea una complejidad adicional: 'rechazar' puede separarse o mantenerse junto, pero las reglas que rigen cuándo la separación es obligatoria, opcional o prohibida no son fáciles de enunciar y deben adquirirse en gran medida a través de la exposición.
sentences.en: The separability of transitive phrasal verbs creates an additional complexity: 'turn down' can be separated ('turn the offer down') or kept together ('turn down the offer'), but the rules governing when separation is obligatory, optional, or prohibited are not easily stated and must largely be acquired through exposure.
sentences.es: La separabilidad de los verbos frasales transitivos crea una complejidad adicional: 'rechazar' puede separarse o mantenerse junto, pero las reglas que rigen cuándo la separación es obligatoria, opcional o prohibida no son fáciles de enunciar y deben adquirirse en gran medida a través de la exposición.

sentences.target: Phrasal verbs are the domain where the native speaker's intuitive competence is most dramatically superior to the advanced learner's: a native speaker has stored thousands of phrasal verbs as single items, while even a very proficient learner must often consciously search for the right combination.
sentences.native: Los verbos frasales son el dominio donde la competencia intuitiva del hablante nativo es más dramáticamente superior a la del aprendiz avanzado: un hablante nativo ha almacenado miles de verbos frasales como ítems únicos, mientras que incluso un aprendiz muy competente a menudo debe buscar conscientemente la combinación correcta.
sentences.en: Phrasal verbs are the domain where the native speaker's intuitive competence is most dramatically superior to the advanced learner's: a native speaker has stored thousands of phrasal verbs as single items, while even a very proficient learner must often consciously search for the right combination.
sentences.es: Los verbos frasales son el dominio donde la competencia intuitiva del hablante nativo es más dramáticamente superior a la del aprendiz avanzado: un hablante nativo ha almacenado miles de verbos frasales como ítems únicos, mientras que incluso un aprendiz muy competente a menudo debe buscar conscientemente la combinación correcta.

questions.q: How does the speaker describe the range of transparency in phrasal verbs?
options: From verbs that are always informal to verbs that can be used in any register including formal academic writing
From virtually literal through partially motivated to entirely opaque with no discernible compositional logic
From those consisting of two elements to those consisting of three or more that are increasingly difficult to acquire
From those where the particle is always separated from the verb to those where it is always kept together
questions.answer: From virtually literal through partially motivated to entirely opaque with no discernible compositional logic

questions.q: What register distinction does the speaker draw in phrasal verb choice?
options: Phrasal verbs are only appropriate in informal speech and should never appear in any written communication
Single-word Latinate verbs are generally preferred in academic and legal writing over Anglo-Saxon phrasal equivalents
The most formal registers prefer the most opaque phrasal verbs because their idiomaticity signals expertise
Phrasal verbs are avoided in British English but commonly used in American professional writing
questions.answer: Single-word Latinate verbs are generally preferred in academic and legal writing over Anglo-Saxon phrasal equivalents

questions.q: Where does the speaker say native speaker intuitive competence most dramatically exceeds advanced learners?
options: In the production of complex grammar structures under time pressure in spontaneous conversation
In phrasal verbs — where natives have stored thousands as single items while learners must consciously search
In the ability to understand rapid native-speed speech with reduced phonetic forms and elision
In the production of appropriate intonation patterns that carry pragmatic meaning in speech
questions.answer: In phrasal verbs — where natives have stored thousands as single items while learners must consciously search

sentences.target: Proverbs encode compressed cultural wisdom — 'a stitch in time saves nine', 'the early bird catches the worm' — but their application is always situational rather than universal: the same culture contains contradictory proverbs ('look before you leap' versus 'he who hesitates is lost') that apply to different circumstances.
sentences.native: Los proverbios codifican sabiduría cultural comprimida, 'un remiendo a tiempo evita ciento', 'a quien madruga Dios le ayuda', pero su aplicación es siempre situacional en lugar de universal: la misma cultura contiene proverbios contradictorios que se aplican a circunstancias diferentes.
sentences.en: Proverbs encode compressed cultural wisdom — 'a stitch in time saves nine', 'the early bird catches the worm' — but their application is always situational rather than universal: the same culture contains contradictory proverbs ('look before you leap' versus 'he who hesitates is lost') that apply to different circumstances.
sentences.es: Los proverbios codifican sabiduría cultural comprimida, 'un remiendo a tiempo evita ciento', 'a quien madruga Dios le ayuda', pero su aplicación es siempre situacional en lugar de universal: la misma cultura contiene proverbios contradictorios que se aplican a circunstancias diferentes.

sentences.target: Literary allusion functions as a high-bandwidth communication shorthand: a well-chosen reference to Hamlet, Don Quixote, or the Bible can convey in a phrase what would take paragraphs to explain from first principles — but only for audiences who share the literary frame of reference.
sentences.native: La alusión literaria funciona como un atajo de comunicación de alto ancho de banda: una referencia bien elegida a Hamlet, Don Quijote o la Biblia puede transmitir en una frase lo que tomaría párrafos explicar desde los principios fundamentales, pero solo para públicos que comparten el marco de referencia literaria.
sentences.en: Literary allusion functions as a high-bandwidth communication shorthand: a well-chosen reference to Hamlet, Don Quixote, or the Bible can convey in a phrase what would take paragraphs to explain from first principles — but only for audiences who share the literary frame of reference.
sentences.es: La alusión literaria funciona como un atajo de comunicación de alto ancho de banda: una referencia bien elegida a Hamlet, Don Quijote o la Biblia puede transmitir en una frase lo que tomaría párrafos explicar desde los principios fundamentales, pero solo para públicos que comparten el marco de referencia literaria.

sentences.target: Popular cultural allusion — to films, television programmes, sports events, or viral moments — has partly replaced literary allusion as the dominant mode of shared cultural reference in contemporary discourse, with implications for the speed at which references date and the audiences they can reach.
sentences.native: La alusión a la cultura popular, a películas, programas de televisión, eventos deportivos o momentos virales, ha reemplazado en parte a la alusión literaria como el modo dominante de referencia cultural compartida en el discurso contemporáneo, con implicaciones para la velocidad a la que las referencias se desactualizan y los públicos a los que pueden llegar.
sentences.en: Popular cultural allusion — to films, television programmes, sports events, or viral moments — has partly replaced literary allusion as the dominant mode of shared cultural reference in contemporary discourse, with implications for the speed at which references date and the audiences they can reach.
sentences.es: La alusión a la cultura popular, a películas, programas de televisión, eventos deportivos o momentos virales, ha reemplazado en parte a la alusión literaria como el modo dominante de referencia cultural compartida en el discurso contemporáneo, con implicaciones para la velocidad a la que las referencias se desactualizan y los públicos a los que pueden llegar.

sentences.target: The in-group allusion — a reference that only members of a specific community will recognise — functions as a powerful identity marker: when someone 'gets' a reference, both parties confirm that they inhabit the same cultural world, which is why the failure to get the reference can produce acute social discomfort.
sentences.native: La alusión de grupo interno, una referencia que solo reconocerán los miembros de una comunidad específica, funciona como un poderoso marcador de identidad: cuando alguien 'entiende' una referencia, ambas partes confirman que habitan el mismo mundo cultural, razón por la cual el fracaso en entender la referencia puede producir un agudo malestar social.
sentences.en: The in-group allusion — a reference that only members of a specific community will recognise — functions as a powerful identity marker: when someone 'gets' a reference, both parties confirm that they inhabit the same cultural world, which is why the failure to get the reference can produce acute social discomfort.
sentences.es: La alusión de grupo interno, una referencia que solo reconocerán los miembros de una comunidad específica, funciona como un poderoso marcador de identidad: cuando alguien 'entiende' una referencia, ambas partes confirman que habitan el mismo mundo cultural, razón por la cual el fracaso en entender la referencia puede producir un agudo malestar social.

sentences.target: Allusive communication requires a delicate calibration of audience knowledge: an allusion that lands perfectly with its intended audience excludes those who do not share the reference, which means that the more specialised the allusion, the higher the risk of excluding the audience you most need to reach.
sentences.native: La comunicación alusiva requiere una calibración delicada del conocimiento del público: una alusión que aterriza perfectamente con su público objetivo excluye a quienes no comparten la referencia, lo que significa que cuanto más especializada es la alusión, mayor es el riesgo de excluir al público que más necesitas alcanzar.
sentences.en: Allusive communication requires a delicate calibration of audience knowledge: an allusion that lands perfectly with its intended audience excludes those who do not share the reference, which means that the more specialised the allusion, the higher the risk of excluding the audience you most need to reach.
sentences.es: La comunicación alusiva requiere una calibración delicada del conocimiento del público: una alusión que aterriza perfectamente con su público objetivo excluye a quienes no comparten la referencia, lo que significa que cuanto más especializada es la alusión, mayor es el riesgo de excluir al público que más necesitas alcanzar.

questions.q: What does the speaker say about the application of proverbs to situations?
options: Proverbs encode universal wisdom that applies in the same way across all cultures and historical periods
Application is always situational rather than universal — the same culture contains contradictory proverbs for different circumstances
Proverbs are most reliable when applied to the specific cultural contexts in which they were originally produced
The most effective proverbs are those that encode wisdom that conflicts with common intuitions, making the point more memorable
questions.answer: Application is always situational rather than universal — the same culture contains contradictory proverbs for different circumstances

questions.q: What does the speaker identify as the risk in using specialised allusions?
options: Specialised allusions may be misidentified by the audience, leading to misinterpretation of the intended reference
The more specialised the allusion, the higher the risk of excluding the audience you most need to reach
Specialised allusions date more quickly than general ones, reducing the shelf life of the communication
Using allusions that only specialists recognise risks appearing elitist in contexts where inclusivity is valued
questions.answer: The more specialised the allusion, the higher the risk of excluding the audience you most need to reach

questions.q: What social function does the speaker attribute to in-group allusions?
options: They serve as a test of cultural knowledge that allows communities to identify and reward their most informed members
They function as identity markers — getting the reference confirms shared cultural world membership
They allow communities to communicate in ways that are opaque to outsiders, protecting private information
They reinforce hierarchies within communities by distinguishing those with more from those with less cultural knowledge
questions.answer: They function as identity markers — getting the reference confirms shared cultural world membership

sentences.target: The register-appropriateness of idiomatic expressions varies enormously: 'bite the bullet' is natural in an informal strategy meeting but a register error in a legal brief, while 'to avail oneself of' is appropriate in formal correspondence but stilted and artificial in casual speech.
sentences.native: La adecuación de registro de las expresiones idiomáticas varía enormemente: 'morder la bala' es natural en una reunión de estrategia informal pero un error de registro en un escrito legal, mientras que 'hacer uso de' es apropiado en la correspondencia formal pero afectado y artificial en el habla casual.
sentences.en: The register-appropriateness of idiomatic expressions varies enormously: 'bite the bullet' is natural in an informal strategy meeting but a register error in a legal brief, while 'to avail oneself of' is appropriate in formal correspondence but stilted and artificial in casual speech.
sentences.es: La adecuación de registro de las expresiones idiomáticas varía enormemente: 'morder la bala' es natural en una reunión de estrategia informal pero un error de registro en un escrito legal, mientras que 'hacer uso de' es apropiado en la correspondencia formal pero afectado y artificial en el habla casual.

sentences.target: Slang idioms have particular register restrictions: because they mark a speaker as belonging to a specific social group or generation, using slang idioms in the wrong context is not just a style error but a social misrepresentation.
sentences.native: Los modismos del argot tienen restricciones de registro particulares: porque marcan a un hablante como perteneciente a un grupo social o generación específica, usar modismos del argot en el contexto equivocado no es solo un error de estilo sino una representación social incorrecta.
sentences.en: Slang idioms have particular register restrictions: because they mark a speaker as belonging to a specific social group or generation, using slang idioms in the wrong context is not just a style error but a social misrepresentation.
sentences.es: Los modismos del argot tienen restricciones de registro particulares: porque marcan a un hablante como perteneciente a un grupo social o generación específica, usar modismos del argot en el contexto equivocado no es solo un error de estilo sino una representación social incorrecta.

sentences.target: The dead metaphor — an expression that was once metaphorical but has been so thoroughly lexicalised that its figurative origin is no longer felt — can often cross register boundaries that living metaphors cannot: 'grasping an idea' is acceptable in academic writing while 'getting your head around an idea' is not.
sentences.native: La metáfora muerta, una expresión que alguna vez fue metafórica pero que ha sido tan completamente lexicalizada que su origen figurativo ya no se siente, a menudo puede cruzar fronteras de registro que las metáforas vivas no pueden: 'comprender una idea' es aceptable en la escritura académica mientras que 'hacerse a la idea de algo' no lo es.
sentences.en: The dead metaphor — an expression that was once metaphorical but has been so thoroughly lexicalised that its figurative origin is no longer felt — can often cross register boundaries that living metaphors cannot: 'grasping an idea' is acceptable in academic writing while 'getting your head around an idea' is not.
sentences.es: La metáfora muerta, una expresión que alguna vez fue metafórica pero que ha sido tan completamente lexicalizada que su origen figurativo ya no se siente, a menudo puede cruzar fronteras de registro que las metáforas vivas no pueden: 'comprender una idea' es aceptable en la escritura académica mientras que 'hacerse a la idea de algo' no lo es.

sentences.target: Professional idioms specific to particular industries — 'in the pipeline', 'off the books', 'on the record' — create community-of-practice belonging: using them correctly signals insider status, while using them incorrectly or in inappropriate contexts signals the opposite.
sentences.native: Los modismos profesionales específicos de industrias particulares, 'en preparación', 'fuera de los libros', 'para el registro', crean pertenencia a la comunidad de práctica: usarlos correctamente señala estatus de iniciado, mientras que usarlos incorrectamente o en contextos inapropiados señala lo contrario.
sentences.en: Professional idioms specific to particular industries — 'in the pipeline', 'off the books', 'on the record' — create community-of-practice belonging: using them correctly signals insider status, while using them incorrectly or in inappropriate contexts signals the opposite.
sentences.es: Los modismos profesionales específicos de industrias particulares, 'en preparación', 'fuera de los libros', 'para el registro', crean pertenencia a la comunidad de práctica: usarlos correctamente señala estatus de iniciado, mientras que usarlos incorrectamente o en contextos inapropiados señala lo contrario.

sentences.target: The advanced learner who has achieved full idiomatic register competence is one who not only knows a wide range of idioms but has internalised the social map that tells them which idiom is appropriate to which context — a meta-competence that native speakers acquire unconsciously but that second-language learners must build deliberately.
sentences.native: El aprendiz avanzado que ha logrado plena competencia idiomática de registro es quien no solo conoce una amplia gama de modismos sino que ha internalizado el mapa social que le dice qué modismo es apropiado a qué contexto, una metacompetencia que los hablantes nativos adquieren inconscientemente pero que los aprendices de segunda lengua deben construir deliberadamente.
sentences.en: The advanced learner who has achieved full idiomatic register competence is one who not only knows a wide range of idioms but has internalised the social map that tells them which idiom is appropriate to which context — a meta-competence that native speakers acquire unconsciously but that second-language learners must build deliberately.
sentences.es: El aprendiz avanzado que ha logrado plena competencia idiomática de registro es quien no solo conoce una amplia gama de modismos sino que ha internalizado el mapa social que le dice qué modismo es apropiado a qué contexto, una metacompetencia que los hablantes nativos adquieren inconscientemente pero que los aprendices de segunda lengua deben construir deliberadamente.

questions.q: What distinction does the speaker draw between dead and living metaphors in relation to register?
options: Dead metaphors are no longer understood by most speakers while living metaphors are currently productive
Dead metaphors can cross register boundaries that living metaphors cannot because their figurative origin is no longer felt
Living metaphors are more expressive and therefore preferred in literary and creative registers
Dead metaphors are the product of historical processes while living metaphors are being created in contemporary slang
questions.answer: Dead metaphors can cross register boundaries that living metaphors cannot because their figurative origin is no longer felt

questions.q: Why does the speaker say using slang idioms in the wrong context is more than a style error?
options: Because slang idioms are often offensive to the audience in formal contexts regardless of their specific meaning
Because slang idioms mark group or generational membership, making their miscontextualised use a social misrepresentation
Because slang idioms evolve quickly and using outdated slang signals that the speaker is not current with their community
Because professional audiences in formal contexts are trained to dismiss arguments delivered in informal register
questions.answer: Because slang idioms mark group or generational membership, making their miscontextualised use a social misrepresentation

questions.q: What meta-competence does the speaker say the truly idiomatically competent advanced learner has internalised?
options: The ability to create new idioms by adapting existing patterns to novel situations
The social map that tells them which idiom is appropriate to which context — that native speakers acquire unconsciously
The complete inventory of all productive idioms in the target language including their historical origins
The skill of explaining idioms to non-native speakers in a way that makes both meaning and usage clear
questions.answer: The social map that tells them which idiom is appropriate to which context — that native speakers acquire unconsciously

sentences.target: Figurative language is not merely decorative but cognitive: the metaphors we use to describe complex phenomena shape the solutions we can imagine, the emotions we experience, and the moral judgements we make — which is why control of figurative language is control of thought.
sentences.native: El lenguaje figurado no es meramente decorativo sino cognitivo: las metáforas que usamos para describir fenómenos complejos moldean las soluciones que podemos imaginar, las emociones que experimentamos y los juicios morales que hacemos, razón por la cual el control del lenguaje figurado es el control del pensamiento.
sentences.en: Figurative language is not merely decorative but cognitive: the metaphors we use to describe complex phenomena shape the solutions we can imagine, the emotions we experience, and the moral judgements we make — which is why control of figurative language is control of thought.
sentences.es: El lenguaje figurado no es meramente decorativo sino cognitivo: las metáforas que usamos para describir fenómenos complejos moldean las soluciones que podemos imaginar, las emociones que experimentamos y los juicios morales que hacemos, razón por la cual el control del lenguaje figurado es el control del pensamiento.

sentences.target: The military metaphor in medicine — 'fighting cancer', 'attacking the tumour', 'the body's defences' — has been criticised for placing unrealistic demands on patients: 'losing the battle' with cancer carries an implication of personal failure that is both empirically false and psychologically damaging.
sentences.native: La metáfora militar en medicina, 'luchar contra el cáncer', 'atacar el tumor', 'las defensas del cuerpo', ha sido criticada por poner demandas poco realistas en los pacientes: 'perder la batalla' contra el cáncer lleva una implicación de fracaso personal que es tanto empíricamente falsa como psicológicamente dañina.
sentences.en: The military metaphor in medicine — 'fighting cancer', 'attacking the tumour', 'the body's defences' — has been criticised for placing unrealistic demands on patients: 'losing the battle' with cancer carries an implication of personal failure that is both empirically false and psychologically damaging.
sentences.es: La metáfora militar en medicina, 'luchar contra el cáncer', 'atacar el tumor', 'las defensas del cuerpo', ha sido criticada por poner demandas poco realistas en los pacientes: 'perder la batalla' contra el cáncer lleva una implicación de fracaso personal que es tanto empíricamente falsa como psicológicamente dañina.

sentences.target: Personification — attributing human agency to non-human forces — is pervasive in economic and political discourse: 'the market decided', 'history will judge', 'technology demands' present contingent human choices as inevitable natural forces beyond control or accountability.
sentences.native: La personificación, atribuir agencia humana a fuerzas no humanas, es omnipresente en el discurso económico y político: 'el mercado decidió', 'la historia juzgará', 'la tecnología exige' presentan elecciones humanas contingentes como fuerzas naturales inevitables más allá del control o la responsabilidad.
sentences.en: Personification — attributing human agency to non-human forces — is pervasive in economic and political discourse: 'the market decided', 'history will judge', 'technology demands' present contingent human choices as inevitable natural forces beyond control or accountability.
sentences.es: La personificación, atribuir agencia humana a fuerzas no humanas, es omnipresente en el discurso económico y político: 'el mercado decidió', 'la historia juzgará', 'la tecnología exige' presentan elecciones humanas contingentes como fuerzas naturales inevitables más allá del control o la responsabilidad.

sentences.target: Synecdoche — substituting the part for the whole or the whole for the part — is a form of figurative condensation: 'hands' for 'workers', 'suits' for 'management', 'boots on the ground' for 'soldiers' — each choice implicitly emphasises certain aspects while suppressing others.
sentences.native: La sinécdoque, sustituir la parte por el todo o el todo por la parte, es una forma de condensación figurativa: 'manos' para 'trabajadores', 'trajes' para 'gerencia', 'botas en el terreno' para 'soldados', cada elección implícitamente enfatiza ciertos aspectos mientras suprime otros.
sentences.en: Synecdoche — substituting the part for the whole or the whole for the part — is a form of figurative condensation: 'hands' for 'workers', 'suits' for 'management', 'boots on the ground' for 'soldiers' — each choice implicitly emphasises certain aspects while suppressing others.
sentences.es: La sinécdoque, sustituir la parte por el todo o el todo por la parte, es una forma de condensación figurativa: 'manos' para 'trabajadores', 'trajes' para 'gerencia', 'botas en el terreno' para 'soldados', cada elección implícitamente enfatiza ciertos aspectos mientras suprime otros.

sentences.target: The extended mixed metaphor — maintaining several incompatible figurative frames simultaneously — is the most common figurative error in advanced writing: 'we need to get all our ducks in a row before we can hit the ground running and put this issue to bed' imports three incompatible spatial and temporal frames into a single sentence.
sentences.native: La metáfora mixta extendida, mantener varios marcos figurativos incompatibles simultáneamente, es el error figurativo más común en la escritura avanzada: importar tres marcos espaciales y temporales incompatibles en una sola oración resulta en un enunciado que activa imágenes contradictorias que el lector no puede sintetizar coherentemente.
sentences.en: The extended mixed metaphor — maintaining several incompatible figurative frames simultaneously — is the most common figurative error in advanced writing: 'we need to get all our ducks in a row before we can hit the ground running and put this issue to bed' imports three incompatible spatial and temporal frames into a single sentence.
sentences.es: La metáfora mixta extendida, mantener varios marcos figurativos incompatibles simultáneamente, es el error figurativo más común en la escritura avanzada: importar tres marcos espaciales y temporales incompatibles en una sola oración resulta en un enunciado que activa imágenes contradictorias que el lector no puede sintetizar coherentemente.

questions.q: What critique does the speaker raise about military metaphors in medical discourse?
options: They create a culture of excessive intervention that leads to overtreatment of terminal patients
They place unrealistic demands on patients — losing the 'battle' implies personal failure that is empirically false and psychologically damaging
They obscure the actual biological mechanisms of disease by substituting dramatic narratives for scientific explanation
They were introduced by pharmaceutical companies to market cancer treatment as heroic struggle requiring expensive intervention
questions.answer: They place unrealistic demands on patients — losing the 'battle' implies personal failure that is empirically false and psychologically damaging

questions.q: What does the speaker say personification does to human choices in economic and political discourse?
options: It makes abstract economic forces more emotionally engaging for audiences who do not follow economic debates
It presents contingent human choices as inevitable natural forces beyond control or accountability
It simplifies complex multi-causal processes into narratives that are easier for journalists to communicate
It assigns blame to impersonal forces rather than to individuals in ways that reduce political accountability
questions.answer: It presents contingent human choices as inevitable natural forces beyond control or accountability

questions.q: What does the speaker identify as the most common figurative error in advanced writing?
options: Over-reliance on clichéd metaphors that have lost their imaginative force through excessive repetition
The extended mixed metaphor — maintaining incompatible figurative frames simultaneously in a single sentence
Using technical metaphors from one domain in another where the mapping breaks down under scrutiny
Extending a single metaphor so far that its limitations become visible and undermine the argument it is supporting
questions.answer: The extended mixed metaphor — maintaining incompatible figurative frames simultaneously in a single sentence

audios.title: Lexical Precision and the Exact Word

sentences.target: The exact word is not the most impressive word but the most precise: the writer who chooses 'gaunt' over 'thin', 'apprehensive' over 'worried', or 'equivocal' over 'unclear' is making a choice about the precise shade of meaning required — not a performance of vocabulary size.
sentences.native: La palabra exacta no es la más impresionante sino la más precisa: el escritor que elige 'demacrado' sobre 'delgado', 'aprensivo' sobre 'preocupado' o 'equívoco' sobre 'poco claro' está tomando una decisión sobre el matiz preciso de significado requerido, no una actuación del tamaño del vocabulario.
sentences.en: The exact word is not the most impressive word but the most precise: the writer who chooses 'gaunt' over 'thin', 'apprehensive' over 'worried', or 'equivocal' over 'unclear' is making a choice about the precise shade of meaning required — not a performance of vocabulary size.
sentences.es: La palabra exacta no es la más impresionante sino la más precisa: el escritor que elige 'demacrado' sobre 'delgado', 'aprensivo' sobre 'preocupado' o 'equívoco' sobre 'poco claro' está tomando una decisión sobre el matiz preciso de significado requerido, no una actuación del tamaño del vocabulario.

sentences.target: Many near-synonym errors in advanced writing result not from ignorance of the words but from failure to attend to the precise contextual requirements: 'infer' and 'imply' are often confused because both involve something not explicitly stated, but they occupy different positions in the communicative act.
sentences.native: Muchos errores de cuasi sinónimos en la escritura avanzada resultan no de la ignorancia de las palabras sino de la falta de atención a los requisitos contextuales precisos: 'inferir' e 'implicar' se confunden frecuentemente porque ambos involucran algo que no se declara explícitamente, pero ocupan posiciones diferentes en el acto comunicativo.
sentences.en: Many near-synonym errors in advanced writing result not from ignorance of the words but from failure to attend to the precise contextual requirements: 'infer' and 'imply' are often confused because both involve something not explicitly stated, but they occupy different positions in the communicative act.
sentences.es: Muchos errores de cuasi sinónimos en la escritura avanzada resultan no de la ignorancia de las palabras sino de la falta de atención a los requisitos contextuales precisos: 'inferir' e 'implicar' se confunden frecuentemente porque ambos involucran algo que no se declara explícitamente, pero ocupan posiciones diferentes en el acto comunicativo.

sentences.target: The distinction between 'disinterested' and 'uninterested' is a paradigmatic case of lexical precision: 'disinterested' means impartial, without personal stake; 'uninterested' means lacking engagement or curiosity — confusing them inverts the meaning and describes the opposite quality.
sentences.native: La distinción entre 'desinteresado' e 'indiferente' es un caso paradigmático de precisión léxica: 'desinteresado' significa imparcial, sin interés personal; 'indiferente' significa carecer de compromiso o curiosidad; confundirlos invierte el significado y describe la calidad opuesta.
sentences.en: The distinction between 'disinterested' and 'uninterested' is a paradigmatic case of lexical precision: 'disinterested' means impartial, without personal stake; 'uninterested' means lacking engagement or curiosity — confusing them inverts the meaning and describes the opposite quality.
sentences.es: La distinción entre 'desinteresado' e 'indiferente' es un caso paradigmático de precisión léxica: 'desinteresado' significa imparcial, sin interés personal; 'indiferente' significa carecer de compromiso o curiosidad; confundirlos invierte el significado y describe la calidad opuesta.

sentences.target: The word 'literally' has undergone semantic broadening through colloquial use — now regularly used to intensify figurative statements ('I literally died laughing') — and this broadening means that 'literally' can no longer unambiguously signal literal rather than figurative meaning in informal contexts.
sentences.native: La palabra 'literalmente' ha experimentado una ampliación semántica a través del uso coloquial, ahora usada regularmente para intensificar declaraciones figurativas ('literalmente me morí de risa'), y esta ampliación significa que 'literalmente' ya no puede señalar de manera inequívoca el significado literal en lugar de figurativo en contextos informales.
sentences.en: The word 'literally' has undergone semantic broadening through colloquial use — now regularly used to intensify figurative statements ('I literally died laughing') — and this broadening means that 'literally' can no longer unambiguously signal literal rather than figurative meaning in informal contexts.
sentences.es: La palabra 'literalmente' ha experimentado una ampliación semántica a través del uso coloquial, ahora usada regularmente para intensificar declaraciones figurativas ('literalmente me morí de risa'), y esta ampliación significa que 'literalmente' ya no puede señalar de manera inequívoca el significado literal en lugar de figurativo en contextos informales.

sentences.target: The careful writer's principle is that every word must earn its place: if a word can be removed without loss of meaning, precision, or rhythm, it should be — because superfluous words do not merely fail to add; they actively dilute the words that remain.
sentences.native: El principio del escritor cuidadoso es que cada palabra debe ganarse su lugar: si una palabra puede eliminarse sin pérdida de significado, precisión o ritmo, debe hacerse, porque las palabras superfluas no meramente fallan en agregar; activamente diluyen las palabras que permanecen.
sentences.en: The careful writer's principle is that every word must earn its place: if a word can be removed without loss of meaning, precision, or rhythm, it should be — because superfluous words do not merely fail to add; they actively dilute the words that remain.
sentences.es: El principio del escritor cuidadoso es que cada palabra debe ganarse su lugar: si una palabra puede eliminarse sin pérdida de significado, precisión o ritmo, debe hacerse, porque las palabras superfluas no meramente fallan en agregar; activamente diluyen las palabras que permanecen.

questions.q: What does the speaker say distinguishes choosing the exact word from performing vocabulary size?
options: The exact word is always the most specialised term available that demonstrates the writer's domain expertise
The exact word is not the most impressive but the most precise — the right shade of meaning for the context
The exact word is always the shorter or simpler option because shorter words are more precise than longer ones
The exact word is the one that most readers will understand immediately without needing additional context
questions.answer: The exact word is not the most impressive but the most precise — the right shade of meaning for the context

questions.q: How does the speaker illustrate the disinterested/uninterested distinction?
options: As a case where the more formal term has been displaced by the more casual one in contemporary usage
As a paradigmatic precision case where confusion inverts the meaning — impartial versus lacking curiosity
As an example of semantic broadening where both words now cover each other's original meanings
As a distinction that matters in legal and academic contexts but is irrelevant in everyday communication
questions.answer: As a paradigmatic precision case where confusion inverts the meaning — impartial versus lacking curiosity

questions.q: What principle does the speaker state about words that can be removed without loss?
options: Optional words should be kept if they improve the rhythm of the sentence even if they are semantically redundant
Words that can be removed without loss should be removed because superfluous words actively dilute those that remain
The decision to remove or keep optional words should be guided by the register and the expectations of the intended audience
Words that seem removable should be tested in context before deletion because some function at a discourse rather than sentence level
questions.answer: Words that can be removed without loss should be removed because superfluous words actively dilute those that remain

sentences.target: Idiomatic fluency cannot be achieved through memorisation of lists: the ability to deploy an idiom at the right moment, in the right register, with the right tone, for the right audience requires the kind of contextual knowledge that only exposure to authentic language use over time can provide.
sentences.native: La fluidez idiomática no puede lograrse a través de la memorización de listas: la capacidad de desplegar un modismo en el momento correcto, en el registro correcto, con el tono correcto, para el público correcto requiere el tipo de conocimiento contextual que solo la exposición al uso auténtico del lenguaje a lo largo del tiempo puede proporcionar.
sentences.en: Idiomatic fluency cannot be achieved through memorisation of lists: the ability to deploy an idiom at the right moment, in the right register, with the right tone, for the right audience requires the kind of contextual knowledge that only exposure to authentic language use over time can provide.
sentences.es: La fluidez idiomática no puede lograrse a través de la memorización de listas: la capacidad de desplegar un modismo en el momento correcto, en el registro correcto, con el tono correcto, para el público correcto requiere el tipo de conocimiento contextual que solo la exposición al uso auténtico del lenguaje a lo largo del tiempo puede proporcionar.

sentences.target: Reading extensively in the target language is the most efficient route to idiom acquisition: not because reading lists are a substitute for authentic exposure, but because extensive reading provides the repeated contextual encounters through which idiom meanings, registers, and usage conditions are gradually internalised.
sentences.native: Leer extensamente en el idioma meta es la ruta más eficiente para la adquisición de modismos: no porque las listas de lectura sean un sustituto de la exposición auténtica, sino porque la lectura extensiva proporciona los encuentros contextuales repetidos a través de los cuales los significados de los modismos, los registros y las condiciones de uso se internalizan gradualmente.
sentences.en: Reading extensively in the target language is the most efficient route to idiom acquisition: not because reading lists are a substitute for authentic exposure, but because extensive reading provides the repeated contextual encounters through which idiom meanings, registers, and usage conditions are gradually internalised.
sentences.es: Leer extensamente en el idioma meta es la ruta más eficiente para la adquisición de modismos: no porque las listas de lectura sean un sustituto de la exposición auténtica, sino porque la lectura extensiva proporciona los encuentros contextuales repetidos a través de los cuales los significados de los modismos, los registros y las condiciones de uso se internalizan gradualmente.

sentences.target: The noticing hypothesis suggests that learners only acquire features of the target language that they actively notice: passive exposure to idiomatic language without attentive noticing is less effective than the same exposure combined with deliberate attention to how idioms are used in context.
sentences.native: La hipótesis de la notación sugiere que los aprendices solo adquieren características del idioma meta que notan activamente: la exposición pasiva al lenguaje idiomático sin notación atenta es menos efectiva que la misma exposición combinada con atención deliberada a cómo se usan los modismos en contexto.
sentences.en: The noticing hypothesis suggests that learners only acquire features of the target language that they actively notice: passive exposure to idiomatic language without attentive noticing is less effective than the same exposure combined with deliberate attention to how idioms are used in context.
sentences.es: La hipótesis de la notación sugiere que los aprendices solo adquieren características del idioma meta que notan activamente: la exposición pasiva al lenguaje idiomático sin notación atenta es menos efectiva que la misma exposición combinada con atención deliberada a cómo se usan los modismos en contexto.

sentences.target: The output hypothesis complements input: learners who attempt to use idioms in their own speaking and writing — and receive feedback on their usage — acquire them more efficiently than those who only comprehend them receptively, because productive use forces a more precise representation of the idiom's constraints.
sentences.native: La hipótesis de producción complementa la entrada: los aprendices que intentan usar modismos en su propia habla y escritura y reciben retroalimentación sobre su uso los adquieren más eficientemente que los que solo los comprenden receptivamente, porque el uso productivo obliga a una representación más precisa de las restricciones del modismo.
sentences.en: The output hypothesis complements input: learners who attempt to use idioms in their own speaking and writing — and receive feedback on their usage — acquire them more efficiently than those who only comprehend them receptively, because productive use forces a more precise representation of the idiom's constraints.
sentences.es: La hipótesis de producción complementa la entrada: los aprendices que intentan usar modismos en su propia habla y escritura y reciben retroalimentación sobre su uso los adquieren más eficientemente que los que solo los comprenden receptivamente, porque el uso productivo obliga a una representación más precisa de las restricciones del modismo.

sentences.target: The milestone of idiomatic mastery is when the learner stops consciously monitoring their idiomatic production and starts simply speaking — trusting that the years of exposure and practice have built the intuitive knowledge that native speakers deploy automatically in every conversation.
sentences.native: El hito del dominio idiomático es cuando el aprendiz deja de monitorear conscientemente su producción idiomática y comienza simplemente a hablar, confiando en que los años de exposición y práctica han construido el conocimiento intuitivo que los hablantes nativos despliegan automáticamente en cada conversación.
sentences.en: The milestone of idiomatic mastery is when the learner stops consciously monitoring their idiomatic production and starts simply speaking — trusting that the years of exposure and practice have built the intuitive knowledge that native speakers deploy automatically in every conversation.
sentences.es: El hito del dominio idiomático es cuando el aprendiz deja de monitorear conscientemente su producción idiomática y comienza simplemente a hablar, confiando en que los años de exposición y práctica han construido el conocimiento intuitivo que los hablantes nativos despliegan automáticamente en cada conversación.

questions.q: Why does the speaker say list memorisation cannot achieve idiomatic fluency?
options: Because lists cannot contain enough idioms to cover the full range needed for authentic communication
Because deploying idioms correctly requires contextual knowledge of register, tone, and audience that only authentic exposure provides
Because idioms change faster than lists can be updated, making any list approach an obsolete method
Because the cognitive load of memorising lists interferes with the fluency required for natural speech production
questions.answer: Because deploying idioms correctly requires contextual knowledge of register, tone, and audience that only authentic exposure provides

questions.q: What does the noticing hypothesis suggest about idiomatic acquisition?
options: That learners acquire idioms most efficiently when they encounter them multiple times in a short period
That learners only acquire language features they actively notice — passive exposure without attentive noticing is less effective
That explicit instruction in idiom meaning accelerates acquisition relative to implicit exposure without explanation
That noticing errors in one's own idiomatic production is more effective than noticing correct usage in others' speech
questions.answer: That learners only acquire language features they actively notice — passive exposure without attentive noticing is less effective

questions.q: What does the speaker say marks the milestone of idiomatic mastery?
options: The ability to produce new idioms that follow productive patterns in ways that native speakers find acceptable
When the learner stops consciously monitoring idiomatic production and trusts their built intuitive knowledge
The point at which the learner's idiomatic errors become infrequent enough not to disrupt communication
When native speaker interlocutors stop noticing or commenting on the learner's idiomatic choices
questions.answer: When the learner stops consciously monitoring idiomatic production and trusts their built intuitive knowledge

sentences.target: Linguistic mediation — the act of bridging communication between speakers of different languages or registers — is never a neutral transmission of content: every mediator makes choices about what to include, what to emphasise, and what to smooth over, and those choices carry consequences.
sentences.native: La mediación lingüística, el acto de tender puentes de comunicación entre hablantes de diferentes lenguas o registros, nunca es una transmisión neutral de contenido: cada mediador toma decisiones sobre qué incluir, qué enfatizar y qué suavizar, y esas decisiones tienen consecuencias.
sentences.en: Linguistic mediation — the act of bridging communication between speakers of different languages or registers — is never a neutral transmission of content: every mediator makes choices about what to include, what to emphasise, and what to smooth over, and those choices carry consequences.
sentences.es: La mediación lingüística, el acto de tender puentes de comunicación entre hablantes de diferentes lenguas o registros, nunca es una transmisión neutral de contenido: cada mediador toma decisiones sobre qué incluir, qué enfatizar y qué suavizar, y esas decisiones tienen consecuencias.

sentences.target: The interpreter who chooses to render an aggressive question in polite form, or a technical term in lay language without marking the simplification, has made an editorial decision that changes what the original speaker communicated — even if the factual content is preserved.
sentences.native: El intérprete que elige convertir una pregunta agresiva en forma cortés, o un término técnico en lenguaje llano sin marcar la simplificación, ha tomado una decisión editorial que cambia lo que el hablante original comunicó, incluso si el contenido factual se preserva.
sentences.en: The interpreter who chooses to render an aggressive question in polite form, or a technical term in lay language without marking the simplification, has made an editorial decision that changes what the original speaker communicated — even if the factual content is preserved.
sentences.es: El intérprete que elige convertir una pregunta agresiva en forma cortés, o un término técnico en lenguaje llano sin marcar la simplificación, ha tomado una decisión editorial que cambia lo que el hablante original comunicó, incluso si el contenido factual se preserva.

sentences.target: In legal and medical contexts, the stakes of mediation errors are exceptionally high: a mistranslation in a medical consultation can lead to misdiagnosis, while an error in a legal proceeding can affect the outcome of a case involving someone's liberty — which is why professional interpreters in these domains are trained in domain-specific terminology as rigorously as the practitioners themselves.
sentences.native: En contextos legales y médicos, las apuestas de los errores de mediación son excepcionalmente altas: una mala traducción en una consulta médica puede llevar a un diagnóstico erróneo, mientras que un error en un procedimiento legal puede afectar el resultado de un caso que involucra la libertad de alguien, razón por la cual los intérpretes profesionales en estos dominios se entrenan en terminología específica del dominio tan rigurosamente como los propios practicantes.
sentences.en: In legal and medical contexts, the stakes of mediation errors are exceptionally high: a mistranslation in a medical consultation can lead to misdiagnosis, while an error in a legal proceeding can affect the outcome of a case involving someone's liberty — which is why professional interpreters in these domains are trained in domain-specific terminology as rigorously as the practitioners themselves.
sentences.es: En contextos legales y médicos, las apuestas de los errores de mediación son excepcionalmente altas: una mala traducción en una consulta médica puede llevar a un diagnóstico erróneo, mientras que un error en un procedimiento legal puede afectar el resultado de un caso que involucra la libertad de alguien, razón por la cual los intérpretes profesionales en estos dominios se entrenan en terminología específica del dominio tan rigurosamente como los propios practicantes.

sentences.target: Cross-cultural mediation adds a layer of complexity that purely linguistic mediation does not: the mediator must decide whether to explain cultural context that would be obvious to a member of one culture but opaque to a member of the other, and that decision is itself a cultural choice.
sentences.native: La mediación intercultural añade una capa de complejidad que la mediación puramente lingüística no tiene: el mediador debe decidir si explicar el contexto cultural que sería obvio para un miembro de una cultura pero opaco para un miembro de la otra, y esa decisión es en sí misma una elección cultural.
sentences.en: Cross-cultural mediation adds a layer of complexity that purely linguistic mediation does not: the mediator must decide whether to explain cultural context that would be obvious to a member of one culture but opaque to a member of the other, and that decision is itself a cultural choice.
sentences.es: La mediación intercultural añade una capa de complejidad que la mediación puramente lingüística no tiene: el mediador debe decidir si explicar el contexto cultural que sería obvio para un miembro de una cultura pero opaco para un miembro de la otra, y esa decisión es en sí misma una elección cultural.

sentences.target: The ethics of mediation require that the mediator serve the communication between parties rather than their own interests, institutional interests, or the interests of whichever party they are more closely affiliated with — a requirement that is simple to state and extraordinarily difficult to honour in practice.
sentences.native: La ética de la mediación requiere que el mediador sirva a la comunicación entre las partes en lugar de sus propios intereses, los intereses institucionales o los intereses de cualquiera de las partes con la que esté más estrechamente afiliado, un requisito que es simple de enunciar y extraordinariamente difícil de cumplir en la práctica.
sentences.en: The ethics of mediation require that the mediator serve the communication between parties rather than their own interests, institutional interests, or the interests of whichever party they are more closely affiliated with — a requirement that is simple to state and extraordinarily difficult to honour in practice.
sentences.es: La ética de la mediación requiere que el mediador sirva a la comunicación entre las partes en lugar de sus propios intereses, los intereses institucionales o los intereses de cualquiera de las partes con la que esté más estrechamente afiliado, un requisito que es simple de enunciar y extraordinariamente difícil de cumplir en la práctica.

questions.q: Why does the speaker say linguistic mediation is never a neutral transmission of content?
options: Because different languages have different grammatical structures that inevitably change the form of a message
Because every mediator makes choices about what to include, emphasise, and smooth over, with real consequences
Because no two languages share exactly the same inventory of concepts, so something is always lost in translation
Because mediators inevitably bring their own cultural interpretations that shape how they render source material
questions.answer: Because every mediator makes choices about what to include, emphasise, and smooth over, with real consequences

questions.q: Why does the speaker say professional interpreters in legal and medical contexts are trained as rigorously as practitioners?
options: Because legal and medical proceedings require interpreters to have equivalent qualifications to the professionals they assist
Because mistranslation in these domains can lead to misdiagnosis or affect liberty — the stakes of mediation errors are exceptionally high
Because legal and medical settings require interpreters to give professional opinions alongside linguistic transfer
Because interpreters in these contexts must manage emotional complexity alongside technical content simultaneously
questions.answer: Because mistranslation in these domains can lead to misdiagnosis or affect liberty — the stakes of mediation errors are exceptionally high

questions.q: What ethical requirement does the speaker state for mediators?
