options: Mediators must document every decision they make so that parties can audit the choices in the mediating process
Mediators must serve the communication between parties rather than their own or institutional interests
Mediators must always translate literally rather than interpretively to avoid imposing their own judgement on the content
Mediators must disclose any affiliations that might compromise their neutrality before beginning any mediation engagement
questions.answer: Mediators must serve the communication between parties rather than their own or institutional interests

sentences.target: A précis is not a summary: a summary reports the content of a text, while a précis reproduces the logical structure of the argument in compressed form, preserving the hierarchy of main and supporting claims and the connective tissue of inference and evidence.
sentences.native: Un précis no es un resumen: un resumen reporta el contenido de un texto, mientras que un précis reproduce la estructura lógica del argumento en forma comprimida, preservando la jerarquía de afirmaciones principales y de apoyo y el tejido conectivo de inferencia y evidencia.
sentences.en: A précis is not a summary: a summary reports the content of a text, while a précis reproduces the logical structure of the argument in compressed form, preserving the hierarchy of main and supporting claims and the connective tissue of inference and evidence.
sentences.es: Un précis no es un resumen: un resumen reporta el contenido de un texto, mientras que un précis reproduce la estructura lógica del argumento en forma comprimida, preservando la jerarquía de afirmaciones principales y de apoyo y el tejido conectivo de inferencia y evidencia.

sentences.target: The discipline of writing a précis forces the writer to have understood the original text at a structural rather than a surface level: one cannot reproduce the logical architecture of an argument one has not fully comprehended, which is why précis writing is one of the most effective tests of reading comprehension.
sentences.native: La disciplina de escribir un précis obliga al escritor a haber entendido el texto original a un nivel estructural en lugar de superficial: uno no puede reproducir la arquitectura lógica de un argumento que no ha comprendido completamente, razón por la cual la escritura de précis es una de las pruebas más efectivas de comprensión lectora.
sentences.en: The discipline of writing a précis forces the writer to have understood the original text at a structural rather than a surface level: one cannot reproduce the logical architecture of an argument one has not fully comprehended, which is why précis writing is one of the most effective tests of reading comprehension.
sentences.es: La disciplina de escribir un précis obliga al escritor a haber entendido el texto original a un nivel estructural en lugar de superficial: uno no puede reproducir la arquitectura lógica de un argumento que no ha comprendido completamente, razón por la cual la escritura de précis es una de las pruebas más efectivas de comprensión lectora.

sentences.target: Synthesis writing requires integrating multiple sources into a coherent argument of one's own: it is the opposite of report writing, which keeps sources separate and labelled, because synthesis merges perspectives into a unified position that the writer controls and is responsible for.
sentences.native: La escritura de síntesis requiere integrar múltiples fuentes en un argumento coherente propio: es lo opuesto de la escritura de informes, que mantiene las fuentes separadas y etiquetadas, porque la síntesis fusiona perspectivas en una posición unificada que el escritor controla y de la que es responsable.
sentences.en: Synthesis writing requires integrating multiple sources into a coherent argument of one's own: it is the opposite of report writing, which keeps sources separate and labelled, because synthesis merges perspectives into a unified position that the writer controls and is responsible for.
sentences.es: La escritura de síntesis requiere integrar múltiples fuentes en un argumento coherente propio: es lo opuesto de la escritura de informes, que mantiene las fuentes separadas y etiquetadas, porque la síntesis fusiona perspectivas en una posición unificada que el escritor controla y de la que es responsable.

sentences.target: The risk in synthesis writing is the loss of individual source identity — the failure to make clear which idea came from which source — which is both an academic integrity failure and an argumentative failure, because sources carry different degrees of authority and the argument depends on knowing who is claiming what.
sentences.native: El riesgo en la escritura de síntesis es la pérdida de identidad de fuente individual, el fracaso en dejar claro qué idea vino de qué fuente, lo cual es tanto un fracaso de integridad académica como un fracaso argumentativo, porque las fuentes tienen diferentes grados de autoridad y el argumento depende de saber quién afirma qué.
sentences.en: The risk in synthesis writing is the loss of individual source identity — the failure to make clear which idea came from which source — which is both an academic integrity failure and an argumentative failure, because sources carry different degrees of authority and the argument depends on knowing who is claiming what.
sentences.es: El riesgo en la escritura de síntesis es la pérdida de identidad de fuente individual, el fracaso en dejar claro qué idea vino de qué fuente, lo cual es tanto un fracaso de integridad académica como un fracaso argumentativo, porque las fuentes tienen diferentes grados de autoridad y el argumento depende de saber quién afirma qué.

sentences.target: The most sophisticated synthesis does not merely integrate sources but evaluates them: it identifies where sources agree and where they conflict, explains why they differ, and uses that analysis to advance the writer's own position — a process that transforms source material into an argument rather than a collection.
sentences.native: La síntesis más sofisticada no meramente integra fuentes sino que las evalúa: identifica dónde las fuentes están de acuerdo y dónde entran en conflicto, explica por qué difieren y usa ese análisis para avanzar la posición propia del escritor, un proceso que transforma el material fuente en un argumento en lugar de una colección.
sentences.en: The most sophisticated synthesis does not merely integrate sources but evaluates them: it identifies where sources agree and where they conflict, explains why they differ, and uses that analysis to advance the writer's own position — a process that transforms source material into an argument rather than a collection.
sentences.es: La síntesis más sofisticada no meramente integra fuentes sino que las evalúa: identifica dónde las fuentes están de acuerdo y dónde entran en conflicto, explica por qué difieren y usa ese análisis para avanzar la posición propia del escritor, un proceso que transforma el material fuente en un argumento en lugar de una colección.

questions.q: How does the speaker distinguish a précis from a summary?
options: A précis is shorter than a summary because it compresses content more aggressively
A summary reports content while a précis reproduces the logical structure of the argument in compressed form
A précis includes the writer's evaluation while a summary restricts itself to reporting without comment
A summary can cover multiple texts while a précis is always derived from a single source text
questions.answer: A summary reports content while a précis reproduces the logical structure of the argument in compressed form

questions.q: What risk does the speaker identify as specific to synthesis writing?
options: The risk that the writer's own position will be obscured by the extensive integration of multiple source perspectives
The loss of individual source identity — failing to make clear which idea came from which source
The risk of over-citing sources in ways that interrupt the argumentative flow and undermine the writer's authority
The possibility that the sources selected will be too homogeneous to generate the tension needed for a strong synthesis
questions.answer: The loss of individual source identity — failing to make clear which idea came from which source

questions.q: What does the speaker say distinguishes the most sophisticated synthesis from basic integration?
options: Sophisticated synthesis includes sources from multiple disciplines rather than restricting itself to a single field
It evaluates sources — identifying agreements and conflicts, explaining differences, advancing the writer's own position
It produces a position that all sources would endorse rather than one that takes sides in the scholarly debate
It cites sources in footnotes rather than in the body text to maintain the fluency of the argumentative prose
questions.answer: It evaluates sources — identifying agreements and conflicts, explaining differences, advancing the writer's own position

sentences.target: Register conversion — the ability to take a text in one register and produce an appropriate version in another — is a key C2 competence: it requires not only knowledge of both registers but the ability to identify which features are register-specific and therefore must change rather than transfer.
sentences.native: La conversión de registro, la capacidad de tomar un texto en un registro y producir una versión apropiada en otro, es una competencia clave de C2: requiere no solo conocimiento de ambos registros sino la capacidad de identificar qué características son específicas del registro y por lo tanto deben cambiar en lugar de transferirse.
sentences.en: Register conversion — the ability to take a text in one register and produce an appropriate version in another — is a key C2 competence: it requires not only knowledge of both registers but the ability to identify which features are register-specific and therefore must change rather than transfer.
sentences.es: La conversión de registro, la capacidad de tomar un texto en un registro y producir una versión apropiada en otro, es una competencia clave de C2: requiere no solo conocimiento de ambos registros sino la capacidad de identificar qué características son específicas del registro y por lo tanto deben cambiar en lugar de transferirse.

sentences.target: Converting a scientific paper into a press release requires more than simplification: it requires identifying the claims that are genuinely newsworthy, finding analogies that bridge specialist and lay knowledge, and managing the tension between accuracy and accessibility that runs through all scientific communication.
sentences.native: Convertir un artículo científico en un comunicado de prensa requiere más que simplificación: requiere identificar las afirmaciones que son genuinamente noticiosas, encontrar analogías que cierren la brecha entre el conocimiento especialista y el profano, y gestionar la tensión entre precisión y accesibilidad que atraviesa toda la comunicación científica.
sentences.en: Converting a scientific paper into a press release requires more than simplification: it requires identifying the claims that are genuinely newsworthy, finding analogies that bridge specialist and lay knowledge, and managing the tension between accuracy and accessibility that runs through all scientific communication.
sentences.es: Convertir un artículo científico en un comunicado de prensa requiere más que simplificación: requiere identificar las afirmaciones que son genuinamente noticiosas, encontrar analogías que cierren la brecha entre el conocimiento especialista y el profano, y gestionar la tensión entre precisión y accesibilidad que atraviesa toda la comunicación científica.

sentences.target: Legal language to plain language conversion is a distinct challenge: legal language is not obscure for rhetorical reasons but functional ones — it is designed to be unambiguous in the specific technical sense, and the plain language version must preserve the precise legal meaning while making it accessible to non-lawyers.
sentences.native: La conversión del lenguaje legal al lenguaje llano es un desafío distinto: el lenguaje legal no es oscuro por razones retóricas sino funcionales, está diseñado para ser inequívoco en el sentido técnico específico, y la versión en lenguaje llano debe preservar el significado legal preciso mientras lo hace accesible a los no abogados.
sentences.en: Legal language to plain language conversion is a distinct challenge: legal language is not obscure for rhetorical reasons but functional ones — it is designed to be unambiguous in the specific technical sense, and the plain language version must preserve the precise legal meaning while making it accessible to non-lawyers.
sentences.es: La conversión del lenguaje legal al lenguaje llano es un desafío distinto: el lenguaje legal no es oscuro por razones retóricas sino funcionales, está diseñado para ser inequívoco en el sentido técnico específico, y la versión en lenguaje llano debe preservar el significado legal preciso mientras lo hace accesible a los no abogados.

sentences.target: The reverse conversion — from informal to formal — is equally demanding: producing a formal version of an informal email or a technical report based on a casual conversation requires not just applying formal vocabulary and grammar but adjusting the argumentative structure to meet the conventions of the target genre.
sentences.native: La conversión inversa, de informal a formal, es igualmente exigente: producir una versión formal de un correo electrónico informal o un informe técnico basado en una conversación casual requiere no solo aplicar vocabulario y gramática formales sino ajustar la estructura argumentativa para cumplir con las convenciones del género meta.
sentences.en: The reverse conversion — from informal to formal — is equally demanding: producing a formal version of an informal email or a technical report based on a casual conversation requires not just applying formal vocabulary and grammar but adjusting the argumentative structure to meet the conventions of the target genre.
sentences.es: La conversión inversa, de informal a formal, es igualmente exigente: producir una versión formal de un correo electrónico informal o un informe técnico basado en una conversación casual requiere no solo aplicar vocabulario y gramática formales sino ajustar la estructura argumentativa para cumplir con las convenciones del género meta.

sentences.target: The highest level of register conversion competence is the ability to convert without a source text: to produce a text in any target register on demand, from knowledge of what that register requires, rather than by translating an existing text — which is exactly what the expert communicator does when they draft a brief, compose an email, or deliver a talk.
sentences.native: El nivel más alto de competencia de conversión de registro es la capacidad de convertir sin un texto fuente: producir un texto en cualquier registro meta a demanda, desde el conocimiento de lo que ese registro requiere, en lugar de traducir un texto existente, lo cual es exactamente lo que hace el comunicador experto cuando redacta un informe, compone un correo electrónico o da una charla.
sentences.en: The highest level of register conversion competence is the ability to convert without a source text: to produce a text in any target register on demand, from knowledge of what that register requires, rather than by translating an existing text — which is exactly what the expert communicator does when they draft a brief, compose an email, or deliver a talk.
sentences.es: El nivel más alto de competencia de conversión de registro es la capacidad de convertir sin un texto fuente: producir un texto en cualquier registro meta a demanda, desde el conocimiento de lo que ese registro requiere, en lugar de traducir un texto existente, lo cual es exactamente lo que hace el comunicador experto cuando redacta un informe, compone un correo electrónico o da una charla.

questions.q: What does the speaker say register conversion requires beyond knowing both registers?
options: The ability to identify which features are audience-specific and therefore need to be adjusted for comprehension
The ability to identify which features are register-specific and must change rather than transfer between registers
Access to reference materials that document the conventions of both source and target registers
The ability to produce multiple versions for different audiences and then select the most appropriate one
questions.answer: The ability to identify which features are register-specific and must change rather than transfer between registers

questions.q: Why does the speaker say legal language is not obscure for rhetorical reasons?
options: Because legal language was designed in a historical period when obscurity was valued in professional writing
Because legal language is designed to be unambiguous in the technical sense — it has functional rather than rhetorical obscurity
Because legal professionals value precision over accessibility and have never considered plain language alternatives
Because ambiguity in legal language is sometimes strategically useful for the parties who drafted the document
questions.answer: Because legal language is designed to be unambiguous in the technical sense — it has functional rather than rhetorical obscurity

questions.q: What does the speaker describe as the highest level of register conversion competence?
options: The ability to convert any text into any target register within a time limit appropriate for professional communication
The ability to produce a text in any target register on demand from knowledge alone, without a source text to translate
The ability to evaluate which register is most appropriate for a given communicative situation and justify that choice
The ability to seamlessly switch registers within a single text to serve the needs of a diverse mixed audience
questions.answer: The ability to produce a text in any target register on demand from knowledge alone, without a source text to translate

sentences.target: Pragmatic competence is the ability to communicate what one means rather than only what one says: the sentence 'can you pass the salt?' does not request information about the hearer's physical capacity but requests the action itself — understanding this requires knowledge of how language functions in social context beyond its literal content.
sentences.native: La competencia pragmática es la capacidad de comunicar lo que uno quiere decir en lugar de solo lo que uno dice: la oración '¿puedes pasar la sal?' no solicita información sobre la capacidad física del oyente sino que solicita la acción en sí, entender esto requiere conocimiento de cómo funciona el lenguaje en el contexto social más allá de su contenido literal.
sentences.en: Pragmatic competence is the ability to communicate what one means rather than only what one says: the sentence 'can you pass the salt?' does not request information about the hearer's physical capacity but requests the action itself — understanding this requires knowledge of how language functions in social context beyond its literal content.
sentences.es: La competencia pragmática es la capacidad de comunicar lo que uno quiere decir en lugar de solo lo que uno dice: la oración '¿puedes pasar la sal?' no solicita información sobre la capacidad física del oyente sino que solicita la acción en sí, entender esto requiere conocimiento de cómo funciona el lenguaje en el contexto social más allá de su contenido literal.

sentences.target: Gricean implicature — the meaning that is conveyed by the violation of conversational maxims — is the mechanism by which much of what is communicated in conversation is communicated: when someone responds to 'how was the film?' with 'the special effects were impressive', they implicate that the rest of the film was not.
sentences.native: La implicatura griciana, el significado que se transmite por la violación de las máximas conversacionales, es el mecanismo por el cual gran parte de lo que se comunica en la conversación se comunica: cuando alguien responde a '¿cómo fue la película?' con 'los efectos especiales fueron impresionantes', implican que el resto de la película no lo fue.
sentences.en: Gricean implicature — the meaning that is conveyed by the violation of conversational maxims — is the mechanism by which much of what is communicated in conversation is communicated: when someone responds to 'how was the film?' with 'the special effects were impressive', they implicate that the rest of the film was not.
sentences.es: La implicatura griciana, el significado que se transmite por la violación de las máximas conversacionales, es el mecanismo por el cual gran parte de lo que se comunica en la conversación se comunica: cuando alguien responde a '¿cómo fue la película?' con 'los efectos especiales fueron impresionantes', implican que el resto de la película no lo fue.

sentences.target: The ability to generate precisely calibrated implicature — to say the right thing to convey exactly the intended inference without over-communication or under-communication — is among the highest pragmatic competencies: it requires simultaneous control of what is said, what is salient in context, and what the hearer can reasonably infer.
sentences.native: La capacidad de generar implicatura precisamente calibrada, decir lo correcto para transmitir exactamente la inferencia pretendida sin sobrecomunicación ni subcomunicación, está entre las competencias pragmáticas más altas: requiere control simultáneo de lo que se dice, lo que es saliente en contexto y lo que el oyente puede inferir razonablemente.
sentences.en: The ability to generate precisely calibrated implicature — to say the right thing to convey exactly the intended inference without over-communication or under-communication — is among the highest pragmatic competencies: it requires simultaneous control of what is said, what is salient in context, and what the hearer can reasonably infer.
sentences.es: La capacidad de generar implicatura precisamente calibrada, decir lo correcto para transmitir exactamente la inferencia pretendida sin sobrecomunicación ni subcomunicación, está entre las competencias pragmáticas más altas: requiere control simultáneo de lo que se dice, lo que es saliente en contexto y lo que el oyente puede inferir razonablemente.

sentences.target: Indirect speech acts — requests formulated as questions, apologies formulated as statements, criticisms delivered as observations — are not evasions but the conventional medium of polite interaction in many cultures: they allow speakers to pursue interactional goals while preserving the face of both parties.
sentences.native: Los actos de habla indirectos, solicitudes formuladas como preguntas, disculpas formuladas como afirmaciones, críticas entregadas como observaciones, no son evasiones sino el medio convencional de la interacción cortés en muchas culturas: permiten a los hablantes perseguir objetivos interaccionales mientras preservan la imagen de ambas partes.
sentences.en: Indirect speech acts — requests formulated as questions, apologies formulated as statements, criticisms delivered as observations — are not evasions but the conventional medium of polite interaction in many cultures: they allow speakers to pursue interactional goals while preserving the face of both parties.
sentences.es: Los actos de habla indirectos, solicitudes formuladas como preguntas, disculpas formuladas como afirmaciones, críticas entregadas como observaciones, no son evasiones sino el medio convencional de la interacción cortés en muchas culturas: permiten a los hablantes perseguir objetivos interaccionales mientras preservan la imagen de ambas partes.

sentences.target: The C2 speaker's pragmatic mastery is visible in precisely what does not happen: they do not over-explain or hedge unnecessarily; they do not take implicature too literally or too liberally; they do not mistime requests or commitments; they navigate the full range of speech acts with the effortless precision that marks full communicative competence.
sentences.native: El dominio pragmático del hablante de C2 es visible en precisamente lo que no ocurre: no sobre-explican ni hacen coberturas innecesarias; no toman la implicatura demasiado literal ni demasiado liberalmente; no hacen mal tiempo las solicitudes o compromisos; navegan el espectro completo de actos de habla con la precisión sin esfuerzo que marca la plena competencia comunicativa.
sentences.en: The C2 speaker's pragmatic mastery is visible in precisely what does not happen: they do not over-explain or hedge unnecessarily; they do not take implicature too literally or too liberally; they do not mistime requests or commitments; they navigate the full range of speech acts with the effortless precision that marks full communicative competence.
sentences.es: El dominio pragmático del hablante de C2 es visible en precisamente lo que no ocurre: no sobre-explican ni hacen coberturas innecesarias; no toman la implicatura demasiado literal ni demasiado liberalmente; no hacen mal tiempo las solicitudes o compromisos; navegan el espectro completo de actos de habla con la precisión sin esfuerzo que marca la plena competencia comunicativa.

questions.q: What does the film example illustrate about Gricean implicature?
options: That film reviews use a conventional format that audiences understand how to interpret correctly
That saying only 'the special effects were impressive' implicates that the rest of the film was not impressive
That conversational partners must share cultural knowledge about films to communicate effectively
That indirect communication is more appropriate in informal than in formal evaluative contexts
questions.answer: That saying only 'the special effects were impressive' implicates that the rest of the film was not impressive

questions.q: Why does the speaker say indirect speech acts are not evasions?
options: Because indirect speech acts are the most efficient way to communicate complex social and emotional content
Because they are the conventional medium of polite interaction — allowing interactional goals while preserving both parties' face
Because directness is culturally specific and what appears evasive in one culture is the norm in another
Because indirect speech acts have evolved because direct communication carries an inherently higher social risk
questions.answer: Because they are the conventional medium of polite interaction — allowing interactional goals while preserving both parties' face

questions.q: How does the speaker characterise C2 pragmatic mastery?
options: By the range of speech acts the speaker can perform — wider than at any lower level of proficiency
By precisely what does not happen — no over-explanation, no mistimed requests, effortless navigation of speech acts
By the speaker's ability to explain pragmatic rules of the language to non-native speakers clearly
By the sophistication of the implicature the speaker generates compared to C1 level speakers
questions.answer: By precisely what does not happen — no over-explanation, no mistimed requests, effortless navigation of speech acts

sentences.target: Cohesion and coherence are related but distinct properties of text: cohesion refers to the surface-level linking devices that connect sentences (pronouns, connectives, lexical chains), while coherence refers to the deep-level logical and conceptual unity that makes a text make sense as a whole rather than a sequence of disconnected statements.
sentences.native: La cohesión y la coherencia son propiedades relacionadas pero distintas del texto: la cohesión se refiere a los dispositivos de enlace a nivel de superficie que conectan oraciones (pronombres, conectivos, cadenas léxicas), mientras que la coherencia se refiere a la unidad lógica y conceptual a nivel profundo que hace que un texto tenga sentido como un todo en lugar de una secuencia de afirmaciones desconectadas.
sentences.en: Cohesion and coherence are related but distinct properties of text: cohesion refers to the surface-level linking devices that connect sentences (pronouns, connectives, lexical chains), while coherence refers to the deep-level logical and conceptual unity that makes a text make sense as a whole rather than a sequence of disconnected statements.
sentences.es: La cohesión y la coherencia son propiedades relacionadas pero distintas del texto: la cohesión se refiere a los dispositivos de enlace a nivel de superficie que conectan oraciones (pronombres, conectivos, cadenas léxicas), mientras que la coherencia se refiere a la unidad lógica y conceptual a nivel profundo que hace que un texto tenga sentido como un todo en lugar de una secuencia de afirmaciones desconectadas.

sentences.target: A text can be highly cohesive without being coherent: stringing together sentences connected by 'therefore', 'however', and 'consequently' does not guarantee logical progression — the connectives signal a logical relationship that the content may not actually instantiate.
sentences.native: Un texto puede ser muy cohesivo sin ser coherente: encadenar oraciones conectadas por 'por lo tanto', 'sin embargo' y 'en consecuencia' no garantiza progresión lógica; los conectivos señalan una relación lógica que el contenido puede no instanciar realmente.
sentences.en: A text can be highly cohesive without being coherent: stringing together sentences connected by 'therefore', 'however', and 'consequently' does not guarantee logical progression — the connectives signal a logical relationship that the content may not actually instantiate.
sentences.es: Un texto puede ser muy cohesivo sin ser coherente: encadenar oraciones conectadas por 'por lo tanto', 'sin embargo' y 'en consecuencia' no garantiza progresión lógica; los conectivos señalan una relación lógica que el contenido puede no instanciar realmente.

sentences.target: The topic sentence — the claim that governs a paragraph's content — is the primary instrument of paragraph-level coherence: when the topic sentence is absent, vague, or inconsistent with the paragraph's actual content, the paragraph becomes an undirected collection of related thoughts rather than a purposeful contribution to the argument.
sentences.native: La oración temática, la afirmación que gobierna el contenido de un párrafo, es el instrumento principal de la coherencia a nivel de párrafo: cuando la oración temática está ausente, es vaga o es inconsistente con el contenido real del párrafo, el párrafo se convierte en una colección sin dirección de pensamientos relacionados en lugar de una contribución con propósito al argumento.
sentences.en: The topic sentence — the claim that governs a paragraph's content — is the primary instrument of paragraph-level coherence: when the topic sentence is absent, vague, or inconsistent with the paragraph's actual content, the paragraph becomes an undirected collection of related thoughts rather than a purposeful contribution to the argument.
sentences.es: La oración temática, la afirmación que gobierna el contenido de un párrafo, es el instrumento principal de la coherencia a nivel de párrafo: cuando la oración temática está ausente, es vaga o es inconsistente con el contenido real del párrafo, el párrafo se convierte en una colección sin dirección de pensamientos relacionados en lugar de una contribución con propósito al argumento.

sentences.target: Discourse markers serve different functions at different scales: at the sentence level they signal syntactic relationships; at the paragraph level they signal argumentative moves; at the text level they signal the discourse structure — understanding which markers operate at which level is essential for producing and comprehending text coherently.
sentences.native: Los marcadores del discurso sirven diferentes funciones en diferentes escalas: a nivel de oración señalan relaciones sintácticas; a nivel de párrafo señalan movimientos argumentativos; a nivel de texto señalan la estructura del discurso; comprender qué marcadores operan a qué nivel es esencial para producir y comprender texto coherentemente.
sentences.en: Discourse markers serve different functions at different scales: at the sentence level they signal syntactic relationships; at the paragraph level they signal argumentative moves; at the text level they signal the discourse structure — understanding which markers operate at which level is essential for producing and comprehending text coherently.
sentences.es: Los marcadores del discurso sirven diferentes funciones en diferentes escalas: a nivel de oración señalan relaciones sintácticas; a nivel de párrafo señalan movimientos argumentativos; a nivel de texto señalan la estructura del discurso; comprender qué marcadores operan a qué nivel es esencial para producir y comprender texto coherentemente.

sentences.target: The advanced writer's management of information structure — which information is given and which is new, what is foregrounded and what is backgrounded, how the thematic progression is managed across the whole text — is the dimension of writing competence that most consistently separates C2 from C1 performance.
sentences.native: El manejo de la estructura informativa por parte del escritor avanzado, qué información es dada y cuál es nueva, qué está en primer plano y qué está en segundo plano, cómo se gestiona la progresión temática a través de todo el texto, es la dimensión de la competencia de escritura que más consistentemente separa el desempeño de C2 del de C1.
sentences.en: The advanced writer's management of information structure — which information is given and which is new, what is foregrounded and what is backgrounded, how the thematic progression is managed across the whole text — is the dimension of writing competence that most consistently separates C2 from C1 performance.
sentences.es: El manejo de la estructura informativa por parte del escritor avanzado, qué información es dada y cuál es nueva, qué está en primer plano y qué está en segundo plano, cómo se gestiona la progresión temática a través de todo el texto, es la dimensión de la competencia de escritura que más consistentemente separa el desempeño de C2 del de C1.

questions.q: How does the speaker distinguish cohesion from coherence?
options: Cohesion is a property of spoken language while coherence is a property of written language
Cohesion is surface-level linking devices while coherence is deep-level logical and conceptual unity
Cohesion requires active reader construction while coherence is encoded in the text itself by the writer
Cohesion refers to the accuracy of individual sentences while coherence refers to the overall argument quality
questions.answer: Cohesion is surface-level linking devices while coherence is deep-level logical and conceptual unity

questions.q: What does the speaker say can be highly cohesive without being coherent?
options: An academic essay that follows all the formal conventions but fails to make a clear central argument
A text with sentences connected by 'therefore', 'however', 'consequently' where the content does not instantiate the logic
A speech that uses all the appropriate discourse markers but fails to adapt to the needs of the audience
A paragraph where all sentences relate to the same topic but use different and incompatible vocabulary registers
questions.answer: A text with sentences connected by 'therefore', 'however', 'consequently' where the content does not instantiate the logic

questions.q: What does the speaker identify as most consistently separating C2 from C1 writing performance?
options: The range of grammatical structures correctly deployed across different text types and genres
Management of information structure — given/new, foregrounded/backgrounded, thematic progression across the whole text
The ability to sustain a complex argument across a text of sufficient length for academic or professional purposes
Control of vocabulary range and precision — the ability to choose the exact word for each communicative function
questions.answer: Management of information structure — given/new, foregrounded/backgrounded, thematic progression across the whole text

sentences.target: Intercultural communicative competence is not the ability to know everything about every culture — an impossible goal — but the disposition to recognise that one's own cultural frameworks are not universal, to attend to cultural difference with curiosity rather than judgement, and to adapt communicative behaviour accordingly.
sentences.native: La competencia comunicativa intercultural no es la capacidad de saber todo sobre cada cultura, un objetivo imposible, sino la disposición a reconocer que los propios marcos culturales no son universales, a atender la diferencia cultural con curiosidad en lugar de juicio, y a adaptar el comportamiento comunicativo en consecuencia.
sentences.en: Intercultural communicative competence is not the ability to know everything about every culture — an impossible goal — but the disposition to recognise that one's own cultural frameworks are not universal, to attend to cultural difference with curiosity rather than judgement, and to adapt communicative behaviour accordingly.
sentences.es: La competencia comunicativa intercultural no es la capacidad de saber todo sobre cada cultura, un objetivo imposible, sino la disposición a reconocer que los propios marcos culturales no son universales, a atender la diferencia cultural con curiosidad en lugar de juicio, y a adaptar el comportamiento comunicativo en consecuencia.

sentences.target: High-context and low-context cultures differ systematically in how much meaning is carried by explicit verbal content versus contextual and non-verbal signals: a low-context communicator who states everything explicitly may appear blunt or arrogant to a high-context interlocutor, while a high-context communicator who relies on context may appear evasive or unclear to a low-context one.
sentences.native: Las culturas de alto contexto y bajo contexto difieren sistemáticamente en cuánto significado es llevado por el contenido verbal explícito versus las señales contextuales y no verbales: un comunicador de bajo contexto que establece todo explícitamente puede parecer brusco o arrogante para un interlocutor de alto contexto, mientras que un comunicador de alto contexto que depende del contexto puede parecer evasivo o poco claro para uno de bajo contexto.
sentences.en: High-context and low-context cultures differ systematically in how much meaning is carried by explicit verbal content versus contextual and non-verbal signals: a low-context communicator who states everything explicitly may appear blunt or arrogant to a high-context interlocutor, while a high-context communicator who relies on context may appear evasive or unclear to a low-context one.
sentences.es: Las culturas de alto contexto y bajo contexto difieren sistemáticamente en cuánto significado es llevado por el contenido verbal explícito versus las señales contextuales y no verbales: un comunicador de bajo contexto que establece todo explícitamente puede parecer brusco o arrogante para un interlocutor de alto contexto, mientras que un comunicador de alto contexto que depende del contexto puede parecer evasivo o poco claro para uno de bajo contexto.

sentences.target: The assumption that communicative norms are universal is one of the most common sources of intercultural misunderstanding: practices around turn-taking, silence, directness, formality, and the use of humour vary enormously across cultures in ways that are largely invisible to members of the cultures that practise them.
sentences.native: El supuesto de que las normas comunicativas son universales es una de las fuentes más comunes de malentendido intercultural: las prácticas en torno a la toma de turnos, el silencio, la franqueza, la formalidad y el uso del humor varían enormemente entre culturas de maneras que son en gran medida invisibles para los miembros de las culturas que las practican.
sentences.en: The assumption that communicative norms are universal is one of the most common sources of intercultural misunderstanding: practices around turn-taking, silence, directness, formality, and the use of humour vary enormously across cultures in ways that are largely invisible to members of the cultures that practise them.
sentences.es: El supuesto de que las normas comunicativas son universales es una de las fuentes más comunes de malentendido intercultural: las prácticas en torno a la toma de turnos, el silencio, la franqueza, la formalidad y el uso del humor varían enormemente entre culturas de maneras que son en gran medida invisibles para los miembros de las culturas que las practican.

sentences.target: The intercultural mediator's task is to make visible what each party's cultural background renders invisible: to name the different assumptions about communication that are generating misunderstanding without privileging either cultural framework as more correct or rational.
sentences.native: La tarea del mediador intercultural es hacer visible lo que el trasfondo cultural de cada parte hace invisible: nombrar los diferentes supuestos sobre la comunicación que están generando malentendidos sin privilegiar ningún marco cultural como más correcto o racional.
sentences.en: The intercultural mediator's task is to make visible what each party's cultural background renders invisible: to name the different assumptions about communication that are generating misunderstanding without privileging either cultural framework as more correct or rational.
sentences.es: La tarea del mediador intercultural es hacer visible lo que el trasfondo cultural de cada parte hace invisible: nombrar los diferentes supuestos sobre la comunicación que están generando malentendidos sin privilegiar ningún marco cultural como más correcto o racional.

sentences.target: Full intercultural competence does not mean becoming culturally neutral: it means acquiring the flexibility to move between cultural frameworks while remaining grounded in one's own — a kind of communicative bilingualism that allows the speaker to inhabit different cultural modes while knowing which mode they are in.
sentences.native: La plena competencia intercultural no significa volverse culturalmente neutral: significa adquirir la flexibilidad para moverse entre marcos culturales mientras se permanece enraizado en el propio, una especie de bilingüismo comunicativo que permite al hablante habitar diferentes modos culturales mientras sabe en qué modo está.
sentences.en: Full intercultural competence does not mean becoming culturally neutral: it means acquiring the flexibility to move between cultural frameworks while remaining grounded in one's own — a kind of communicative bilingualism that allows the speaker to inhabit different cultural modes while knowing which mode they are in.
sentences.es: La plena competencia intercultural no significa volverse culturalmente neutral: significa adquirir la flexibilidad para moverse entre marcos culturales mientras se permanece enraizado en el propio, una especie de bilingüismo comunicativo que permite al hablante habitar diferentes modos culturales mientras sabe en qué modo está.

questions.q: How does the speaker define intercultural communicative competence?
options: The ability to know everything about all cultures one is likely to encounter in professional communication
The disposition to recognise one's frameworks are not universal, attend to difference with curiosity, and adapt accordingly
The ability to communicate equally effectively in any cultural context without adjusting one's communicative style
The knowledge of which cultural norms are most widely shared and therefore safest to apply across different contexts
questions.answer: The disposition to recognise one's frameworks are not universal, attend to difference with curiosity, and adapt accordingly

questions.q: What does the speaker say a low-context communicator risks in interactions with high-context interlocutors?
options: Being misunderstood because they fail to use the contextual signals that high-context interlocutors depend on
Appearing blunt or arrogant because high-context interlocutors read explicit statement as a violation of relational norms
Being perceived as uninformed because they lack knowledge of the contextual information the high-context speaker assumes
Generating conflict because explicit direct communication activates defensive responses in high-context communicators
questions.answer: Appearing blunt or arrogant because high-context interlocutors read explicit statement as a violation of relational norms

questions.q: What does the speaker say full intercultural competence does NOT mean?
options: It does not mean mastering the specific cultural conventions of every culture one encounters in professional life
It does not mean becoming culturally neutral — it means moving between frameworks while remaining grounded in one's own
It does not mean abandoning cultural self-awareness in favour of a context-dependent approach to every new situation
It does not mean accepting all cultural practices as equally valid regardless of their ethical implications
questions.answer: It does not mean becoming culturally neutral — it means moving between frameworks while remaining grounded in one's own

audios.title: Style, Voice, and the Writer's Identity

sentences.target: Style is not the decoration applied to content after the content has been determined: style and content co-emerge, and a change in style is always a change in what is said, not merely in how it is said — the same proposition expressed with irony, with gravity, or with urgency is not the same proposition.
sentences.native: El estilo no es la decoración aplicada al contenido después de que el contenido ha sido determinado: el estilo y el contenido co-emergen, y un cambio de estilo es siempre un cambio en lo que se dice, no meramente en cómo se dice; la misma proposición expresada con ironía, con gravedad o con urgencia no es la misma proposición.
sentences.en: Style is not the decoration applied to content after the content has been determined: style and content co-emerge, and a change in style is always a change in what is said, not merely in how it is said — the same proposition expressed with irony, with gravity, or with urgency is not the same proposition.

sentences.target: The concept of voice in writing refers to the distinctive personality that emerges from a writer's consistent choices across many dimensions — sentence length, diction level, use of metaphor, rhythm, attitude toward the reader — and it is this consistency of choice that readers experience as the writer's presence.
sentences.native: El concepto de voz en la escritura se refiere a la personalidad distintiva que emerge de las elecciones consistentes de un escritor en muchas dimensiones: longitud de oración, nivel de dicción, uso de metáfora, ritmo, actitud hacia el lector; y es esta consistencia de elección lo que los lectores experimentan como la presencia del escritor.
sentences.en: The concept of voice in writing refers to the distinctive personality that emerges from a writer's consistent choices across many dimensions — sentence length, diction level, use of metaphor, rhythm, attitude toward the reader — and it is this consistency of choice that readers experience as the writer's presence.
sentences.es: El concepto de voz en la escritura se refiere a la personalidad distintiva que emerge de las elecciones consistentes de un escritor en muchas dimensiones: longitud de oración, nivel de dicción, uso de metáfora, ritmo, actitud hacia el lector; y es esta consistencia de elección lo que los lectores experimentan como la presencia del escritor.

sentences.target: Voice is not the same as personality: a writer can construct a public voice that differs from their private personality, can sustain multiple voices for different genres and audiences, and can strategically suppress personal voice to achieve the apparently objective tone of academic or technical writing.
sentences.native: La voz no es lo mismo que la personalidad: un escritor puede construir una voz pública que difiere de su personalidad privada, puede sostener múltiples voces para diferentes géneros y públicos, y puede suprimir estratégicamente la voz personal para lograr el tono aparentemente objetivo de la escritura académica o técnica.
sentences.en: Voice is not the same as personality: a writer can construct a public voice that differs from their private personality, can sustain multiple voices for different genres and audiences, and can strategically suppress personal voice to achieve the apparently objective tone of academic or technical writing.
sentences.es: La voz no es lo mismo que la personalidad: un escritor puede construir una voz pública que difiere de su personalidad privada, puede sostener múltiples voces para diferentes géneros y públicos, y puede suprimir estratégicamente la voz personal para lograr el tono aparentemente objetivo de la escritura académica o técnica.

sentences.target: The tension between personal voice and genre convention is one of the most productive in writing: the most memorable writing often emerges from the friction between a distinctive individual voice and the demands of a conventional form — the sonnet, the legal brief, the academic paper — rather than from a comfortable alignment with conventions.
sentences.native: La tensión entre la voz personal y la convención de género es una de las más productivas en la escritura: la escritura más memorable a menudo emerge del roce entre una voz individual distintiva y las exigencias de una forma convencional, el soneto, el escrito legal, el artículo académico, en lugar de una cómoda alineación con las convenciones.
sentences.en: The tension between personal voice and genre convention is one of the most productive in writing: the most memorable writing often emerges from the friction between a distinctive individual voice and the demands of a conventional form — the sonnet, the legal brief, the academic paper — rather than from a comfortable alignment with conventions.
sentences.es: La tensión entre la voz personal y la convención de género es una de las más productivas en la escritura: la escritura más memorable a menudo emerge del roce entre una voz individual distintiva y las exigencias de una forma convencional, el soneto, el escrito legal, el artículo académico, en lugar de una cómoda alineación con las convenciones.

sentences.target: Acquiring a style in a second language is one of the last achievements of full proficiency: it requires sufficient control of the target language to make consistent choices that feel natural rather than laboured, and sufficient knowledge of the target language's stylistic traditions to understand what one is departing from and why.
sentences.native: Adquirir un estilo en una segunda lengua es uno de los últimos logros de la plena competencia: requiere suficiente control del idioma meta para hacer elecciones consistentes que se sientan naturales en lugar de trabajosas, y suficiente conocimiento de las tradiciones estilísticas del idioma meta para entender de qué se está apartando y por qué.
sentences.en: Acquiring a style in a second language is one of the last achievements of full proficiency: it requires sufficient control of the target language to make consistent choices that feel natural rather than laboured, and sufficient knowledge of the target language's stylistic traditions to understand what one is departing from and why.
sentences.es: Adquirir un estilo en una segunda lengua es uno de los últimos logros de la plena competencia: requiere suficiente control del idioma meta para hacer elecciones consistentes que se sientan naturales en lugar de trabajosas, y suficiente conocimiento de las tradiciones estilísticas del idioma meta para entender de qué se está apartando y por qué.

questions.q: What does the speaker say about the relationship between style and content?
options: Style is a secondary property that communicates attitude while content communicates information
Style and content co-emerge — a change in style is always a change in what is said, not merely how it is said
Good style makes content more persuasive but does not change the proposition being advanced
Style is the aspect of writing that the writer controls while content is determined by the requirements of the genre
questions.answer: Style and content co-emerge — a change in style is always a change in what is said, not merely how it is said

questions.q: How does the speaker say voice differs from personality in writing?
options: Voice is shaped by the audience's expectations while personality is an intrinsic property of the writer
A writer can construct a voice differing from private personality, sustain multiple voices, or suppress voice entirely
Voice is consistent across all a writer's texts while personality varies depending on context and mood
Voice is a property of published writing while personality is expressed only in personal correspondence and diaries
questions.answer: A writer can construct a voice differing from private personality, sustain multiple voices, or suppress voice entirely

questions.q: Why does the speaker say acquiring a style in a second language is among the last achievements of full proficiency?
options: Because style requires the kind of historical and cultural knowledge that takes many years of immersion to acquire
Because it requires control for natural-feeling consistent choices AND knowledge of stylistic traditions to know what one departs from
Because stylistic choices are unconscious in the first language but must be made consciously in a second language
Because second language writers always feel more constrained by convention than first language writers due to lower risk tolerance
questions.answer: Because it requires control for natural-feeling consistent choices AND knowledge of stylistic traditions to know what one departs from

audios.title: Critical Reading at the Highest Level

sentences.target: Critical reading at C2 level is not scepticism for its own sake but a systematic method for evaluating what a text is doing, how it is doing it, and whether it does it well: it requires simultaneously engaging with the content, evaluating the argumentation, and attending to the rhetorical and stylistic choices that shape how content is presented.
sentences.native: La lectura crítica a nivel C2 no es escepticismo por sí mismo sino un método sistemático para evaluar qué está haciendo un texto, cómo lo está haciendo y si lo hace bien: requiere simultáneamente involucrarse con el contenido, evaluar la argumentación y atender a las elecciones retóricas y estilísticas que moldean cómo se presenta el contenido.
sentences.en: Critical reading at C2 level is not scepticism for its own sake but a systematic method for evaluating what a text is doing, how it is doing it, and whether it does it well: it requires simultaneously engaging with the content, evaluating the argumentation, and attending to the rhetorical and stylistic choices that shape how content is presented.
sentences.es: La lectura crítica a nivel C2 no es escepticismo por sí mismo sino un método sistemático para evaluar qué está haciendo un texto, cómo lo está haciendo y si lo hace bien: requiere simultáneamente involucrarse con el contenido, evaluar la argumentación y atender a las elecciones retóricas y estilísticas que moldean cómo se presenta el contenido.

sentences.target: The critical reader asks not only 'what does this text claim?' but 'what does it assume?', 'what does it exclude?', 'what interests does it serve?', and 'what would a reader who disagreed with its assumptions make of this text?' — questions that situate the text within its ideological and social context.
sentences.native: El lector crítico no pregunta solo '¿qué afirma este texto?' sino '¿qué asume?', '¿qué excluye?', '¿qué intereses sirve?' y '¿qué haría de este texto un lector que no estuviera de acuerdo con sus supuestos?', preguntas que sitúan el texto dentro de su contexto ideológico y social.
sentences.en: The critical reader asks not only 'what does this text claim?' but 'what does it assume?', 'what does it exclude?', 'what interests does it serve?', and 'what would a reader who disagreed with its assumptions make of this text?' — questions that situate the text within its ideological and social context.
sentences.es: El lector crítico no pregunta solo '¿qué afirma este texto?' sino '¿qué asume?', '¿qué excluye?', '¿qué intereses sirve?' y '¿qué haría de este texto un lector que no estuviera de acuerdo con sus supuestos?', preguntas que sitúan el texto dentro de su contexto ideológico y social.

sentences.target: The distinction between argument and evidence is central to critical reading: evidence is what a text offers in support of its claims; the critical reader evaluates whether the evidence is relevant, sufficient, representative, and whether the inference from evidence to claim is valid or involves an unjustified leap.
sentences.native: La distinción entre argumento y evidencia es central para la lectura crítica: la evidencia es lo que un texto ofrece en apoyo de sus afirmaciones; el lector crítico evalúa si la evidencia es relevante, suficiente, representativa, y si la inferencia de la evidencia a la afirmación es válida o involucra un salto injustificado.
sentences.en: The distinction between argument and evidence is central to critical reading: evidence is what a text offers in support of its claims; the critical reader evaluates whether the evidence is relevant, sufficient, representative, and whether the inference from evidence to claim is valid or involves an unjustified leap.
sentences.es: La distinción entre argumento y evidencia es central para la lectura crítica: la evidencia es lo que un texto ofrece en apoyo de sus afirmaciones; el lector crítico evalúa si la evidencia es relevante, suficiente, representativa, y si la inferencia de la evidencia a la afirmación es válida o involucra un salto injustificado.

sentences.target: Identifying the implied reader — the reader the text constructs and addresses through its diction, its assumptions, and its argumentative choices — is a key tool of critical reading: texts that address 'we all know that...' are constructing an implied reader who shares certain assumptions and implicitly excluding readers who do not.
sentences.native: Identificar al lector implícito, el lector que el texto construye y dirige a través de su dicción, sus supuestos y sus elecciones argumentativas, es una herramienta clave de la lectura crítica: los textos que se dirigen con 'todos sabemos que...' están construyendo un lector implícito que comparte ciertos supuestos y excluyendo implícitamente a los lectores que no los comparten.
sentences.en: Identifying the implied reader — the reader the text constructs and addresses through its diction, its assumptions, and its argumentative choices — is a key tool of critical reading: texts that address 'we all know that...' are constructing an implied reader who shares certain assumptions and implicitly excluding readers who do not.
sentences.es: Identificar al lector implícito, el lector que el texto construye y dirige a través de su dicción, sus supuestos y sus elecciones argumentativas, es una herramienta clave de la lectura crítica: los textos que se dirigen con 'todos sabemos que...' están construyendo un lector implícito que comparte ciertos supuestos y excluyendo implícitamente a los lectores que no los comparten.

sentences.target: The charitable reading — the practice of engaging with the strongest possible version of an argument before criticising it — is not a concession to texts one disagrees with but an epistemically necessary practice: criticising a weak or misrepresented version of a position demonstrates nothing about the position's actual merits.
sentences.native: La lectura caritativa, la práctica de involucrarse con la versión más fuerte posible de un argumento antes de criticarlo, no es una concesión a los textos con los que uno no está de acuerdo sino una práctica epistémicamente necesaria: criticar una versión débil o mal representada de una posición no demuestra nada sobre los méritos reales de la posición.
sentences.en: The charitable reading — the practice of engaging with the strongest possible version of an argument before criticising it — is not a concession to texts one disagrees with but an epistemically necessary practice: criticising a weak or misrepresented version of a position demonstrates nothing about the position's actual merits.
sentences.es: La lectura caritativa, la práctica de involucrarse con la versión más fuerte posible de un argumento antes de criticarlo, no es una concesión a los textos con los que uno no está de acuerdo sino una práctica epistémicamente necesaria: criticar una versión débil o mal representada de una posición no demuestra nada sobre los méritos reales de la posición.

questions.q: What questions does the speaker say the critical reader asks beyond 'what does this text claim'?
options: What are the text's sources, when was it written, and who funded the research it reports
What does it assume, what does it exclude, what interests does it serve, and what would a disagreeing reader make of it
What is the text's genre, who is its intended audience, and what purpose was it produced to serve
What evidence does it cite, how does it treat counter-evidence, and does it acknowledge its own limitations honestly
questions.answer: What does it assume, what does it exclude, what interests does it serve, and what would a disagreeing reader make of it

questions.q: What does the speaker say the implied reader tool reveals about 'we all know that...' constructions?
options: They establish shared knowledge claims that readers are invited to evaluate against their own experience
They construct an implied reader who shares certain assumptions and implicitly exclude readers who do not
They signal that the following claim is so well established that citation is unnecessary and its omission is acceptable
They create a false sense of consensus that is a form of rhetorical manipulation equivalent to an appeal to authority
questions.answer: They construct an implied reader who shares certain assumptions and implicitly exclude readers who do not

questions.q: Why does the speaker say the charitable reading is epistemically necessary rather than a concession?
options: Because engaging charitably with an argument demonstrates intellectual open-mindedness that is socially valued
Because criticising a weak or misrepresented version of a position demonstrates nothing about its actual merits
Because charitable reading allows critics to find points of agreement that might otherwise be obscured by disagreement
Because the strongest version of an argument is always the most widely held and therefore the most important to address
questions.answer: Because criticising a weak or misrepresented version of a position demonstrates nothing about its actual merits

sentences.target: Language mastery is not a static achievement but a dynamic relationship: the speaker who has reached C2 level has not finished learning the language but has reached the point where the learning is self-sustaining — every conversation, text, and encounter enriches the linguistic resource rather than depleting the learner's attention and energy.
sentences.native: El dominio del lenguaje no es un logro estático sino una relación dinámica: el hablante que ha alcanzado el nivel C2 no ha terminado de aprender el idioma sino que ha llegado al punto donde el aprendizaje es autosustentable; cada conversación, texto y encuentro enriquece el recurso lingüístico en lugar de agotar la atención y energía del aprendiz.
sentences.en: Language mastery is not a static achievement but a dynamic relationship: the speaker who has reached C2 level has not finished learning the language but has reached the point where the learning is self-sustaining — every conversation, text, and encounter enriches the linguistic resource rather than depleting the learner's attention and energy.
sentences.es: El dominio del lenguaje no es un logro estático sino una relación dinámica: el hablante que ha alcanzado el nivel C2 no ha terminado de aprender el idioma sino que ha llegado al punto donde el aprendizaje es autosustentable; cada conversación, texto y encuentro enriquece el recurso lingüístico en lugar de agotar la atención y energía del aprendiz.

sentences.target: The phenomenology of mastery is characterised by transparency: the language no longer feels like a medium through which thought must be laboriously translated but becomes the thought itself — native speakers do not first think in an inner code and then translate; they think in the language, and the C2 speaker begins to share this experience.
sentences.native: La fenomenología del dominio se caracteriza por la transparencia: el idioma ya no se siente como un medio a través del cual el pensamiento debe ser laboriosamente traducido sino que se convierte en el pensamiento mismo; los hablantes nativos no piensan primero en un código interno y luego traducen; piensan en el idioma, y el hablante de C2 comienza a compartir esta experiencia.
sentences.en: The phenomenology of mastery is characterised by transparency: the language no longer feels like a medium through which thought must be laboriously translated but becomes the thought itself — native speakers do not first think in an inner code and then translate; they think in the language, and the C2 speaker begins to share this experience.
sentences.es: La fenomenología del dominio se caracteriza por la transparencia: el idioma ya no se siente como un medio a través del cual el pensamiento debe ser laboriosamente traducido sino que se convierte en el pensamiento mismo; los hablantes nativos no piensan primero en un código interno y luego traducen; piensan en el idioma, y el hablante de C2 comienza a compartir esta experiencia.

sentences.target: The C2 speaker notices things about the language that lower-proficiency speakers cannot: the slight register unevenness in a text, the collocational strain in a phrase, the irony that depends on a cultural reference, the word that is technically correct but pragmatically wrong — all of this becomes available as a resource for both production and appreciation.
sentences.native: El hablante de C2 nota cosas sobre el idioma que los hablantes de menor competencia no pueden: el ligero desequilibrio de registro en un texto, la tensión colocacional en una frase, la ironía que depende de una referencia cultural, la palabra que es técnicamente correcta pero pragmáticamente incorrecta; todo esto se vuelve disponible como recurso tanto para la producción como para la apreciación.
sentences.en: The C2 speaker notices things about the language that lower-proficiency speakers cannot: the slight register unevenness in a text, the collocational strain in a phrase, the irony that depends on a cultural reference, the word that is technically correct but pragmatically wrong — all of this becomes available as a resource for both production and appreciation.
sentences.es: El hablante de C2 nota cosas sobre el idioma que los hablantes de menor competencia no pueden: el ligero desequilibrio de registro en un texto, la tensión colocacional en una frase, la ironía que depende de una referencia cultural, la palabra que es técnicamente correcta pero pragmáticamente incorrecta; todo esto se vuelve disponible como recurso tanto para la producción como para la apreciación.

sentences.target: Mastery includes the mastery of one's own gaps: the C2 speaker knows what they do not know, can identify where their knowledge becomes uncertain, and has the metacognitive resources to manage uncertainty in communication — to hedge appropriately, to ask for clarification without losing authority, to acknowledge limitation without appearing incompetent.
sentences.native: El dominio incluye el dominio de las propias brechas: el hablante de C2 sabe lo que no sabe, puede identificar dónde su conocimiento se vuelve incierto, y tiene los recursos metacognitivos para gestionar la incertidumbre en la comunicación; para cubrir apropiadamente, para pedir aclaraciones sin perder autoridad, para reconocer las limitaciones sin parecer incompetente.
sentences.en: Mastery includes the mastery of one's own gaps: the C2 speaker knows what they do not know, can identify where their knowledge becomes uncertain, and has the metacognitive resources to manage uncertainty in communication — to hedge appropriately, to ask for clarification without losing authority, to acknowledge limitation without appearing incompetent.
sentences.es: El dominio incluye el dominio de las propias brechas: el hablante de C2 sabe lo que no sabe, puede identificar dónde su conocimiento se vuelve incierto, y tiene los recursos metacognitivos para gestionar la incertidumbre en la comunicación; para cubrir apropiadamente, para pedir aclaraciones sin perder autoridad, para reconocer las limitaciones sin parecer incompetente.

sentences.target: The deepest level of language mastery is when the language becomes a source of pleasure — when the apt phrase, the precisely calibrated irony, the elegantly constructed sentence, and the perfectly chosen word give the speaker or writer the same satisfaction that a craftsperson takes in the thing made well.
sentences.native: El nivel más profundo del dominio del lenguaje es cuando el idioma se convierte en una fuente de placer; cuando la frase apropiada, la ironía precisamente calibrada, la oración elegantemente construida y la palabra perfectamente elegida dan al hablante o escritor la misma satisfacción que un artesano obtiene del objeto bien hecho.
sentences.en: The deepest level of language mastery is when the language becomes a source of pleasure — when the apt phrase, the precisely calibrated irony, the elegantly constructed sentence, and the perfectly chosen word give the speaker or writer the same satisfaction that a craftsperson takes in the thing made well.
sentences.es: El nivel más profundo del dominio del lenguaje es cuando el idioma se convierte en una fuente de placer; cuando la frase apropiada, la ironía precisamente calibrada, la oración elegantemente construida y la palabra perfectamente elegida dan al hablante o escritor la misma satisfacción que un artesano obtiene del objeto bien hecho.

questions.q: What does the speaker say characterises the phenomenology of language mastery?
options: The ability to perform all language tasks without error and to recognise and correct errors in others' production
Transparency — the language no longer feels like a medium to translate through but becomes the thought itself
The experience of having identical emotional responses to L1 and L2 content, indicating complete equivalence
The point at which the speaker no longer needs to monitor their production because accuracy has become automatic
questions.answer: Transparency — the language no longer feels like a medium to translate through but becomes the thought itself

questions.q: What does the speaker say mastery of one's own gaps involves?
options: Knowing which areas of the language require continued study and directing learning effort accordingly
Knowing what one does not know, identifying uncertainty, and having metacognitive resources to manage it in communication
Accepting that all speakers have gaps and that communicative success does not require complete knowledge
The ability to disguise gaps in knowledge so effectively that interlocutors cannot identify areas of uncertainty
questions.answer: Knowing what one does not know, identifying uncertainty, and having metacognitive resources to manage it in communication

questions.q: How does the speaker describe the deepest level of language mastery?
options: When the speaker can operate across all registers and genres without preparation or effort
When the language becomes a source of pleasure — the apt phrase and perfectly chosen word give craftsperson-like satisfaction
When the speaker's production is indistinguishable from that of a highly educated native speaker of the language
When the speaker can reflect on and explain the language's structure as fluently as they can use it in communication
questions.answer: When the language becomes a source of pleasure — the apt phrase and perfectly chosen word give craftsperson-like satisfaction

audios.title: The Language Learning Journey: From A1 to C2

sentences.target: The journey from A1 to C2 is not a single trajectory but a series of qualitative transformations: the A1 learner is mastering the code; the B1 learner is mastering communication; the C1 learner is mastering nuance; the C2 learner is mastering the full range of the language's expressive possibilities.
sentences.native: El viaje de A1 a C2 no es una trayectoria única sino una serie de transformaciones cualitativas: el aprendiz de A1 está dominando el código; el de B1 está dominando la comunicación; el de C1 está dominando el matiz; el de C2 está dominando todo el rango de las posibilidades expresivas del idioma.
sentences.en: The journey from A1 to C2 is not a single trajectory but a series of qualitative transformations: the A1 learner is mastering the code; the B1 learner is mastering communication; the C1 learner is mastering nuance; the C2 learner is mastering the full range of the language's expressive possibilities.
sentences.es: El viaje de A1 a C2 no es una trayectoria única sino una serie de transformaciones cualitativas: el aprendiz de A1 está dominando el código; el de B1 está dominando la comunicación; el de C1 está dominando el matiz; el de C2 está dominando todo el rango de las posibilidades expresivas del idioma.

sentences.target: What changes most profoundly across the levels is not vocabulary size or grammar accuracy — though both improve — but the learner's relationship to the language: from the language as obstacle, through language as tool, to language as medium, and finally to language as home.
sentences.native: Lo que cambia más profundamente a través de los niveles no es el tamaño del vocabulario ni la precisión gramatical, aunque ambos mejoran, sino la relación del aprendiz con el idioma: desde el idioma como obstáculo, a través del idioma como herramienta, hasta el idioma como medio, y finalmente hasta el idioma como hogar.
sentences.en: What changes most profoundly across the levels is not vocabulary size or grammar accuracy — though both improve — but the learner's relationship to the language: from the language as obstacle, through language as tool, to language as medium, and finally to language as home.
sentences.es: Lo que cambia más profundamente a través de los niveles no es el tamaño del vocabulario ni la precisión gramatical, aunque ambos mejoran, sino la relación del aprendiz con el idioma: desde el idioma como obstáculo, a través del idioma como herramienta, hasta el idioma como medio, y finalmente hasta el idioma como hogar.

sentences.target: The milestones of language learning are memorable precisely because they mark transitions in relationship: the first conversation that was enjoyable rather than effortful; the first film understood without subtitles; the first joke that worked; the first time a thought arose in the second language without passing through the first.
sentences.native: Los hitos del aprendizaje de idiomas son memorables precisamente porque marcan transiciones en la relación: la primera conversación que fue agradable en lugar de esforzada; la primera película entendida sin subtítulos; el primer chiste que funcionó; la primera vez que surgió un pensamiento en la segunda lengua sin pasar por la primera.
sentences.en: The milestones of language learning are memorable precisely because they mark transitions in relationship: the first conversation that was enjoyable rather than effortful; the first film understood without subtitles; the first joke that worked; the first time a thought arose in the second language without passing through the first.
sentences.es: Los hitos del aprendizaje de idiomas son memorables precisamente porque marcan transiciones en la relación: la primera conversación que fue agradable en lugar de esforzada; la primera película entendida sin subtítulos; el primer chiste que funcionó; la primera vez que surgió un pensamiento en la segunda lengua sin pasar por la primera.

sentences.target: The C2 speaker has not become a native speaker: they have become something more interesting — a bicultural, bilingual mind that can inhabit two linguistic worlds simultaneously, perceiving things in the second language that native speakers take for granted and bringing to that language a perspective that native speakers can never have.
sentences.native: El hablante de C2 no se ha convertido en un hablante nativo: se ha convertido en algo más interesante, una mente bicultural y bilingüe que puede habitar dos mundos lingüísticos simultáneamente, percibiendo cosas en el segundo idioma que los hablantes nativos dan por sentadas y aportando a ese idioma una perspectiva que los hablantes nativos nunca pueden tener.
sentences.en: The C2 speaker has not become a native speaker: they have become something more interesting — a bicultural, bilingual mind that can inhabit two linguistic worlds simultaneously, perceiving things in the second language that native speakers take for granted and bringing to that language a perspective that native speakers can never have.
sentences.es: El hablante de C2 no se ha convertido en un hablante nativo: se ha convertido en algo más interesante, una mente bicultural y bilingüe que puede habitar dos mundos lingüísticos simultáneamente, percibiendo cosas en el segundo idioma que los hablantes nativos dan por sentadas y aportando a ese idioma una perspectiva que los hablantes nativos nunca pueden tener.

sentences.target: Every language learned is a new way of seeing — a new set of categories, distinctions, and collocations that carve the world at different joints and make available a range of perceptions and expressions that exist nowhere else; which is why the language journey, however long and however difficult, is always worth continuing.
sentences.native: Cada idioma aprendido es una nueva forma de ver, un nuevo conjunto de categorías, distinciones y colocaciones que dividen el mundo en articulaciones diferentes y hacen disponibles una gama de percepciones y expresiones que no existen en ningún otro lugar; razón por la cual el viaje del idioma, por largo y difícil que sea, siempre vale la pena continuar.

questions.q: What does the speaker say changes most profoundly across the CEFR levels?
options: Vocabulary size and grammar accuracy, which improve continuously from A1 through to C2
The learner's relationship to the language — from obstacle, through tool, to medium, to home
The complexity of communicative tasks the learner can successfully complete in authentic contexts
The speed and fluency with which the learner can produce language under time pressure in real situations
questions.answer: The learner's relationship to the language — from obstacle, through tool, to medium, to home

questions.q: How does the speaker characterise what the C2 speaker has become compared to a native speaker?
options: A speaker who has achieved a level of competence that is practically indistinguishable from native speaker performance
Something more interesting — a bicultural bilingual mind inhabiting two linguistic worlds with unique perspective
A speaker who has transcended the limitations of their first language by achieving mastery of the second
An expert communicator who can outperform native speakers in formal and professional communicative contexts
questions.answer: Something more interesting — a bicultural bilingual mind inhabiting two linguistic worlds with unique perspective

questions.q: What does the speaker say makes the language journey always worth continuing?
options: The economic and professional advantages that higher language proficiency provides in the global job market
Every language is a new way of seeing — new categories that carve the world differently and make unique perceptions available
The social connections and cultural experiences that language learning makes accessible at each new level
The cognitive benefits of language learning that accumulate across a lifetime of study and practice
questions.answer: Every language is a new way of seeing — new categories that carve the world differently and make unique perceptions available
